details.body: And, conj. ca repeated after each word joined, or after all. In the case of nouns, ex. by Dvandva comps.; ‘the Sun and the Moon’ AdityacaMdrO. 2 (With adjectives) gen. ex. by Karm. comps.; alasalulitamugDAni aMgakAni; (with numerals) by a comp. with aDika, uttara; ‘100 a(nd) 8’ azwADikaM-azwottaraM SataM. 3 (In the case of verbs) ex. by the use of gerunds; ‘go a(nd) tell him’ gatvA tasmE kaTaya; sometimes by vA in questions; jAta asti te mAtA smarasi vA tAtaM (U. 4). 4 api ca, anyacca, kiM ca. ‘A(nd) then’ aTa, tadanu, tataH; ‘a(nd) yet’, taTApi, or ex. by ca-ca; asulaBA sakaleMdumuKI ca sA kimapi cedamanaMgavicezwitaM (V. 2).

AND: I In case of subs. and adj. s: (a) by dva. comp.: summer a. spring grIzmavasantO; father a. mother mAtApitarO; or, sim. pitarO [so brother a. sister BrArarO; son a. daughter putrO; father-in- law a. mother-in-law SvaSurO]; with his superior birth, asceticism, erudition, valour a. deeds amijana- tapovidyAkriyAtiSayErnijEH, Vi. ii.; exhausted, tremu- [Page027] -lous, and (therefore) pleasant alasalalitamugDAni, U. i.;(6) by ca (enclitic): fresh youth, in- comparable beauty, a. superhuman prowess aBinava- yOvanatvamapratimarUpatvamamAnuzaSaktitvaM ca, K.II. In case of numerals:(1) By a comp. with aDikaH (kA, kaM), or uttaraH (rA, raM): one hundred a. two dvaDikaM SataM or sim., dvavADikaSataM: three thousand a. sixty-eight azwazazwayu ttaratrisahasraM;(2) By a comp. with sa-,: after a reign of 18 years a. thirteen days so'zwAdaSAbdAn kzamAM BuktvA satrayodaSa- vAsarAn, Raj.;(3) by ca (very rare), Vi.III In case of verbs, generally by participles: go a. speak this to the minister gatvEvamamAtyaM brU hi, Sa. vi.; then he alighted (from the horse) a. tied it up to a. branch of a tree, a. then approached a. saluted Śiva a. then again gazed on the same lady tato'vatIrya taruSAKAyAM badDvA turagamupasftya praRamya trilocanAya tAmeva yozitaM cakzuzA punarnirUpayAmAsa, K. v. (iv).IV In connecting sentences:(1) By ca (never at the beginning): (these remem- brances) burn my body a. rend my heart dehaM dahanti hfdayaM ca vidArayanti; Ma. x.;(2) Some- -times ca is omitedomitted: behave so that you will not be laughed at by men, will not be censured by the good, will not be reviled by the seniors taTA prayateTAH yaTA nopahasyase janEH, na nindAse sADuBiH, na Dikkriyase gurUBiH, K.V. In Interrogation, generally by vA (enclitic): who is he, whose son, a. what is his name ? ko'sO, kasya vApatyaM kimaBiDAno vA? K. ; O. fair lady, who are you, whose spouse, a. what is your object for coming to me ? kA tvaM SuBe kasya parigraho vA kiM vA madaByAgamanakAraRaM te, R. xiv. 8.

AND , conj. ca placed after the word which it connects with another. In many cases ‘and’ may be omitted in San- skrit, and the connection expressed by the use of the indeclinable participle; as, ‘the beasts assembled and informed the lion,’ paSuBirmilitvA siMho vijYaptaH. — (Moreover) apica, kiYca, aparaM, anyacca. — (And then) aTa.

AND THEN: denoting immediate sequence: (1) tadanu in childhood a. then again in youth SESave tadanu, yOvane punaH U. i.;(2) tataH, a. then allowed his son to go tato'nujYe gamanaM sutasya B. i. 23.;(3) tadanu ca (very rare), Vi. ii. v. and (III).
AND YET: taTApi: v. YET.
ANDANTE , s. GanaM, tattvaM, vilambitaM, spazwaM.
ANDIRON , s. lohanirmmitaH SUlADAraH.
ANDROGYNAL or ANDROGYNOUS, a. dviliNgaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
Androgynous, a. dviliMgaviSizwa.
Aneal, v. t. tElena aByaMj 7 P.
Anear, adv. prAyaH. 2 prep. saMniDO, sakASaM. 3 v. t. aBigam 1 P, aByupa-i 2 P.
Anecdote, s. kaTA, upAKyAnaM, AKyAyikA.
ANECDOTE: (1) kaTA;(2) upAKyAnam: v. Story
ANECDOTE , s. upakaTA, upAKyAnaM.
Anemograph, s. vAyuvegadigdarSakaM yaMtraM.
Anemometer, s. vAyuvegamApakaM yaMtraM.
Anent, prep. uddiSya, aDikftya, vizaye in comp.
ANENT , prep. (Concerning) prati, uddiSya ind., pratIkzya ind., vizayakaH -kA -kaM.
ANEURISM: Perh. nAqIbraRam.
ANEURISM , s. nAqisPAtiH f., nAqInAM raktapravAhakARAm atiSayasPAtiH.
Anew, adv. punaH, punarapi. 2 aBinavaM.
ANEW: (1) punar;(2) punarapi: v. Again.
ANEW , adv. (Over again) punar, punaHpunar, punarapi. — (Newly) nUtanaM, pratinavaM.
Angel, s. devadUtaH, ISvaraprezyaH, svargadUtaH, ‘you are my a(ngel)’ tvaM me priyatamA, prARapreyasI. [Angel]ic, [Angel]ical, a. divya, devadUtopama, amAnuza, (zI f.).
ANGEL: I Lit.: devadUtaH; ganDarvaH.II Fig: as a term of endearment:(1) priyatamA;(2) preyasIH v. Love, darling.
ANGEL, ANGELIC (adj.): I Belonging to angels: by tat. comp.II Resembling angels:(1) divyaH (vyA, vyaM);(2) amAnuzaH (zI, saM).
ANGEL , s. ISvaradUtaH, devadUtaH, ISvaraprepyaH, svargI m. (n), parameSvarapreritaH, svargIyadUtaH, svargadUtaH, divyatUtaH.
ANGELICAL , ANGELIC, a. ISvaradUtopamaH -mA -maM, divyaH -vyA -vyaM, devarUpI -piRI -pi (n), svargIyaH -yA -yaM.
ANGELICALLY , adv. ISvaradUtavat, svargIyajanavat, divyaprakAreRa.

Anger, s. kroDaH, kopaH, amarzaH, rozaH, manyuH. v. t. prakup c., kruD c. Angry, a. jAtAmarza, ruzwa, sAmarza, saroza, kopin, kupita, krudDa, samanyu; ‘to be a(ngry)’ kup-kruD-ruz- 4 P, (with dat.). Angrily, adv. sakopaM, sarozaM, kopAt &c.

ANGER (subs): (1) kroDaH;(2) kopaH, to give way to a. kopavaSaM gacCati, V. iv.; restraining his a. kopaM nigfhgan, B. xii. 81.;(3) rozaH; (4) amarzaH, void of a. amarzaSUnyaH (nyA, nyaM), Ki. i. 33.;(5) manyuH deeprooteddeep-rooted a. possessed (him) manyuraBajadavagAdataraH, Si. xv. 2.;(6) saMramBaH;(7) rUz, (f.);(8) kruD (f.);(9) rUzA.
ANGER (v. t.): (1) kopayati (c. of kup);(2) kroDaM, manyu karoti (with gen.)
ANGER , s. kroDaH, kopaH, amarzaH, rozaH, cetovikAraH; ‘my anger is appeased,’ mama kroDaH SAmyati; ‘through anger,’ kopAt. — (Smart of a sore) vraRavedanA.
To ANGER , v. a. kup in caus. (kopayati -yituM), prakup, saNkup; kruD in caus. (kroDayati -yituM).
Angle, s. asraH, koRaH. v. i. baqiSena matsyAn grah 9 P, udDf-hf 1 P. [Angl]er, s. matsyaveDakaH. [Angl]ing, s. matsyagrahaRaM. Angular, a. koRaviSizwa, asropeta.
ANGLE (subs): (I) koRaH; (2) asnaH. Right a. samakoRaH; obtuse a. *vizamakoRaH; acute a. samona- koRaH, sUkzmakoRaH; alternate a. viparyastakoRaH.
ANGLE (v).: (1) Perh. vaqiSayati (nomi.);(2) vaqiSena matsyAn viDyati (vyaD, c. 4.), or gfhvAti (grah, c. 9.).
ANGLE , s. asraH, koRaH, dviBujaH. — (Apparatus to take fish) matsya- veDanopakaraRaM.
To ANGLE , v. a. vaqiSena matsyAn jalAd udDf (c. 1. -harati -te -harttuM), vaqiSa (nom. vaqiSayati), matsyaveDanena mInAn vyaD (c. 4. viDyati vyadDuM) or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti grahItuM).
ANGLE , s. (Obtuse) aDikakoRaH, viSAlakoRaH, see OBTUSE, &c.
ANGLE-ROD or ANGLING-ROD, s. matsyagrahaRArTaM daRqaM.
ANGLER: I One who angles matsyaveDakaH v. fish- -erman.II A species of fish: matsyaviSezaH.
ANGLER , s. matsyaveDakaH, matsyabanDI m. (n), yo vaqiSena matsyAn gfhlAti.
ANGLICISM: *iMrejaBAzArItiH.
ANGLICIZE (v. t.): *iMrejayati (nomi.).
ANGLING (subs).: vaqiSena matsyabanDanam, or matsya- DAraRam.
ANGLING , s. vaqiSena matsyaveDanaM, matsyabanDanaM.
ANGLING-LINE , s. matsyagrahaRArTaM sUtraM or rajjuH m.
ANGLING-ROD: Perh. vaqiSadaRqam.
ANGRILY: (1) sakopam;(2) sakroDam;(3) sarozam; (4) sAmarzam.
ANGRILY , adv. sakopaM, sarozaM, sAmarzaM, kopeRa, kroDAt.
ANGRILY , adv. for kopeRa, read kopena.
ANGRY: (1) krudDaH (dDA, dDaM);(2) kupitaH (tA, taM): v. Enraged.

ANGRY, BE OR GET: (1) kruDyati (kruD, c. 4.); (2) kuzyati (kup, c. 4.);(3) rUzyati (rUz, c. 4.) N. B. These verbs are const. with dat. or with prati and acc.: a. with the king of Chedi krudDasya cEdyaM prati Si. i. 75.

ANGRY , a. krudDaH -dDA -dDaM, kroDI -DinI -Di (n), kopI -pinI -pi (n), jAtAmarzaH -rzA -rzaM, ruzwaH -zwA -zwaM, kroDAkrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, sAmarzaH -rzA -rzaM, kftakopaH -pA -paM, kftakruDaH -DA -DaM, AgatamanyuH -nyuH -nyu, sarozaH -zA -zaM, rozaRaH -RA -RaM, sakopaH -pA -paM, samanyuH -nyuH -nyu. — (To be angry) kruD (c. 4. kruDyati krodDuM), anukruD, samaBikruD, saMkruD, aBisaMkruD; ruz (c. 4. ruzyati rozituM), kup (c. 4. kupyati kopituM), prakup, saNkup with dative; asUy (asUyati -te, asUyituM) with acc.
Anguish, s. paritApaH, pIqA, bADA, vedanA, yAtanA, AtaMkaH; ‘a(nguish) of mind’ manastApaH.
ANGUISH: (1) manastApaH (a. of mind);(2) yAtanA ( =bodily pain): v. Agony.
ANGUISH , s. paritApaH, vedanA, tIvravedanA, kleSaH, pIqA, duHKaM, ADiH m., manastApaH, parivedanaM, vibADA, kfcCaM, kazwaM, todaH.
ANGULAR: (1) koRaviSizwaH (zwA, zwaM) (?);(2) sAsnaH (snA, snaM) (?).
ANGULAR or ANGULOUS, a. sAsraH -srA -sraM, koRaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, asravAn -vatI -vat (t), asropetaH -tA -taM.
Anhelation, s. ucCvasanaM, hfdayakaMpaH, vepaTuH.
ANHELATION , s. ucCvasanaM, niHSvasanaM. — (Palpitation) hfdayakampanaM.
ANIMADVERSION: upAlamBaH: v. Reproof, cen- -sure.
ANIMADVERSION , s. (Reproof) anuyogaH, nindA, upAlamBaH, GfRA. — [Page018-a+ 51] — (Infliction of punishment) daRqayogaH. — (Observation) carcA, nirIkzaRaM, anvezaRaM.
Animadvert, v. i. niMd 1 P, upAlaB 1 A; See Censure. 2 parIkz 1 A, carcAM kf. Animadversion, s. niMdA, upAlaMBaH. 2 parIkzaRaM, carcA.

To ANIMADVERT , v. n. (To pass censure on) pratinind (c. 1. -nindati -nindituM), upAlaB (c. 1. -laBate -labDuM). — (To punish) daRqaM praRI (c. 1. -nayati -netuM), daRq (c. 10. daRqayati -yituM). — (To make observation) nirIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -IkzituM), carcAM kf.
ANIMADVERTED , p. p. pratininditaH -tA -taM. — (Punished) daRqitaH -tA -taM.
ANIMADVERTER , s. pratinindakaH, daRqapraRetA m. (tf), anuyogI m. (n).

Animal, s. jaMtuH, prARin m., jIvin m., jIvaH, janmavat m. 2 paSuH, mfgaH, tiryac m. a. prARisaMbaMDin &c. 2 cetana; ‘a(nimal) food’ mAMsAhAraH; ‘a(nimal) pleasures’ vizayAH, vizayasuKAni; ‘a(nimal) passions’ (carnal) zaq-ripavaH-iMdriyARi; ‘a(nimal) kingdom’ prARivargaH. [Animal]cule, s. kzudrajaMtuH.

ANIMAL: I Any living creature:(1) prARin (m);(2) jIvaH;(3) cetanaH. (=a rational a.) ;(4) jantuH (usually applied to lower a. s only);(5) janmin (m);(6) janmavat (m.)II. A beast: q. v.:(1) BfgaH;(2) paSuH.

ANIMAL (adj.): Expr. by gen. of above: Ph. a. food Amizam: v. Or meat; a. pleasures vizayAH or vizayasuKAni (pl.): a. passions indriyARi (n. pl.) (lit. organs of sense), or, kAmAdayaH zaqripavaH; the a. kingdom *jIvasfzwiH, niKilaprARivargaH
ANIMAL , s. jantuH m., prARI m. (n), cetanaH, jIvI m. (n), jantuH m., janmI m. (n), SarIrI m. (n). — (Beast) paSuH m., tiryyaN m. (-Yc).
ANIMAL , a. jIvI -vinI -vi (n), prARI -RinI -Ri (n), cetanaH -nA -naM, cetanAvAn -vatI -vat (t). — (Animal food) mAMsAhAraH.

ANIMAL , s. sattvaM. Animals are divided by the Hindūs into four classes, viz. 1. ‘Egg-born,’ aRqajAH m. pl.; 2. ‘Womb- born,’ jarAyujAH m. pl.; 3. ‘Generated by heat and damp,’ svedajAH m. pl.; 4. ‘Vegetable-born,’ udBijjAH m. pl.
ANIMALCULE (subs): (1) sUkzmajIvaH;(2) ati- kzudrajantuH.
ANIMALCULE , s. kzudrajIvI m. (n), kzudrajantuH m.

Animate, v. t. jIv c., samA-A-Svas c., prAR c. 2 protsah c., jIvaM saMcar c., uttij c., udyuj 10, parARud c. [Animat]ed, a. sajIva, cetana, cara, prARin. 2 protsAhita, ASvAsita. 3 praPulla, protsAhanAprerita, sAravat; ‘a(nimated) by passion’ madollAsita, samada. [Animat]ion, s. jIvasaMcAraRaM, jIvapradAnaM. 2 protsAhanaM, praPullatA, ullAsaH. [Animat]or, s. prARadaH, protsAhakaH &c.
ANIMATE: (v. t.): I To give life to:(1) jIvayati (c. of jIv);(2) jIvaM saYcArayati (c. of car), P.II. FIG.: To encourage, incite q. v.: (1) ASvAsayati (c. of Svas);(2) protsAhayati (c. of sah).
ANIMATE, ANIMATED (adj.): I Alive: sajIvaH (vA, vaM): Ph. a. being(1) jIvaH;(2) prARI. II Lively, vigorous: q. v.:(1) praPullaH (llA, llaM);(2) ullasaH (sA, saM).

To ANIMATE , v. a. jIv in caus. (jIvayati -yituM), prAR in caus. (-Anayati -yituM), ASvas in caus. (-SvAsayati -yituM), samASvas, viSvas, pariviSvas in caus.; utTA in caus. (utTApayati -yituM), udyuj in caus. (-yojayati -yituM), protsah in caus. (-sAhayati -yituM), uttij (c. 10. -tejayati -yituM).

ANIMATE , ANIMATED, part. a. (Inspirited) ASvAsitaH -tA -taM, udyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, uttejitaH -tA -ta. — (Living) cetanaH -nA -naM, prARI -RinI -Ri (n). — (Vivacious) praPullavadanaH -nA -naM, hfzwahfdayaH -yA -yaM, rasikaH -kA -kaM, sAravAn -vatI -vat (t).
ANIMATE , a. sajIvaH -vA -vaM, saprARaH -RA -RaM, sacezwaH -zwA -zwaM; ‘animate and inanimate,’ cetanAcetanaH -nA -naM, carAcaraH -rA -raM.
ANIMATION: I Bestowal of life:(1) jIvana- dAnam;(2) jIvasaYcAraH.II life: q. v.: jIvanam. III liveliness, vivacity: q. v.(1) praPullatA; (2) ullAsaH.
ANIMATION , s. (The act of enlivening) ASvAsanaM, uttejanaM. — (The state of being enlivened, vivacity) praPullatA, hfzwatA.
ANIMATOR , s. ASvAsakaH, jIvadaH, prARadaH, protsAhakaH.
Animosity, s. dvezaH, vEraM, viroDaH, mAtsaryaM.
ANIMOSITY: (1) dvezaH;(2) vidvezaH;(3) vEram; (4) viroDaH.
ANIMOSITY , s. vEraM, dvezaM, viroDaH, mAtsaryyaM.
Animus, s. codanA, uddeSaH.
Anise, s. CatrA, sAleyaH.
ANISE: (1) atiCatrA,(2) CatrA.
ANISE , s. CatrA, sAleyaH, SItaSivaH, maDurikA, miSI, miSreyA.
ANKER , s. rasAnAM parimARaviSezaH.
Ankle, s. gulPaH, GuwikA.
ANKLE: (1) gulPa (mn.);(2) GuwikA;(3) GuwiH.
ANKLE , s. gulPaH -lPaM, GuwikA or GawikA, GuwiH f., caraRagranTiH f.
ANKLED , a. gulPayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, gulPasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
Anklet, s. nUpuraH-raM, maMjIraM.
ANKLET: (1) nUpuram;(2) pAdANgadam;(3) tulA- kowiH;(4) maYjIram.
ANKLET , s. nUpuraH, pAdANgadaM, maYjIraM, pAdakawakaH.
ANNALIST: (1) AKyAnavid; Vi. (?);(2) AKyAnaracakaH (?).
ANNALIST , s. kramAnusAreRa caritraracakaH, caritraleKakaH, purAvfttaracakaH, AKyAnaracakaH, vfttAntaleKakaH, AKyAnasaNgrAhakaH.
To ANNALIZE , v. a. caritrARi or purAvfttakaTA rac (c. 10. racayati -yituM).
Annals, s. vArzikavfttAMtaH, vArzikavfttetihAsaH. 2 purAvfttakaTA, caritrAKyAnaM. Annalist, s. caritraleKakaH.
ANNALS: (1) AKyAnacayaH (?);(2) itihAsaH (?);(3) *vArzikavfttAni.
ANNALS , s. kramAnusAreRa saNgfhIta itihAsaH, purAvfttaM, purAvfttakaTA, cari- trAKyAnaM, vfttAntavivaraRaM.
ANNATES , s. praTamaPalaM, navaSasyaM. — (Sacrifice of first-fruits) agrAyaRaM.
ANNATS: (1) praTamavarzaPalAni (n. pl.) (?).
ANNEAL: (1) *pratapati (tap, c. 1.)
To ANNEAL , v. n. raNgasTirIkaraRanimitte kAcaM tap (c. 1. tapati taptuM or caus. tApayati -yituM).
ANNEALING , s. yat kAcasya tapanaM raNgasTirIkaraRAya kriyate.

Annex, v. t. saMyuj 10, anubaMD 9 P, upADA 3 U; ‘Oudh was a(nnex)ed to the British territory’ avaDadeSa AMglarAjyAMgaM kftaH, -rAjyena saMyojitaH. 2 aMte nirdiS 6 P; ‘a list of names is a(nnex)ed’ nAmAvalI leKAMte dattA, nAmAni leKAMte nirdizwAni. [Annex]ation, s. saMyojanaM, anubaMDanaM; ‘a thing annexed’ anubaMDaH. [Annex]ed, a. saMyojita, upAhita.
ANNEX: I To subjoin: Ph. I. a. a list of articles for sale *leKAnte vikreyadravyARi nirdizwAni. II To unite: saM-yojayati (c. of yuj).
To ANNEX , v. a. anubanD (c. 9. -baDnAti -bandDuM), AbanD; saMyuj in caus. (-yojayati -yituM), upADA (c. 3. -daDAti -Datte -DAtuM), ADA; upasTA in caus. (-sTApayati -yituM).
ANNEXATION: (1) saMyojanam;(2) saMyogaH: v. Union.
ANNEXATION , s. anubanDanaM, upasTApanaM, saMyogaH, saMyojanaM, upaDAnaM.
ANNEXED , p. p. saMyojitaH -tA -taM, upAhitaH -tA -taM, anuvadDaH -dDA -dDaM.
ANNEXMENT , s. (The act of annexing). See the last. — (The thing annexed) anubanDaH, upAhitaM, saMyuktaBAgaH.
Annihilate, v. t. ut-samut-Cid 7 P, unmUl 10, ava-ut-sad c., naS c., vilup c. [Annihilat]ion, s. ucCedaH, kzayaH, avasAdanaM, vilopaH, vinASaH; pralayaH (of the world).
ANNIHILATE: (1) ut-Cinatti, samut- (Cid, c. 7.); (2) unmUlayati (mUl, c. 10):(3) ut-sAdayati (c. of sad);(4) pra-lAyayati (c. of lI);(5) vilopayati (c. of lup): v. To destroy.
To ANNIHILATE , v. a. naS in caus. (nASayati -yituM), vinaS; pralI in caus. (-lApayati or -lAyayati -yituM), udDf (c. 1. -harati -te -harttuM), ucCid (c. 7. -Cinatti -CettuM), lopaM kf.
ANNIHILATED , p. p. ucCinnaH -nnA -nnaM, vinASitaH -tA -taM.
ANNIHILATION: (1) ucCedaH, samucCedaH;(2) lopaH, vilopaH;(3) kzayaH;(4) pralayaH (rare, except with reference to the a. of the world): v. Destruction.
ANNIHILATION , s. nASaH, kzayaH, pralayaH, vinASaH, aBAvaH, samucCedaH, lopaH, nirBAvaH, pralInatA.

details.body: Anniversary, a. sAMvatsarika-vArzika (kI f.). s. sAMvatsariko viDiH; ‘a(nniversary) of birth’ janmadivasaH; ‘a(nniversary) of death’ mftatiTiH.
ANNIVERSARY: (1) vArzikaH (kI, kaM);(2) sAMvat- sarikaH (kI, kaM). The a. of Kṛṣṇa's birth janmAzwamI; the a. of Rāma's birth rAmanavamI.

Anticipate, v. t. pUrvaM prAgeva-jYA 9 U or ni-rUp 10 or grah 9 P. 2 agrataH anuBU 1 P or Buj 7 A, pUrvAsvAdanaM kf. [Anticipat]ion, s. pUrvameva jYAnaM, pUrvaBukti f., pUrvAsvAdanaM.

ANTICIPATE (v. t.): I To foresee: Ph. old men can a. what is coming vfdDabudDiranAgataM paSyati Vi.; even a. ing his death tasya BAvimaraRaM jAnannapi. II To be before in doing: Ph. I a. d his designs by removing to London *tasyASayaM nirUpya laRqanamahaM jagAma; Scipio a. d Hannibal in cross- ing the Po. *henibAlasyABiprAyaM jYAtvA sipiyaH prAgeva ponadImuttatAra.

To ANTICIPATE , v. a. (Before the time) pUrvvatas grah (c. 9. gfhlAti grahItuM), pravekz (c. 1. -Ikzate -IkzituM). — (To foretaste) pUrvvasvAdanaM kf, agratas anuBU (c. 1. -Bavati -BavituM), pUrvvaM jYA (c. 9. jAnAti jYAtuM) or Buj (c. 7. Bunakti, BuMkte, BoktuM), uddfS (c. 1. utpaSyati uddrazwuM), pradfS.
To ANTICIPATE , v. a. niyamitakAlAt pUrvvaM grah, pUrvvaBogaM kf.
ANTICIPATED , p. p. pUrvvaBuktaH -ktA -ktaM, pUrvvatas anuBUtaH -tA -taM, pradfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, pravekzitaH -tA -taM, sandfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, cittakalitaH -tA -taM, puraskftaH -tA -taM.
ANTICIPATION , s. pUrvvaBuktiH f., pUrvvaBojanaM, pUrvvajYAnaM, pravekzaRaM.
ANTICLIMAX , s. sArAlaNkAravipakzaH, sArAlaNkArapratilomaH.
ANTIDOTAL , a. vizanASI -SinI -Si (n), vizaGAtI -tinI -ti (n), vizaGnaH -GnI -GnaM, garaGnaH -GnI -GnaM.
Antidote, s. vizaGno'gadaH, prativizaM; ‘a(ntidote) against anxiety’ ciMtAvizaGno'gadaH, ‘dealer in a(ntidote)s’ vizavEdyaH, jAMgulikaH. 2 pratikAraH. [Antidot]al, a. vizaGna (GnI f.).
ANTIDOTE: I Any remedy: q. v.: pratikAraH. II For poison: vizaGnOzaDam etc. A dealer in a. s:(1) vizavEdyaH;(2) jANgalikaH,(3) narendraH. III For fever: jvaraGnOzaDam.
ANTIDOTE , s. vizanASanaM, prativizaM. — (Dealer in) vizavEdyaH, jANgulikaH.
ANTIFEBRILE , a. jvaraGnaH -GnI -GnaM, jvaranASakaH -kA -kaM, jvarAntakaH -kA -kaM.
Antimony, s. srotoMjanaM, yAmunaM, sOvIraM.
ANTIMONY: (1) srotoYjanam;(2) kApotam;(3) sOviram;(4) yAmunam. These words properly mean sulphuret of a.
ANTIMONY , s. srotoYjanaM, sOvIraM, kApotAYjanaM, yAmunaM. — (Made of anti- mony) srotoYjanamayaH -yI -yaM.
Antipathy, s. viroDaH, vEraM, dvaMdvaBAvaH, vidvezaH; ‘natural a(ntipathy)’ SASvatiko viroDaH.
ANTIPATHY: vidvezaH: Hatred, aversion.
ANTIPATHY , s. sahajo viroDaH, dvandvaBAvaH, viraktiH f., vEritA, SatrutA, vimatiH f., anicCA.
ANTIPHLEGMATIC , a. kaPanASanaH -nI -naM, kaPaGnaH -GnI -GnaM, SlezmaGnaH -GnI -GnaM.
Antiphony, s. pratiDvaniH, pratigAnaM.
ANTIPHONY , s. pratigAnaM, parasparagItiH f., pratiDvaniH f.
ANTIPHRASIS: Nearest word nihatArTatvam, Sah. vii.; *viparItArTatvam.
Antipodes, s. pratilomaM; ‘living in a(ntipodes)’ pratilomAH.

ANTIPODES: I The opposite part of the globe: *pratilomam; BUgolasyADoBAgam.II Those who inhabit it: *pratiloBA. Ph. the a. and those who live in other parts of the globe, live just as com- fortably as we do here anAkulAstiryagaDaH sTitASca tizWanti te tatra vayaM yaTAtra, S. s.
ANTIPODES , s. BUmaRqalasya viparItaBAge varttinaH; anyatarasmin BUgolaBAge varttinaH parasparAm aBimuKapAdatalA janAH.
ANTIPODES , s. anupAtaH, parasparasammuKapAdajanAH m. pl.
Antipyrin(e), s. jvaraGnaM OzaDaM.
ANTIQUARIAN (adj.): Ph. a. knowledge prAkkAlI- navizayavijYAnam.
ANTIQUARIAN, ANTIQUARY (subs): *prAkkAlIna- vizayezu paRqitaH, aBijYaH, etc. (?).
ANTIQUARIAN , a. prAkkAlInaH -nA -naM, pUrvvakAlInaH -nA -naM, prAktanaH -nI -naM.
Antiquary, [Antiqua]rian, s. prAkkAlInavizayakovidaH-paMqitaH. a. prAkkAlIna, prAktana (nI f.)
ANTIQUARY , ANTIQUARIAN, s. prAkkAlInavizayezu paRqitaH, purAtanadra- vyAnusanDAyI m. (n).
ANTIQUARY , s. prAkkAlikadravyasaMgrahI m., prAkkAlikadravyAnvezI m.

Antiquated, Antique, a. prAcIna, purAtana-prAktana (nI f.), purARa; (style) apracalita, luptaprayoga (BAzAsaraRiH). Antiquity, s. Ancients, q. v. 2 prAkkAlaH, pUrvakAlaH. 3 purAtanatvaM, prAkkAlInatvaM.
ANTIQUATED (adj.): apracalitaH (tA, taM): v. Obsolete, oldfashionedold-fashioned.
ANTIQUATED , a. gatakAlikaH -kI -kaM, prAkkAlikaH &c. See OBSOLETE.
ANTIQUE (adj.): prAcInaH (nA, naM): v. Ancient, old.
ANTIQUE (subs): (1) prAcInadravyam (?);(2) purARa- dravyam (?).
ANTIQUE , a. (Ancient) purARaH -RA or -RI -RaM, purAtanaH -nI -naM, prAktanaH -nI -naM, pUrvvakAlInaH -nA -naM, cirantanaH -nI -naM. — (Old- fashioned) apracalaH -lA -laM, aparUpaH -pA -paM.
ANTIQUE , s. prAcInadravyaM, prAkkAlInavizayaH.

ANTIQUITY: I The ancients:(1) vfdDAH (m. pl.);(2) pUrve (m. pl.);(3) cirantanAH (m. pl.); (4) prAcInAH or prAcInalokAH (m. pl.) etc.II The ancient time:(1) prAkkAlaH;(2) pUrva- kAlaH.III Ancientness:(1) prAcInatvam; (2) purARatvam;(3) purAtanatvam.IV The remains of a.:(1) prAcInadravyam (=an old thing);(2) prAkkAlInavizayaH ( = antiquarian subject).
ANTIQUITY , s. (Old-times) prAkkAlaM, pUrvvakAlaM, gatakAlaM. — (The an- cients) prAcInapuruzAH m. pl. — (Ancientness) purAtanatvaM, prAcInatvaM.
Antiseptic, a. pUtinASaka.
ANTISEPTIC , a. pUtiGnaH -GnI -GnaM, pUtinivArakaH -kA -kaM, pUtinASakaH -kA -kaM.
ANTISTES , s. praDAnapurohitaH, DarmmADyakzaH.
Antithesis, s. pratipakzatA, viroDaH, arTavEparItyaM.
ANTITHESIS: nearest word viroDaH, Sah. x.
ANTITHESIS , s. arTAntaranyAsaH, arTavEparItyaM, vikalpaH, pratipakzatA, viroDaH.
Antitype, s. mUlamUrti f., AdarSaH.
ANTITYPE: AdarSaH.
ANTITYPE , s. pratimUrttyA pradarSitA mUrttiH f., mUlamUrttiH f., vastu n., AdarSaH.
ANTITYPE , s. prativimbamUlaM, pratimUrttimUlaM, darSyavizayaH.
Antler, s. hariRaSfMgaM, mfgavizARaM. [Antler]ed, a. SfMgavat, vizARin.
ANTLER: hariRaSfNgam (or simp. SfNgam when the meaning is clear).
ANTLER , s. mfgaSfNgaM, mfgaSfNgaSAKA, mfgavizARaM.
ANTLERED: SfNgin (f. RI): v. Horned.
ANTLERED , a. SfNgI -NginI -Ngi (n), vizARI -RinI -Ri (n).
ANTONOMASIA: lakzaRA.
Anus, s. gudaM, apAnaM, pAyuH.
ANUS: (1) gudam;(2) guhyam;(3) pAyuH;(4) apAnam.
ANUS , gudaM, pAyuH m., mEtraH, apAnaM.
Anvil, s. SUrmaH-rmI, sTURA.
ANVIL: (1) SUrmiH (m.);(2) sUrmI (f.).
ANVIL , s. sUrmI f., SUrmmiH m., sTURA, lohapratimA.

Anxiety, s. ciMtA, utkaMWA, OtsukyaM, vyagratA, manastApaH, cittodvegaH; AkulatvaM, utkalikA, raRaraRakaH. Anxious, a. vyAkulita, udvigna, utkaMWita, ciMtApara, vyagra. 2 utsuka, Ipsu, sakAma; ‘he thus passes a(nxious) nights’ evamudvignasya yAMti rajanyaH; ‘to be a(nxious) (for)’ utkaMW 1 A, utsukAyate (D.), uttam 4 P; ‘he is a(nxious) to see you near’ utkaMWate yuzmatsannikarzasya (U. 6). 3 ciMtAprada, udvegakara (rI f.). [Anxious]ly, adv. sodvegaM, sotkaMWaM, saciMtaM.
ANXIETY: utkaRWA; (2) udvegaH (restless a.); (3) cintA: v. Care;(4) vyAkulatA: v. Agi- -tation;(5) utkalikA;(6) raRaraRakaH (rare).
ANXIETY , s. cintA, cittodvegaH, OtsukyaM, manoduHKaM, sanastApaH, cittavedanA, ADiH m., vyagratA, udvegaH -janaM, uttApaH, cintABAraH, mAnasI vyaTA.

ANXIOUS: I Beset with anxiety:(1) utkaRWitaH (tA, taM);(2) udvignaH (gnA, gnaM);(3) vyAkulaH (lA, [Page031] laM);(4) cintitaH (tA, taM);II Solicitous, cager:(1) vyagraH (grA, graM);(2) utsukaH (kA, kaM).III Causing anxiety:(1) udvegakaraH (rI, raM);(2) utkaRWApradaH (dA, daM).
ANXIOUS, TO BE: unmanAyate (nomi.), a. to see darSanAyonmanAyamAnaH, D.

ANXIOUS , a. (Solicitous) udvignaH -gnA -gnaM, udvignamanAH -nAH -naH (s), cintAparaH -rA -raM, vyagraH -grA -graM, uttaptaH -ptA -ptaM, utsukaH -kA -kaM, viDuraH -rA -raM, samanyuH -nyuH -nyu. — (Eagerly endeavouring) sayatnaH -tnA -tnaM. — (Desirous of) IpsuH -psuH -psu, icCuH -cCuH -cCu; ‘anx- ious to see,’ darSanepsuH; ‘anxious to do,’ karttukAmaH -mA -maM. — (To be anxious) utsukAy (nom. utsukAyate).
ANXIOUSLY: I With anxiety:(1) sotkaRWam; (2) sodvegam;(3) by the adj. v. Anxious (I). II Eagerly: by the adj.: v. Anxious (II)
ANXIOUSLY , adv. Otsukyena, udvegena, manoduHKena, cintayA, sodvegaM, sayatnaM.

sanskrit.slp1: syAnyasya vA nAmApi grahItuM te tanayasya
sanskrit.word: स्यान्यस्य वा नामापि ग्रहीतुं ते तनयस्य
sanskrit.iast: syānyasya vā nāmāpi grahītuṃ te tanayasya

details.body: Any, a. Ex. by cit, cana, or api with the forms of kim; ‘a(ny) man’ kopi naraH; ‘a(ny) woman’ kAcitstrI &c., ‘at a(ny) time’ kadAcit. 2 (Any whosoever) Ex. by forms of yat with the above; yaH kaScanAgacCatu ‘let a(ny) come’; ‘I may be a(ny) one’ yo vA ko vA BavAmyahaM; ‘a(ny)how’ kaTaMcit, yena kena prakAreRa, yaTA kaTaMcit; ‘a(ny) longer’ punaH, itaH-ataH-paraM, ‘a(ny)where’ kutrApi, kvacidapi; ‘a(ny)thing’ Izadapi, stokamapi.

ANY: (1) kaScit (kAcit, kiYcit), have you got a. one named Vimardaka kimasti kaScidvimardako nAmAtraBavataH; D. ii.: is there a. doubt about it kimatra kAcidBrAntiH Vi.: I could not find a. thing in the house gfhaM praviSyana kiYcinmayA samAsAdi- tam, Mr. iii.;(2) ko'pi, (kApi, kimapi), a. one else anyaH ko'pi etc.;(3) kaScana (kAcana, kiYcana) (rare). Ph. in the ab-sense of a. wit- ness sAkzyaBAve; without a. wisdom jYAnaM vinA; what power has Dhanañjaya or a. body else even to take the name of your son kA Saktirasti DanaYjaya- syAnyasya vA nAmApi grahItuM te tanayasya, Vi. ii. N. B. When a. means any one or anything whatever, it is expr.: (a) by yaH kaScit etc. a. one could be a witness in a house or in a forest antarveSmanyaraRye vA yaH kaScit sAkzyaM kuryAt, M. viii. 69.; I want to give even the gold bracelet of my hand to a. one (I meet) svahastasTamapi suvarRakaNakaRaM yasmEkasmEciddAtu- micCAmi; (b) by yaH...... saH etc., they can attack a. number of horsemen *yAvAnaSvavArAnaDigacCanti tAvAnevAmiyoktuM Sakruvanti.

ANY , a. kaScit m. kAcit f. kiYcit n., ko 'pi m. kApi f. kimapi n., kaScana m. kAcana f. kiYcana n.; ‘any thing,’ kiYcit, kimapi; ‘any where,’ kvacit, kvApi, kutracit, kutrApi; ‘any longer,’ punar; ‘any how,’ kaTaYcana, kaTaYcit, yaTAtaTA; ‘at any time,’ kadAcit, karhicit; ‘any further,’ dUrataraM; ‘any one soever,’ yaH kaScit.
ANY LONGER, ANY MORE: (1) itaH param (=from this time);(2) tataH param ( =from that time). I will not think any more of other girls na cintayemitaH paramitaranArIM, D. iii.
ANYHOW: (1) yena kena prakAreRa;(2) yaTA taTA.

ANYWHERE: (1) kutrApi, a. else anyatra kutrApi; (2) kvacidapi, N. kiii. 55. Ph. go a. you like gacCa yaTecCam, N. i. 143.; die a. you like yatra tatra vA prARatyAgaM kuru, Vi. vi.; I do not allow you to go a. ele from here ito'nyato na vo gantumanu- manye, Sa. iiii.
AORIST: no equiv.: anadyatanaBUtaH (=indefinite past).
AORIST , s. aniyamitakAlaH. APART, a. vyAptaH -ptA -ptaM.
AORTA: hfdayasya vAmakozanirgatA raktavahA bfhannAqI.
AORTA , s. hftpiRqavAmakopanirgatA raktapravAhakA vfhannAqI.
Apace, adv. satvaraM, SIGraM; See Quickly.
APACE: satvaram: v. Quickly, rapidly.
APACE , adv. satvaraM, SIGraM, kzipraM, sahasA, drutaM, savegaM.

Apart, adv. pfTak; vi-pra-gata a.; ‘having knees a(part)’ prajYuH. 2 niBftaM, rahasi, vijane, ekAMte, vivikte. 3 dUre. 4 svagataM, janAMtikaM. ‘a(part) from this consideration’, ‘this consideration a(part)’ idaM kAraRaM vihAya-tyaktvA, etadarTaBinna a.; ‘excellence of virtues a(part), a woman must have modesty at least’ guRasaMpatstriyA mA nAma Bavatu, SAlInatA punaravaSyaM syAdeva. [Apart]ment, s. kozWaH, SAlA, kakzA, AvAsaH, sODaM; ‘inner a(partment)s’ aMtaHpuraM, aMtarveSman n.
APART: I Separately: q. v.: pfTak.II At a distance: dUre.III Privately:(1) vijane; (2) niBftam. Ph.: a. from this, there is no other fault in the man. etadBinnastasya dozo nAsti.

APART , adv. Often expressed by the prep. vi; pfTak, viralaM, pravi- ralaM, pragataH -tA -taM, ujjfmBaH -mBA -mBaM; ‘having the knees apart,’ pragatajAnuH -nuH -nu. — (Privately) ekAnte, ekAntatas ind., niBftaM, rahasi, viviktaM, vijane. — (At a distance) dUre, kiyaddUre. — (Aside, to one's self) svagataM, vijane, janAntikaM.
APARTMENT: kozWaH: v. Room. The inner a. s antaHpuram. The attendants on the inner a. s anta- rvaMSikAH puruzAH D. i.
APARTMENT , s. SAlA, kozWaH, AvAsaH, AgAraM, gfhaM. — (The inner apartments) antaHpuraM, antargfhaM.
APARTMENT , s. kakzaH; ‘inner,’ kakzAntaraM, antarBavanaM.
APATHETIC; I Void of passion:(1) vItarAgaH (gA, gaM);(2) vItaspfhaH (hA, haM);(3) nispfhaH (hA, haM);(4) udAsaH (sA, saM);(5) virAgin (f. nI).II Indifferent: q. v.
APATHETIC , a. vItarAgaH -gA -gaM, niHsaNgaH -NgA -NgaM, niHspfhaH -hA -haM, nirIhaH -hA -haM, nirapekzaH -kzA -kzaM.
Apathy, s. OdAsInyaM, udAsInatA, vErAgyaM. [Apath]etic, a. udAsIna. 2 vItaspfha-rAga, niHspfha, nirIha, nirapekza. 3 nirutsAha.
APATHY: I Stoicism:(1) verAgyam;(2) OdAsyam.II Indifference.
APATHY , s. virAgaH, vErAgyaM, nirIhatA, jAqyaM, mAndyaM.
Ape, s. vAnaraH, kapiH, plava(vaM)gaH. 2 anukArin m. v. t. vAnaravat anukf 8 U. (gen.). Apish, a. kApeya (yI f.), vAnaropama.
APE (subs.): pucCahIno vAnaraH; kapiBedaH.
APE , s. vAnaraH, apucCaH kapiH m., plavaNgaH. — (Imitator) anukArI m. (n).
To APE , v. a. vAnaravat or kapivat anukf (c. 8. -karoti -karttuM).
Apepsy, s. ajIrRaM.
APEPSY , s. ajIrRaM, AmayAvitvaM, tIkzRAgniH m.
Aperient, s. recakaM, recanaM.

APERIENT , a. recakaH -kI -kaM. — (An aperient medicine) recakaH.
APERIENT , s. visraMsanaM. APEX, s. uccaH, mastakaH -kaM.
Aperture, s. CidraM, raMDraM, sUkzmaM dvAraM.
APERTURE: (1) Cidram;(2) ranDram; v. Open- -ing, fissure.
APERTURE , s. CidraM, ranDraM, dvAraM, paTaH. — (Act of opening) vyAdAnaM.
Apetalous, a. dalahIna, nizpatra, nirdala.
APETALOUS , a. dalahInaH -nA -naM, puzpapatrarahitaH -tA -taM, nizpatraH -trA -traM.
Apex, s. SiKA, cUqA, agraM; Siras n., mastakaM.
APEX: (1) cUqA;(2) SiKaram: v. Tip, point.
APEX , s. SiKA, SiKaraM, agraM, cUqA, SiraH n. (s).
Aphorism, s. sUtraM, vacanaM.
APHORISM: (1) sUtram;(2) vacanam: v. Maxim.
APHORISM , s. sUtraM, vacanaM, tattvaM, upadeSavAkyaM, AdeSaH.
APHORISTIC: Ph. the method of the book is a. *sUtrErgraTito granTaH.
APHRODISIAC , a. (Exciting passion) vAjIkaraH -rA -raM, kAmAgni- dIpanaH -nA -naM.
Apiary, s. maDumakzikA-karaMqaH-ADAraH-samudgakaH.
APIARY: *maDumakzikASAlA: v. Bee-hive.
APIARY , s. karaRqaH, CatrakaH, maDumakzikArakzaRasTAnaM, maDukarasTAnaM.
Apiece, adv. ekEkaSaH, pfTak pfTak, ekEkaM.

APIECE , adv. pratyekaM, ekEkaSas ind., ekaSas ind., ekatas ind., ekEkaM, pfTak pfTak, viBAgaSam ind.
APISH , a. kApeyaH -yI -yaM, kapisvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, vAnarozamaH -mA -maM. — (Imitative) anukAraSIlaH -lA -laM.
APISHNESS , s. kApeyaM, vAnaratA, anukAraSIlatA.
APITPAT , adv. pawapawA ind.
APOCALYPSE: prakASanam: v. Revelation.
APOCALYPSE , s. prakASitaM BavizyadvAkyaM, prakASanaM, vivftiH f., spazwIkaraRaM.
APOCOPE; *antyAkzaralopaH; *antyAkzaralopAlaNkAraH.
APOCOPE , s. antyAkzaralopaH, antyAkzaralopAlaNkAraH.
APOCRYPHA: kfzwIyopavedaH; *upaDarmapustakam.
APOCRYPHA , s. prarmmagranTAnAM maDye gaRitaH sandigDapramARo granTaH.

APOCRYPHAL , a. (Of uncertain authority) sandigDapramARaH -RA -RaM, asidDapramARaH -RA -RaM.
APOGEE: uccaH; candrakAntimaRqalasya pfTivyA davizWa- padam.
APOGEE , s. uccaM. APOLOGETIC, a. dozanyUnatAdarSakaH -kA -kaM.
APOLOGETIC , APOLOGETICAL, a. vyapadeSakaH -kA -kaM, pakzapAtI -tinI -ti (n), prativAdakaH -kA -kaM, CAdmikaH -kI -kaM.

APOLOGISE , v. n. (To state some plea) vyapadiSa (c. 6. -diSati [Page020-b+ 51] dezwuM), Cadma or vyapadeSaM or pratyavaskandaM kf. — (To acknowledge one's fault) svadopasya svIkAraM kf. — (To apologise for another) pakza- pAtaM kf, pararakzArTaM prativad (c. 1. -vadati -vadituM).

APOLOGIZE: (1) kzamAM prArTayate or yAcate;(2) marzayati (mfz, c. 10.), a. to the king for what we said amongst ourselves against etiquette marzayata lokapAlaM yadasmABirviSrabDapralApinIBirUpacArAtikrameRa BaRitam. Sa. iii.;(3) anu-nayati (nI, c. 1.) ( =to propitiate).

APOLOGUE , s. upakaTA, hitopadeSakaM upAKyAnaM, nItivAkyaM.

Apology, s. kzamAprArTanA, kzamAyAcanA, svadozasvIkAraH. 2 vyapa-apa-deSaH, Cadman n. [Apolog]ist, s. svadozasvIkArin m., vyapadezwf m. [Apolog]ize, v. i. kzamAM yAc 1 A, or prArTa 10 A, svadozaM svIkf-aMgIkf 8 U. 2 vyapadiS 6 P, vyapadeSaM-Cadma-kf. Apologetic, a. vyapadeSaka.

APOLOGY: I An excuse for a fault: Ph. to make an a. kzamAprArTanAM karoti; to accept an a. anunayavacanaM parigfhvAti (after ge.): v. Excuse. [Page032] II An apologetic treatise; no equiv.: *prativAdaH.
APOLOGY , s. vyapadeSaH, apadeSaH, upadeSaH, prativAdaH, uttaraM, Cadma n. (n), pratyavaskandaH, svadozasvIkAraH, CadmakaraRaM. — (For another) pakzapAtaH, pararakzArTaM prativAdaH.
APOLOGY , s. SamakaBAzaRaM, dozanivArakaBAzaRaM, kzamAprArTanaM.
Apophlegmatic, a. kaPanASana (nI f.).
APOPHLEGMATIC , a. kaPanASanaH -nI -naM, kaPaGnaH -GnI -GnaM, SlezmaGnaH -GnI -GnaM.
Apophthegm, s. sUtraM, vacanaM, nItivacanaM.
APOPHTHEGM: (1) vacanam:(2) vAkyam: v. Saying, maxim.
APOPHTHEGM , s. sUtraM, nItivAkyaM, vacanaM, AdeSaH.
APOPLECTIC: I subs.: sanyAsarogin (f. RI). II Adj.: Expr. by tat. comp.
APOPLECTICAL , APOPLECTIC, a. (Relating to apoplexy) aNgavi- kftivipayaH -yA -yaM. — (Inclined to apoplexy) aNgavikftiSIlaH -lA -laM.
Apoplexy, s. aMgavikfti f., saMnyAsaH.
APOPLEXY: sanyAsarogaH.
APOPLEXY , s. aNgavikftiH f.
APOPLEXY , s. sannyAsaH, SarIraviBraMSaH, aNgaviBraMSaH.
APOSTACY , s. svaDarmmatyAgaH, svaDarmmacyutiH f., avahAraH, svaDarmmaBraMSaH, BrazwatvaM, svajAtIyaDarmmatyAgAnantaraM paraDarmmASrayaH.
APOSTASY: (1) svaGarmatyAgaH (=abandonment of one's religion);(2) svamatatyAgaH ( = a. of one's principles);(3) paraDarmASrayaH (taking another religion): v. Desertion.

sanskrit.slp1: svaDarmaM svamataM svapakzaM vA parityajya paraDarmaM
sanskrit.word: स्वधर्मं स्वमतं स्वपक्षं वा परित्यज्य परधर्मं
sanskrit.iast: svadharmaṃ svamataṃ svapakṣaṃ vā parityajya paradharmaṃ

details.body: Apostate, s. svaDarmatyAgin m., svaDarmaBrazwaH-cyutaH, patitaH. Apostacy, s. svaDarmatyAgaH, DarmaBraMSaH, paraDarmASrayaH. Apostatize, v. i. svaDarmAt BraMS 1 A, 4 P or pat 1 P, paraDarmamASri 1 U.
APOSTATE: (1) *svaDarmatyAgin (f. nI);(2) yaH (yA, yat) svaDarmaM svamataM svapakzaM vA parityajya paraDarmaM, paramataM, parapakzaM vA avalambate, ASrayati, etc.
APOSTATE , s. svaDarmmatyAgI m. (n), svajAtIyavyavahAraBrazwaH, AtmaDarmmacyutaH, anyaSAKaH, svajAtIyaDarmmaM tyaktvA paraDarmmASritaH.
APOSTATIZE: svaDarmaM, svamataM, svapakzaM vA tyajati, pari- tyajati; svaDarmAt svamatAt vA BraMsate (BraMs, c. 1.), cyavate (cyu, c. 1.).

To APOSTATIZE , v. n. svaDarmmAt or svajAtIyavyavahArAd BraMS (c. 4. BraSyati, c. 1. BraMSate BraMSituM) or cyu (c. 1. cyavate cyotuM), vicyu; svajA- tIyaDarmmaM tyaktvA paraDarmmaM ASri (c. 1. -Srayati -SrayituM).
APOSTEME , APOSTHUME, s. SvayaTuH, vidraDiH m., SoPaH, sPowaH, pUyasa- mpUrRaH sPowaH.
Apostle, s. ISvarapreritaH, ISvaradUtaH.
APOSTLE: (1) *ISvaradUtaH;(2) maharziH. A. -Ship *ISvaradOtyam.
APOSTLE , s. ISvarapreritaH, ISvaradUtaH, ISvarAjYAvahaH, preritaH.
APOSTLESHIP , s. ISvarapreritatvaM, ISvaradOtyaM, preritvaM.
APOSTOLICAL , APOSTOLIC, a. (Enjoined by an apostle) ISvara- preritenAdizwaH -zwA -zwaM. — (Relating to the Apostles) ISvarapreritasa- sbanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
Apostrophe, s. saMboDanaM. [Apostroph]ize, v. t. saMbuD c., AmaMtr 10 A.
APOSTROPHE: I In Rhe.: samboDanam.II In gram.: *aminiDAnam.
APOSTROPHE , s. samboDanaM, vAkyAlaNkAraviSezaH.
APOSTROPHE , s. samboDitAnyasamboDanaM, prasaktAnuprasaktAnyasamboDanaM.
To APOSTROPHISE , v. a. samboDanaM kf, samboDanena Amantr (c. 10. -mantrayate -yituM).
APOSTROPHIZE: (1) samboDayati (c. of buD); (2) Ahvayati (hve, c. 1.).: v. To address.
APOSTUME , s. pUyasampUrRaH sPowaH, vidraDiH m.
Apothecary, s. OzaDAnAM vikretf m., Bezajavikrayin m.
APOTHECARY: (1) *OzaDakAraH;(2) Bizaj (m) ( =physician, q. v.).
APOTHECARY , s. vikrayArTaM OzaDapeSvaraH, BezajavikretA m. (tf), OzaDavi- kretA m. (tf), agadaNkAraH.
APOTHEOSIS , s. devatvaM, brahmatvaM, brahmanirvvARaM, devagaRitatvaM.
APPAL: vi-trAsayati, saM-, (c. of tras): v. To terrify.
To APPAL , v. a. BI in caus. (BAyayati or BIzayati -yituM), tras in caus. (trAsayati -yituM), vitras, santras; udvij in caus. (-vejayati -yituM), vyAkulIkf.
Appall, v. t. saM-vi-tras c., BI c., udvij c., vyAkulIkf 8 U; ‘he was a(ppall)ed with fear’ Bayena vivarRIBUtaH; ‘a(ppall)ing sight’ mahAtrAsajanakaM sTAnaM or darSanaM.
APPALLED , p. p. BayaviplutaH -tA -taM, BayasaMhfzwaromA -mA -ma (n), SaNkitaH -tA -taM, santrastaH -stA -staM, vyAkulIkftaH -tA -taM.
Apparatus, s. upakaraRaM, sAmagrI.
APPARATUS: upakaraRam: v. Tools, instruments.
APPARATUS , s. upakaraRaM, sajjA, yantraM, sAmagryaM, sAmagrI f. — (Military apparatus) SastropakaraRaM.
Apparel, s. veSaH-zaH, vastra, pariDAnaM, ABaraRaM. v. t. vas c., prAvf 5 U, saMvye 1 P.
APPAREL (subs.): paricCadaH: v. Dress, attire.
APPAREL , s. veSaH, vastraM, pariDAnaM, paricCadaH, ambaraM, ABaraRaM, saMvyAnaM

To APPAREL , v. a. vastra (nom. vastrayati -yituM), ACad (c. 10. -CAda- yati -yituM); vezw (c. 1. vezwate, vezwituM), vas in caus. (vAsayati -yituM), pravas; pravf (c. 5. -vfRoti, -varituM or -varItuM), savye (c. 1. -vyayati -vyAtuM). — (To apparel one's self) vas (c. 2. vaste, vasituM).
APPARELLED , p. p. AcCAditaH -tA -taM, pracCAditaH -tA -taM, paricCannaH -nnA -nnaM, vastravezwitaH -tA -taM, saMvItaH -tA -taM.

Apparent, a. vyakta, aBivyakta, sPuwa, spazwa, pratyakza, prakASa, AvirBUta. 2 miTyA ind., avAstava (vI f.); ‘a(pparent) praise’ vyAjastuti f. 3 bAhya, bahiH in comp.; ‘to make a(pparent)’ Avizkf, spazwI-prakawI-kf. [Apparent]ly, adv. vyaktaM, spazwaM &c. 2 bahiH; ‘a wise man acts a(pparently) agreeably’ vidvAn jano bahI ramaRIyaM vyavaharati (Mal. 1).

APPARENT (adj.): I Visible: q. v. prAdurBUta. (tA, taM).II Evident, clear: q. v.:(1) vyaktaH (ktA, ktaM);(2) sPuwaH (wA, waM);(3) spazwaH (zwA, zwaM). III Seeming (as opposed to real):(1) prakASaH (SA, SaM);(2) prakawaH (wA, waM);(3) bAhyaH (hyA, hyaM) ( =external, q. v.): v. Feigned, false.

APPARENT , a. vyaktaH -ktA -ktaM, aBivyaktaH -ktA -ktaM, pravyaktaH -ktA -ktaM, spazwaH -zwA -zwaM, sPuwaH -wA -waM, prekzaRIyaH -yA -yaM, prekzyaH -kzyA -kzyaM, pratyakzaH -kzA -kzaM. — (Not real) avAstavaH -vI -vaM; apparent praise,’ i. e. [Page021-a+ 51] ‘not real,’ vyAjastutiH f., miTyApraSaMsA; ‘heir-apparent,’ yuvarAjaH. — (To make apparent) prAduzkf, Avizkf, pratyakzIkf, spazwIkf, prakawIkf.
APPARENT , a. prakASaH -SA -SaM, AvirBUtaH -tA -taM, prAdurBUtaH &c.

APPARENTLY: I Plainly, clearly: q. v.: vyaktam.II Ostensibly, seemingly:(1) prakASaM;(2) prakawaM, Si. xvi. 19.;(3) bahiH ( =externally, q. v.), a. sweet, but really un- friendly maDuraM bahirantarapriyam, Si. xvi. 17.
APPARENTLY , adv. prAdus ind., sAkzAt ind., Avis, pratyakzatas, spazwaM.
Apparition, s. ABAsaH, CAyA, AkAraH. 2 vetAlaH, piSAcaH.
APPARITION: I Appearance: q. v.:II A ghost, phantom: q. v.: CAyA.
APPARITION , s. (Appearance, form) ABAsaH, ABA, CAyA, AkAraH, AkftiH f., rUpaM. — (Spectre, walking spirit) rAtriYcaraH, pretanaraH, pretaH, vetAlaH.
APPARITOR: no equiv.: dUtaH; anucaraH.
APPARITOR , s. yazwiDaraH, prepyajanaH, rAjadUtaH.
APPEACHMENT , s. aBiyogaH, apavAdaH.

Appeal, v. i. punarvicAraM prArT 10 A. 2 pramA-RIkf 8 U, pramARayati (D.); or by pramARaM; ‘I a(ppeal) to your lordship in this case’ atra vizaye'traBavaMtaM pramARIkaromi, atraBavAn pramARaM. s. punarvicAraprArTanAH; pramARIkaraRaM.

APPEAL (subs.): I Leg. t. t.: *punarvicAraprArTanA. A court of a. *ye prAqvivAkAH punarvicAraprArTanAM Srotumarhanti or SfRvanti.II Reference to some one as an authority or witness: Ph. to make an a. to pramARayati (nomi.).III Resort, recourse: q. v.IV An address of entreaty: prArTanA.

APPEAL (v. i.): I Leg. t. t.: punarvicAraM prArTayate (arT, c. 10.).II To refer to another as an authority: pramARayati: Ph. I a. to gods about it atra vizaye mama devAH sAkziRastizWanti.III To implore, entreat: q. v.IV To excite, affect: q. v.

To APPEAL , v. n. parAvarttaM prArT (c. 10. -arTayate -yituM); yat kAryyaM avaraprAqvivAkena tIritaM or nirRItaM tasyApi punarvicAram uttamaprAqvi- vAkasakASAt prArT. — (To call another as witness) sAkziRaM kf, Ahve (c. 1. -hvayati -te -hvAtuM).
APPEAL , s. parAvarttyavyavahAraH, punarAhvAnaM, punarvicAraprArTanA, uttamaprAqvi- vAkasAkzAd AhvAnaM. — (The calling upon any one as witness or judge) AhvAnaM.

Appear, v. i. udi 2 P, udgam 1 P, prakAS 1 A, prAdurBU 1 P, AvirBU. 2 upasTA 1 U, sanniDA pass. 3 pratiBA 2 P, avaBAs 1 A, dfS pass., lakz pass.; ‘so as to a(ppear) dead’ mftamivAtmAnaM saMdarSya; ‘the witness did not a(ppear)’ sAkzI nopatasTO. [Appear]ance, s. udayaH, prAdurBAvaH, AvirBAvaH. 2 upasTiti f. 3 AkAraH, Akfti f., rUpaM; ‘good in a(ppearance)’ SoBanAkfti, sudfSya, prekzaRIya. 4 ABAsaH, CAyA, ABA; ‘your story has an a(ppearance) of truth’ tava kaTA satyeva pratiBAti-avaBAsate. 5 anumAnaM.

APPEAR (v. i.): I To be visible:(1) AvirBavati or prAdurBavati, a herd of deer a. ed mfgARAM yUTamAvirbaBUva, R. ix. 55.;(2) prAdurasti (as, c. 1.) R. xi. 63.;(3) dfSyate, aTi-, prati-, (pass. of dfS) (=to be seen) not restricted to real life as (1) and (2).; a swan a. ed in their dream tayoH svapne kaScijjAlapAdaH pratyadfSyata, D. i.II To show one's self: Ph. she does not a. before me sA matsamakzaM nAgacCati (not darSanaM dadAti, see R. xix. 7.).III To be out: nirgacCati, an article a. ed in the Induprakāsha about so and so *amukavizayakaH prabanDa induprakASapatrikAyAM nirgataH. IV Leg. t. t: to be present:(1) upatizWati (sTA, c. 1.);(2) Perh. darSanaM dadAti. V. To seem: q. v. pratiBAti (BA, c. 2.).VI To be evident or clear: q. v.

To APPEAR , v. n. (To become visible) dfS in pass. (dfSyate), aBidfS, pratidfS; praBU (c. 1. -Bavati -BavituM), samBU, prakAS (c. 1. -kASate -kASituM), samprakAS, saNkAS, udi (c. 1. udayati -yituM), aByudi, uccar (c. 1. -carati -carituM). — (Show one's self) AtmAnaM dfS in caus. (darSayati -yituM), darSanaM dA. — (To seem) pratiBA (c. 2. -BAti -BAtuM), sampraBA, nirBA, ABA; lakz in pass. (lakzyate). — (To be evident) prakAS, prAdurBU (c. 1. -Bavati -BavituM), AvirBU; prAduras (c. 2. -asti); ‘you appear dismayed,’ vismita iva pratiBAsi.

APPEARANCE: I The act of becoming visible;(1) AvirBAvaH (=actual a. especi- -ally of invisible spirits). who wants to make his a. (in this world) yaScAvirBAvamicCati, Mah.; (2) by the verb: v. To appear (I);(3) prAdurBAvaH (rare), Kuv.II Act of being present:(1) upasTitiH;(2) darSanam, he who stands a security for one's a. yo yasya pratiBUstizWe- rSanAya. M. viii. 58.III personal a.: (1) AkAraH;(2) AkftiH. of good a.: sudfSyaH (SyA, SyaM).IV Semblance, mere show: [Page033] Ph. outward a. vAhyAkftiH; has an a. of justice nyAyamivAvaBAsate, Ki. xiv. 7.: v. Apparently (II). V. A phenomenon: q. v.:VI Proba- -bility, likelihood: q. v.

APPEARANCE , s. (Coming into sight) darSanaM, sandarSanaM. — (Entry into a place or company) upasTitiH f., praveSanaM. — (The thing seen) rUpaM, AkftiH f., mUrttiH f., AkAraH. — (Semblance, not reality) CAyA, ABAsaH, ABA, avastutA. — (Presence, mien) rUpaM, avasTA, BAvaH, AkAraH. — (Probability) anumeyatvaM, anuBavanIyatvaM.
APPEASABLE: SamanIyaH (yA, yaM): v. Placable.
Appease, v. t. sAM(SAM)tv 10, pra-upa-Sam c. (Samayati), tuz c., prasad c., anunI 1 P; ‘to be a(ppeas)ed’ prasad 1 P, paSam 4 P. [Appeas]ing, s. sAMtvanaM, pra-upa-SAMti f., prasAdanaM, anunayaH.
APPEASE: (1) Samayati, pra-, upa-, (c. of Sam); (2) sAntvayati, upa-, pari-, (sAntva, c. 10): v. Calm, propitiate.

To APPEASE , v. a. Sam in caus. (Samayati -yituM), upaSam, praSam; sAntv or SAntv (c. 10. sAntvayati -yituM), aBiSAntv, pariSAntv, upa- sAntv; tuz in caus. (tozayati -yituM), paritup, santuz; prasad in caus. (-sAdayati -yituM), aBiprasad, samprasad; susTiraM -rAM -raM kf; parimfS (c. 6. -mfSati -rmazwuM), parAmfS, anunI (c. 1. -nayati -te -netuM). — (To be ap- peased) Sam (c. 4. SAmyati, SamituM), upaSam; prasad (c. 1. -sIdati -sattuM).
APPEASED, TO BE: (1) SAmyati (Sam, c. 4.);(2) pra-sIdati (sad, c. 1.).
APPEASED , p. p. SAntaH -ntA -ntaM, SamitaH -tA -taM, praSAntaH -ntA -ntaM, ArA- DitaH -tA -taM, anunItaH -tA -taM, prasannaH -nnAM -nnaM, prasAditaH -tA -taM.
APPEASER: SamayitA; praSamayitA. v. To appease.
APPEASING (subs.): (1) SAntiH;(2) praSAntiH; (3) sAntvanA.
APPEASING , s. SAntiH f., upaSAntiH f., praSAntiH f., ArADanaM, prasAdanaM.
APPELLANT: *punarvicAraprArTin (f. nI); nideSa- BaNgArTin (f. nI).
APPELLANT , s. uttamaprAqvivAkasakASAt parAvarttaprArTakaH, parAvarttaprArTayitA m. (tf), punarAhvAnakarttA m. (rttf), AhvAnakarttA m. (rttf), AvedakaH.
APPELLATE: Ph. a. jurisdiction *punarvicArADikAraH; a. court ye prAqvivAkAH punarvicAraprArTanAM Srotumarhanti.
APPELLATE , s. punarAhUtaH, uttamaprANvivAkasAkzAd AhUtaH, pratyarTI m. (n).
Appellation, s. See Name. Appellative, a. aBiDAyin. 2 sAmAnya.
APPELLATION: nAmaDeyam; v. Name.
APPELLATION , s. nAmaDeyaM, nAma n. (n), AKyA, saMjYA, aBiDAnaM, aBiDA, aBiKyA, AhvA.
APPELLATIVE: i. e. common: (1) sADAraRaH (RA, RaM);(2) sAmAnyaH (nyA, nyaM).
APPELLATIVE , a. aBiDAyikaH -kA -kaM, aBiDAnIyakaH -kA -kaM. — (Common) sAmAnyaH -nyA -nyaM, sADAraRaH -RA -RaM
APPELLEE , s. AhUtaH, aBiyuktaH, pratyarTI m. (n).
Append, v. t. anubaMD 9 P, upADA 3 U, AsaMj c. [Append]age, s. anubaMDaH; upAhitaBAgaH. 2 upakaraRaM. [Append]ed, s. saMyojita, upAhita. [Append]ix, s. pariSizwaM, SezasaMgrahaH.
APPEND: anubaDnAti (banD, c. 9.) (?).
To APPEND , v. a. anubanD (c. 9. -baDnAti -bandDuM) or caus. -banDayati -yituM), AbanD; upADA (c. 3. -daDAti -Datte -DAtuM), ADA; avalamb in caus. (-lambayati -yituM).
APPENDAGE: Ph. a house with its a. s *sopakaraRaM gfhaM; virtue is an a. of belief in God *sadAcAra AstikyabudDimanubaDnAtiH, v. Concomitant.
APPENDAGE , s. anubanDaH, sambanDaH, upAhitaM, SepAMSaH, upAhitaBAgaH.
APPENDANT , adj. anubanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), sambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n). [Page021-b+ 51] avalambI -mbinI -mbi (n).
APPENDIX: pariSizwam.
APPENDIX , s. pariSizwaM, upagranTaH, SezagranTaH.
APPENDIX , s. uttaraKaRqaH, parivfMhaRaH, granTaSezaH, SezasaNgrahaH.
Appertain, v. i. See Belong. Appertenance, s. anubaMDaH; upakaraRaM, upaskaraH, sAmagrI.

To APPERTAIN , v. n. (To belong to one's self) AtmasAt or AtmADInaH -nA -naM, or svADInaH -nA -naM, or svakIyaH -yA -yaM as. — (To belong, in general) sambanG in pass. (-baDyate). The sense of ‘appertaining’ may often be expressed by the root as or vid with the gen. case: as, ‘money appertains to me,’ mama DanaM vidyate.
APPERTAINING , p. sambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), anubanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
APPERTENANCE , s. anubanDaH, sambanDaH, upakaraRaM, sAmagrI.
APPETENCY , s. kAmaH, loBaH, aBilAzaH, vAYCA, icCA.
Appetite, s. kAmaH, rAgaH, aBilAzaH, icCA, ruci f. 2 buBukzA, kzuDA-D f.; ‘sensual a(ppetite)’ vizayaruciH, vizayoparAgaH.
APPETITE: I Any mental desire:(1) kAmaH; (2) rAgaH; v. Desire, longing.II actual desire for food:(1) kzuDA;(2) buBukzA;(3) aSanAyA.

APPETITE , s. (Desire) kAmaH, loBaH, rAgaH, ruciH f., aBiruciH f., ativAYCA, atiSayaloBaH, aBilAzaH, icCA. — (Hunger) buBukzA, kzuDA, AhArAdivAYCA, BaktaCandaM. — (The digestive faculty caus- ing appetite) agniH m., vahniH m., agnivfdDiH f. — (One who has no appetite for food) agnirahitaH.
APPETITIVE , a. kAmukaH -kA -kaM, aBilApukaH -kA -kaM, icCukaH -kI -kaM.

sanskrit.word: उच्चैः प्रशंसावाच उदीरयत्सु श्रोतृषु स वक्तुमुदतिष्ठत्
sanskrit.iast: uccaiḥ praśaṃsāvāca udīrayatsu śrotṛṣu sa vaktumudatiṣṭhat

details.body: Applaud, v. t. praSaMs 1 P, SlAG 1 A, aBinaMd 1 P, stu 2 U. 2 upagE 1 P. Applause, s. praSaMsA, SlAGA, stuti f. 2 praSaMsAvAcaH (pl.). DanyavAdaH; ‘he rose to speak amidst loud a(pplause)’ uccEH praSaMsAvAca udIrayatsu Srotfzu sa vaktumudatizWat. Applausive, a. SlAGAnvita; stutimaya (yI f.).
APPLAUD: (1) praSaMsati (SaMs, c. 1.) v. To praise; (2) gAyati, upagAyati (gE, c. 1.) Ki. xvii. 47.; (3) vandate, pari-, (vand, c. 1.), a. ed by the chiefs of the clans gaRapatiBiH parivanditena, Ki.
To APPLAUD , v. a. praSaMs (c. 1. -SaMsati -SaMsituM), aBipraSaMs; pratinand (c. 1. -nandati -nandituM), praRAdena praSaMs, praSaMsAM kf, SlAGAM kf. — (By clapping the hands) karatAlena praSaMs.

APPROACH , s. AgamaH, aBigamanaM, AgamanaM, upagamaH, upasTitiH f., upasannatA.

II To take to one's self:(1) AtmasAt karoti (kf, c. 8.), what princes strive to a. even by misdeeds duritErapi kartumAtmasAt prayatante nfpasUnavo hi yat, R. viii. 2;(2) svAyattaH (ttA, ttaM) or svADInaH (nA, naM) (agreeing with the object) karoti, M. n. (not very common).
APPROPRIATE (adj.): I Apposite, suitable: q. v.: upapannaH (nnA, nnaM), this epithet is very a. for the breeze upapannaM viSezaRamasya vAyoH V. ii.II Peculiar: q. v.

To APPROPRIATE , v. a. (To consign to some particular use) prayuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yuMkte -yoktuM, caus. -yojayati -yituM), upayuj, viniyuj. — (To claim to one's self by an exclusive right) svIkf, svIyamiti or mameti vad (c. 1. vadati vadituM), svakIyaM -yAM -yaM or AtmIyaM -yAM -yaM or svADInaM -nAM -naM or AtmADInaM -nAM -naM or AtnasAt kf, svasvatvaM buD in caus. (boDayati -yituM), or jYA in caus. (jYApa- yati -yituM.)

(Suited to the occasion) prastAvasadfSaH -SI -SaM. — (Belonging peculiarly) AtmanInaH -nA -naM, svakIyaH -yA -yaM, sambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), sambanDakaH -kA -kaM, viSezakaH -kA -kaM, janInaH -nA -naM. — (Suitable) yuktaH -ktA -ktaM, yogyaH -gyA -gyaM, saNgataH -tA -taM, upayogI -ginI -gi (n).

APPROPRIATENESS , s. (Fitness of application) yuktatA, yogyatvaM, OcityaM, upayuktatA, sAmaYjasyaM, saNgatatA.
APPROPRIATION: (1) prayogaH;(2) viniyogaH; (3) upakalpanam (?).
APPROPRIATION , s. (The application of something to a par- ticular purpose) upayogaH, prayogaH, viniyogaH. — (Claiming any thing as peculiar) AtmagrahaRaM, svatvaboDanaM, AtmasAtkaraRaM.
APPROVAL: (1) anumodanam (rare);(2) sammatiH (=assent);(3) by the verb, you have received my a. mayAnumodito'si: v. Also approba- -tion.

APPROVAL , APPROBATION, s. anumodanaM, AnumatyaM, pratigrahaH.

III To commend: q. v.

(rocayati -yituM), anuruc; ‘that is approved by me,’ tan mayA praSasyate or tan mahyaM rocate. pratinand (c. 1. -nandati -nandituM), anuruD (c. 4. -ruDyate -rodDuM). — (To prove, show) pramARIkf, pramAR (nom. pramARayati -yituM), viBU in caus. (-vArayati -yituM). — (To stay for) pratIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -IkzituM).

ARABIA , s. yavanaH, yavanadeSaH.
ARABIAN , a. yavanasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), yavanadeSIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘an Arabian,’ yavanadeSajaH.
ARABIC , s. (Language) yavanaBAzA, yAvanaBAzA.

ARBOROUS , a. vArkzaH -rkzI -rkzaM, vArkzyaH -rkzyI -rkzyaM, vfkzasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
