Arcadian, a. grAmya, grAmIRa.

Arch, s. KaMqamaMqalaM, vfttaKaMqaM; ‘a(rch) of heaven’ naBomaMqalaM. 2 toraRaH-RaM. v. t. maMqalIkf toraRarUpeRa nirmA 3 A, golAkAreRa AcCad 10, ‘a(rch)ed’ satoraRa, nyastatoraRa; Bugna, kuMcita, vakra, toraRAkAra. a. vidagDa, DUrta, catura; muKya, SrezWa, uttama, praDAna, agraRI; ‘a(rch) fiend’ piSAcAgraRIH; ‘a(rch) angel’ praDAnadevadUtaH; ‘a(rch) bishop’ muKyo DarmADyakzaH.
ARCH (subs.) toraRa (mn) (properly=an arched gateway, but may, by analogy, be applied to other arches).
ARCH (v): I To cover with an arch: toraRaM nyasyati (as, c. 4) (after Mu.) or toraRena pracCA- dayati (Cad c. 10).II To bend, curve: q. v.
ARCH (adj.): caturaH (rA, raM): v. Cunning, sly.
ARCH , s. (Part of a circle) KaRqamaRqalaM, vfttaKaRqaM, golaKaRqaM. — (Arched gateway) toraRaH -RaM. — (The arched roof of a house) KoqakaSIrzaM. — (Vault of heaven) KagolaH, naBImaRqalaM.
ARCH , a. (Sly, waggish) krIqASIlaH -lA -laM, rasikaH -kA -kaM, lolApANgaH -NgA -NgaM, vidagDaH -gDA -gDaM. — (Chief) praDAnaH -nA -naM, muKyaH -KyA -KyaM, uttamaH -mA -maM, SrezWaH -zWA -zWaM.

To ARCH , v. a. (To make in the form of an arch) maRqalIkf, golIkf toraRarUpeRa nirmA (c. 2. -mAti, c. 4. -mAyate -mAtuM) or kf in caus. (kArayati -yituM), toraRAkArapawalena ACad (c. 10. -CAdayati -yituM). — (To build an arch) toraRaM nirmA.
ARCHAEOLOGIST: *purARasAhityavid; prAkkAlIna- sAhityAdivizayezu paRqitaH.
Archæology, s. purARavastuSAstraM.
ARCHAEOLOGY: *purARasAhityam; prAkkAlInasAhi- tyAdivizayakA vidyA.
Archaic, a. Arza, prAcIna.
ARCHAIOLOGY or ARCHAEOLOGY, s. prAkkAlInavyavahAravizayaM vAkyaM, purA- tanaSAstraM.
Archaism, s. prAcIna-Arza-prayogaH.
ARCHAISM: *prAcInaprayogaH: A. s occurring in the Mahābhārata, Rāmāyana, Manu, etc. are called ArzaprayogaH.
ARCHANGEL: *ISvarasya praDAnadUtaH.
ARCHANGEL , s. ‘ISvaradUtAnAM maDye muKyadUtaH or praDAnadUtaH, ISvaradUtADi- zWAtA m. (tf).
ARCHBISHOP: *kfzwIyasampradAyezu sarvapraDAnAcAryaH.
ARCHBISHOP , s. DarmmADyakzARAM maDye praDAno or muKyo DarmmADyakzaH.
ARCHBISHOPRIC: *kfzwIyasampradAyezu yaH sarvapraDAnAcAryaH, tasyADikAraH.
ARCHDEACON: *IlaRqadeSe viSapasya nimnasTo Darmo- pAsakaH.
ARCHDEACON , s. (The bishop's vicegerent) DarmmADyakzasahAyaH, DarmmADyakzopakArakaH.
ARCHDEACONRY: I The office of an arch- -deacon: *Arcaqikanapadam.II His residence: *ArcaqikanAvAsaH.III His jurisdiction *Arcaqi- kanasyADikAraH.
ARCHDUCHY: Ph. a. of Baden vAdenarAjyam: v. Kingdom.
ARCHDUKE (m.), Archduches (f.): upADiviSezaH; *uparAjaH (m), uparAYjI (f.).
ARCHED: I Covered with an arch: nyastatoraRaH (RA, RaM) (?), an a. gateway toraRam.II In the form of an arch, curved:(1) BugnaH (gnA, gnaM); (2) kuYcitaH (tA, taM).
ARCHED , p. p. maRqalIkftaH -tA -taM, golIkftaH -tA -taM, toraRAkAraH -rA -raM, kuYcitaH -tA -taM.
Archer, s. Danvin m., DAnuzkaH, izuDaraH, nizaMgin m., DanurDaraH. [Archer]y, s. DanurvidyA, SarAByAsaH, DanurvedaH.
ARCHER: I A bowman: q. v.: DAnuzkaH.II The constellation: Danus (n.)
ARCHER , s. DanurDaraH DanvI m. (n), DanvA m. (n), DanupmAn m. (-t), DAnuzkaH, DanurDArI m. (n), izvAsaH, izuDaraH, kARqIraH, nizaNgI m., astrI m.
ARCHERY: (1) DanurvidyA (the art);(2) SarAByAsaH (the practice).
ARCHERY , s. DanurvidyA, SarAByAsaH, upAsanaM, SarAGAtaH, vARamokzaRaM. — (Skilled in) kftahastaH, suprayogaviSiKaH, kftapuNKaH.
Archetype, s. mUlarUpaM, AdarSaH.
ARCHETYPE: AdarSaH: v. Pattern, model.
ARCHETYPE , s. mUlaM, mUlamUrttiH f., AdarSaH, sUkzmaSarIraM.
Archipelago, s. dvIpasamUhaH. 2 dvIpacitArRavaH.
ARCHIPELAGO: dvIpasamUhaH; dvIpasaNGAtaH; etc.

sanskrit.slp1: loke gurutvaM viparItatAM vA svacezwitAnyeva naraM nayaMti
sanskrit.word: लोके गुरुत्वं विपरीततां वा स्वचेष्टितान्येव नरं नयंति
sanskrit.iast: loke gurutvaṃ viparītatāṃ vā svaceṣṭitānyeva naraṃ nayaṃti

details.body: Architect, s. sTapatiH, Silpin m.; ‘man is the a(rchitect) of his own fortune’ loke gurutvaM viparItatAM vA svacezwitAnyeva naraM nayaMti (H. 2). [Architect]ure, s. SilpaM, vastunirmARakOSalaM, nirmARaSilpaM.
ARCHITECT: I Lit.:(1) vAstuvidyopajIvin (m), K. b.;(2) sTapatiH, P. i. 1.;(3) Silpin (n.) (=artisan, but may be appropriately used when the sense is clear), R.II. Fig.: a maker: q. v.: kartA.
ARCHITECT , s. sTapatiH m., gfhAdinirmmARavidyAjYaH, gfhanirmmARADyakzaH, nirmmAtA m. (tf).
ARCHITECTURAL: expr. by comp., a. skill nirmARakOSalama.
ARCHITECTURAL , a. nirmmARavidyAsambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
ARCHITECTURE: (1) vAstuvidyA;(2) gfhanirmARaSilpam (?);(3) Silpam (when the sense is clear). Si. iii. 35.
ARCHITECTURE , s. nirmmARavidyA, nirmmARaSilpaM, gfhAdinirmmARaSilpaM.
ARCHITRAVE: no equiv.: *upastamBaH.
ARCHITRAVE , s. gfhasya yo BAgaH stamBAgre avalambate or niveSyate.
Archives, s. graMTarakzAgAraM. 2 purAvfttaM.
ARCHIVES: I Records: *prAcInapatrasaYcayaH.II The place where they are kept: *prAcIna- patrAgAram.
ARCHIVES , s. prAkkAlInagranTarakzAgAraM. — (Ancient records) itihAsaH, purAvfttaM
ARCHLY: (1) caturam;(2) vidagDam.
ARCHNESS: (1) cAturyam;(2) cAturI;(3) vEdagDam.
ARCHNESS , s. vidagDatA, vEdagDyaM, rasitvaM.
ARCHWISE , adv. toraRarUpeRa, ardDamaRqalAkAreRa, toraRavat; DanurAkAreRa.
Arctic, a. uttara, udIcIna, uttarakeMdrIya.
ARCTIC: *uttarakendrIyaH (yA, yaM): the a. pole uttara- kendram.
ARCTIC , a. uttaraH -rA -raM, udIcInaH -nA -naM, uttarakendrIyaH -yA -yaM, citraSiKaRqyaDaHsTito BUgolaBAgaH.
ARCUER , s. tarkI m. (n), vivAdI m. (n), vicArakaH, prativAdI m. (n), nyAyI m. (n).
ARDENCY , s. uttApaH, utsAhaH, ugratA, vyagratA, kOtUhalaM, utsukatA.

Ardent, a. uttapta, pracaMqa, utkawa, utsuka, kutUhalin, utsAhin, vyagra; ‘a(rdent) love’ niratiSayonurAgaH; ‘a(rdent) looks’ satfzRA dfzwiH. [Ardent]ly, adv. utkawaM, satfzRaM, sAnurAgaM. Ardour, s. uttApaH, atyaMtatA, niratiSayaH, atirekaH, utkawatA, utsAhaH, vyagratA, kutUhalaM, OtsukyaM.

ARDENT: I Fiery, hot: q. v.: pracaRqaH (RqA, RqaM). II Eager: Ph. a. eyes (of a lover) satfzRanayane. III Warm, affectionate: atyantaH (ntA, ntaM) or niratiSayaH (yA, yaM) (=excessive), a. love [Page037] niratiSayAnurAgaH: Ph. a. vows (of a lover) SapaTAH (m. pl.).

ARDENT , a. (Hot) uttaptaH -ptA -ptaM, pracaRqaH -RqA -RqaM. — (Eager) kutUhalI -linI -li (n), utsukaH -kA -kaM, atIcCaH -cCA -cCaM, vyagraH -grA -graM, utsAhI -hinI -hi (n). — (Affectionate) anurAgI -giRI -gi (n).
ARDENTLY: satfzRaM (as in gazing); (2) atyantaM (=excessively).
ARDENTLY , adv. uttApena, kOtUhalena, Otsukyena, sAnurAgaM.
ARDOUR: I Heat: q. v. uttApaH.II Warmth, eagerness: utsAhaH; with a. sotsAhaM. Ph. the a. of his love tasya niratiSayAnurAgaH.
ARDOUR , s. uttApaH, AsaktiH f., ugratA, vyagratA, kOtUhalaM, OtsukyaM, utsAhaH. — (Of affection) anurAgaH.
Arduous, a. duzkara, yatnasADya, duHsADya, su-ati-duzkara. 2 prAMSu, durAroha, ucca.
ARDUOUS: I Lofty: q. v.II Difficult: q. v. duzkaraH (rA, raM).

ARDUOUS , a. (Lofty) uccaH -ccA -ccaM, prAMSuH -SuH -Su, ArohaRadurgamyaH -myA -myaM. — (Difficult) duzkaraH -rA -raM, suduzkaraH -rA -raM, atiduzkaraH -rA -raM, kaWinaH -nA -naM, durgamyaH -myA -myaM, duHsADyaH -DyA -DyaM, duScaraH -rA -raM.
ARDUOUSNESS , s. uccatA, uttuNgatA. — (Difficulty) kaWinatA, kAWinyaM.
Area, s. PalaM; ‘a(rea) of a field’ kzetraPalaM. 2 aMgaRaM-naM; ‘inner a(rea)’ prakozWaH.
AREA I Outer a.: aNganam: v. Yard.II Inner a. prakozWaH.III In geo. Palam, a. of a circle vfttakzetraPalam; a. of a triangle triBujaPalam, Li.
AREA , s. aNgaRaM, prANgaRaM, amyantarasTAnaM.
AREA , s. (In geometry) PalaM, kzetraPalaM, garBaH, aByantaraM; ‘precise area,’ sPuwaPalaM. — (Any open surface) aNganaM, aNgaRaM, kzetraM.
Arena, s. raMgaH, raMgaBUmi f., mallaBUH.
ARENA: (1) raNgaH;(2) raNgaBUmiH;(3) akzavAwaH (rare).
ARENA , s. raNgaH, raNgaBUmiH f., mallaBUH, akzavAwaH.
Argent, a. rAjata (tI f.), rOpya (pyI f.).
ARGENT , a. rUpyaH -pyA -pyaM, rOpyaH -pyI -pyaM, rAjataH -tI -taM.
ARGILLOUS , a. mfRmayaH -yI -yaM, mArttikaH -kI -kaM, cikkaRamfttikAmayaH -yI -yaM.
ARGONAUTIC: Ph. a. expedition *kanakorRAnveza- RAya jesanasya kalvisaM prati yAtrA.
ARGOSY: bfhannOviSezaH: v. Merchantman.

Argue, v. i. tark 10, UhApohaM kf 8 U, vicar c., vivecanaM kf. 2 vivad 1 A, vAde uttaraM-pratyuttaraM kf. v. t. pramARena-tarkeRa siD c.; (sADayati), pramARayati (D.), yuktivAdena siD c., yuktyA tark 10, Uh 1 A. [Argu]er, s. tarkin m., vicArakaH, vAdin m. Argument, s. yukti f., upapatti f. 2 pakzaH, pramARaM, hetuH, nyAyaH, vitarkaH; ‘a wrong a(rgument)’ pakzABAsaH, hetvABAsaH. 3 vAdAnuvAdaH, vivAdaH, vAkkalahaH. 4 vizayaH, anukramaRikA. [Argument]ative, a. tArkika (kI f.), tarkAnubadDa, nyAyAnusArin upapattimat. 2 vAdaSIla, vivAdapriya. [Argument]ly, adv. sopapattikaM, savitarkaM, yuktivAdena.
ARGUE (v. i.): I To reason: tarkayati, vi-, (tark, c. 10) or tarkaM karotiII To infer: q. v.: (1) tarkayati; Uhate (Uh, c. 1).
ARGUE (v. t.): I To discuss: Ph. he a. d the cause very ably *sa yuktiM pradaSrya sunipuRaM tarkayAmAsa. II To prove or evince: q. v.

To ARGUE , v. n. (To reason) vicar in caus. (-cArayati -yituM), tark (c. 10. tarkayati -yituM), vitark, vivecanaM kf. — (To dispute) vivad (c. 1. -vadate -vadituM), vAdAnuvAdaM or uttarapratyuttaraM kf.

To ARGUE , v. a. (To prove by argument) pramAR, (nom. pramA- Rayati -yituM), pramARIkf, pramARena or tarkeRa or vicAreRa sidDIkf; sUc (c. 10. sUcayati -yituM). — (To charge with, as a crime) dopAropaM kf, apavad (c. 1. -vadati -vadituM), aDikzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM).

ARGUMENT: I A process of reasoning:(1) tarkaH;(2) vitarkaH.II Any reason alleged: (1) yuktiH, when all a. s fail yuktizvapyavasannAsu; (2) uppattiH Ki. ii. 23.III A debate, dis- -cussion: q. v.: vAdAnuvAdaH.IV The subject of a discourse, etc.: Ph. I will give the a. (of the play) saMkzepata itivfttamaBiDIyate, Tārānāth: v. Subect. v. An abstract summary: q. v.

ARGUMENT , s. (A reason stated) pakzaH, pramARaM, hetuH m., kAraRaM, vitarkaH, nyAyaH; ‘a false argument,’ pakzABAsaH; ‘a different side of the argument,’ pakzAntaraM. — (Controversy) vAdAnuvAdaH, vAdayudDaM, vAkkalahaM, vicAraH, vitarkaH, vivAdaH, vitaRqA. — (The subject of any [Page024-b+ 51] work) vizayaH. — (Table of contents) anukramaRikA, nirGaRwaH.

ARGUMENT , s. (Apposite argument) udAharaRaM, udAhAraH, upodGAtaH, sADanaM, sADakaM; ‘to bring forward another argument,’ arTAnta- ropanyAsaM kf. — (Contents, heads) upodGAtaH, granTasTavizayAnukramaRikA.
ARGUMENTATION: tarkaH: v. Reasoning.
ARGUMENTATION , s. vitarkaRaM, vicAraRaM, nyAyaH.
ARGUMENTATIVE: tArkikaH (kI, kaM): Ph. it is a. of almighty power in the creator etadISvarasya sarvaSaktitvaM pradarSayati.

ARGUMENTATIVE , a. (Consisting of argument) tArkikaH -kI -kaM, vitarkI -rkiRI -rki (n), vivAdI -dinI -di (n), nyAyI -yinI -yi (n), vicArI -riRI -ri (n). — (Disposed to controversy) vi- vAdaSIlaH -lA -laM, vivAdArTI -rTinI -rTi (n), vivAdapriyaH -yA -yaM.
ARGUMENTATIVE , a. vAdavivAdarUpaH -pA -paM, vivAdAtmakaH -kA -kaM.
ARGUMENTATIVELY , adv. savitarkaM, vAdAnuvAdapUrvvakaM, vitarkapUrvvakaM, nyAyavat.
Arid, a. Suzka, AtapAkrAMta; ‘a(rid) soil’ maruH, marusTalaM-lI.
ARID: (1) SuzkaH (zkA, zkaM);(2) pariSuzkaH (zkA, zkaM): v. Dry, parched.
ARID , a. SuzkaH -zkA -zkaM, SozitaH -tA -taM, pariSuzkaH -zkA -zkaM; ‘arid soil,’ maruH m., marusTalI, DanvA m. (n).
ARIDITY: SuzkatA.: v. Dryness.
ARIDITY , s. SuzkatA, -tvaM, SozaH, SozaRaM, pariSozaH
ARIES: a constellation: mezaH; mezarASiH.
ARIES , s. (The Sign) mezaH, see ZODIAC.
Aright, adv. yuktaM, yaTAtaTaM, yaTAsTAnaM, samyak, yaTArhaM.
ARIGHT: (1) yuktam,(2) yaTocitam;(3) samyak.
ARIGHT , adv. yuktaM, ftaM, yaTAtaTaM, yaTocitaM, yaTAyogyaM, samyak, yaTArhaM.

Arise, v. i. utTA 1 P; utpadU 4 A, ut-pra-saM-BU 1 P, prajan 4 A, pravft 1 A; udi 2 P, udgam 1 P; Avi-prAdu-rBU, viniH-pra-sf 1 P, ‘a(ris)ing from’ ex. by ja, Bava, udBava, praBava, in comp.; smarajA pIqA ‘torment a(ris)ing from love’; yOvanapraBavaM tamaH &c.; oft. by utTa, samutTa; nayanasamutTaM jyotiH, ‘Flash arising from the eye’.

ARISE: (1) udeti (i, c. 2);(2) udgacCati (gam, c. 1): v. To rise, produce (iv). N. B. These two verbs are used in all the senses the English verb: a. ing from the seat Asa- nAdudvan, Ki. ii. 57.; the moon arose udagAt suDA- sUtiH, K.; does (not) your fear a., maiden udeti te BIrapi kinnu bAle, N. iii. 13.

To ARISE , v. n. (To stand up) utTA for utsTA (c. 1. -tizWati -te -TAtuM). — (To have origin) utpad (c. 4. -padyate -pattuM), samutpad; uccar (c. 1. -carati -carituM), udi (c. 1. -ayati -etuM), aByudi, samudi; praBU (c. 1. -Bavati -BavituM), samBU, AvirBU, prAdurBU; pravft (c. 1. -varttate -varttituM), prasf (c. 1. -sarati -sarttuM), udBA (c. 2. -BAti -BAtuM), nirBA; AtmAnaM dfS in caus. (darSayati -yituM), jan (c. 4. jAyate janituM), aBijan, upajan, saYjan. — (From death) pratisaYjan, samutTA.
ARISEN , p. p. utTitaH -tA -taM, saYjAtaH -tA -taM, jAtaH -tA -taM, janitaH -tA -taM, utpannaH -nnA -nnaM, samutpannaH -nnA -nnaM, viniHsftaH -tA -taM, janyaH -nyA -nyaM.

ARISING FROM (as adj.): (1) jaH (jA, jaM) or janitaH (tA, taM) (in comp.), the infamy a. from the assassination of Parvateśvara parvateSvaravinASa- janitasyAyaSasaH, Mu. iii.;(2) BavaH, udBavaH, praBavaH (vA, vaM) (in comp.), the darkness a. from youth is very impervious atigahanaM tamo yOvanapraBavaBa, K.; (3) utTaH, samutTaH (tTA, tTaM), bodily pains are those a. from diseases etc. tatra SArIraM vyADyAdyu tTam, S.p. b.
Aristocracy, s. kulIna-viSizwa-janAH. 2 SizwajanasattAkaM rAjyaM. Aristocratic, a. kulIna, aBijAta.
ARISTOCRACY: I A form of Government: *kulInaSAsanam or kulInapraButvam.II The persons of whom it is composed *kulInasampradAyaH or rAjyaSAsakakulInavargaH.
ARISTOCRACY , s. (A form of government) kflInajanADizWitaM rAjyaM, kflInavargapramuKaM rAjyaM, kulInavargapraButvaM. — (The persons of whom it is composed) kulInajanAH, kulInavargaH.
ARISTOCRAT: I A member of an aristo- -cracy: *kulInaH.II One who supports aristocracy: *kulInaSAsanasamarTakaH.
ARISTOCRATIC: Ph. a. government *kulInaSAsa- nam; a. pride kulABimAnaH; of a. family kulInaH (nA, naM) or aBijAtaH (tA, taM).
ARISTOCRATICAL , a. kulInaH -nA -naM, kulInakaH -kA -kaM, kOleyaH -yI -yaM, kulInavargayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, utkfzwaH -zwA -zwaM.
ARISTOCRATICALLY , adv. kulInajanavat, rAjanyavat, kulInakaprakAreRa.
Arithmetic, s. aMkavidyA-gaRitaM, parikarman n. [Arithmetic]ian, s. aMkavidyAjYaH, gaRakaH.
ARITHMETIC: (1) aNkavidyA;(2) pAwIgaRitam. The eight rules of a. parikarmAzwakam.
ARITHMETIC , s. gaRanAvidyA, gaRitaM, pAwIgaRitaM, aNkavidyA, paripAwiH f. -wI parikarmma n. (n); ‘the eight rules of arithmetic,’ parikarmmAzwaka.

ARITHMETIC , s. vyaktaM, vyaktagaRitaM, saMKyAvidyA; ‘the eight rules of arithmetic,’ parikarmmAzwakaM. These are, 1. Addition, saNkalanaM; 2. Subtraction, vyavakalanaM; 3. Multiplication, guRanaM; 4. Divi- sion, BajanaM; 5. Raising to the square, vargaH; 6. Extracting the square-root, vargapadaM; 7. Raising to the cube, GanaH; 8. Extracting the cube-root, GanapadaM.
ARITHMETICAL: (1) aNkavidyAvizayakaH (kA, kaM) (relating to a.);(2) aNkavidyAnusAreRa (according to the rules of a.).
ARITHMETICAL , a. gaRanAvidyAnurUpaH -pA -paM, aNkavidyAnusArI -riRI -ri (n).
ARITHMETICIAN: aNkavidyAviSAradaH (dA, daM) and sim. comp. s.
ARITHMETICIAN , s. gaRanAvidyAjYaH, gaRanASAstrapaRqitaH, aNkavidyAjYaH, gaRakaH.

ARJUNA , s. (The third and most celebrated of the five sons of Pāndu. He was the son of Pāndu only by courtesy, being in fact the child of his wife Pṛthā or Kuntī by the god Indra) arjunaH. — (As son of Pṛthā) pArTaH, kOnteyaH, kuntisutaH — (As son of Indra) EndriH, pAkaSAsaniH. — (The crested one) kirIwI m. — (The Conqueror) jizRuH. — (Wealth- acquiring) DanaYjayaH. — (Drawing the bow with the left hand) savyasAcI m. — (Having hair like the Euphorbia) guqAkeSaH. — (Son of Pāndu) pARquputraH; his bow is called gARqIvaH -vaM or gARqivaH -vaM.
Ark, s. nO f., taraRI, potaH. 2 ADAraH, kozaH.
ARK: I A vessel: q. v.:(1) nOH;(2) taraRI. II. A. chest:(1) pewikA;(2) ADAraH.
ARK , s. (A vessel, ship) nOH, nOkA, potaH, taraRI, vfhannOkA. — (A chest) ADAraH, kozaH, pewikA, pewaH -wA -wI.

Arm, s. bAhuH, BujaH, BujA, dos m. n.; ‘fore-a(rm)’ prakozWaH. 2 SAKA. 3 nadIvaMkaH, vakraM. 4 Sakti f., balaM vIryaM; ‘got by oneʼs own a(rm)’ svaBujavIryeRa labDaM, BujopArjitaM. v. t. sannah c., sajjIkf 8 U, astrEH saMyuj, 10, sAyuDa a. kf. v. i. sannah 4 U, sajjIBU 1 P. s. astraM, SastraM, AyuDaH-DaM, SastrAstraM. 2 vigrahaH, raRasamayaH, saMgrAmaH, yudDaM; ‘taking up a(rm)’ yudDAraMBaH; ‘passage of a(rm)’ astravidyA. [Arm]ed, sAyuDa, sannadDa, sajja; ‘a(rmed) with a sword’ saKaNgaH. [Arm]less, a. aBuja, aSastra, anAyuDa. [Arm]pit, [Arm]hole, s. kakzAkzaH, bAhumUlaM, BujakowaraH-raM, dormUlaM. [Arm]let, keyUraH-raM, aMgadaH-daM. 2 kzudrabAhuH, upaSAKA.

ARM (subs.): I Of the human body:(1) BujaH;(2) bAhuH;(3) dos; (m);(4) pravezwaH. A. The fore a. prakozWaH. The upper a. pragaRqaH.II any object analogous to an arm: (a) of a tree SAKA. v. Bough. (b) of a chair: *bAhuH. (c) of the sea or of a river:(1) vaNkaH;(2) vakram. (d) of the polypi: v. Feelers.III A weapon: v. Arms.IV A branch of the military service: aNgam. v. Power: q. v.

ARM (v. i.): I To take arms:(1) saMnahyati (nah, [Page038] c. 4) (=to accoutre), ordered the generals to a. senApatIn saMnahanArTamAdiSat, Ku. xv. 5.;(2) astraM gfhvAti (grah, c. 9);(3) sAyuDaH (DA, DaM) Bavati.II To prepare for war yudDAya sajjI- Bavati.
ARM (v. t.): (1) sannAhayati (c. of naha);(2) sAyuDaH (DA, DaM) karoti;(3) sajjIkaroti (=to equip).

ARM , s. (Of the body) bAhuH m. f., BujaH or -jA f., dozA f., doH m. (-s), pravezwaH. — (Of a tree) SAKA, upaSAKA. — (Of the sea) samudravaNkaH. — (Of a river) vakraM, vaNkaH, nadIvaNkaH, nadIvakraM, puwaBedaH. — (Power, might) balaM, SaktiH f.; ‘a dominion acquired by one's own arm,’ svaBujopArjjitaM rAjyaM. — (The upper arm) pragaRqaH.

To ARM , v. a. sannah (c. 4. -nahyati -nadDuM), sajjIkf, astrEH or SastrEH sajjIkf, or yuj in caus. (yojayati -yituM), or samAyuj. — (To arm one's self, put on one's arms) nah (c. 4. nahyate nadDuM), sannah. — (To put on armour) varmm (nom. varmmayati -yituM or saMvarmmayati).
ARM-HOLE , s. kakzaH, bAhumUlaM, BujakowaraH, kakzasTAnaM, dormUlaM.
ARM-PIT: kakzaH; v. Arm-hole.
ARM-PIT , s. kakzaH, bAhumUlaM, BujakowaraH, dormUlaM.
ARM-PIT , s. KaRqikaH. ARRACK, s. tAqiH -qI, tAlI.
Armada, s. bfhannOsADanaM.
ARMADA: potAvaliH. v. Fleet.
ARMADA , s. vfhannOkAsamUhaH, samudrayudDAya sajjIkfto vfhannOkAsamUhaH.
ARMADILLO: vileSayaH kzudrajantuviSezaH; *varmaDaraH.
ARMADILLO , s. GuRaH, kavacAkAracarmmaDArI vilavAsI kzudrajantuH.
Armament, s. balaM, sajjIkftaM balaM, yudDopakaraRAni.
ARMAMENT: I A body of forces equipped for war: balam: v. Army, fleet.II The guns and ammunitions of a man-of-war: yudDo- pakaraRAni (n. pl.) (?).
ARMAMENT , s. sEnikaH, yudDAya sajjIkftaM balaM, yodDfsajjanaM.
ARMED (adj.): (1) sAyuDaH (DA, DaM);(2) saMnadDaH (dDA, dDaM)(3) sajjaH (jjA, jjaM) (=equipped).

ARMED , p. p. sajjaH -jjA -jjaM, varmitaH -tA -taM, sannadDaH -dDA -dDaM, aBisannadDaH -dDA -dDaM, sAyuDaH -DA -DaM, kftAstraH -strA -straM, SastrI -striRI -stri (n). — (Having a weapon in the hand) SastrapARiH -RiH -Ri.
ARMHOLE: (1) kakzaH;(2) bAhumUlam;(3) BujakowaraH; (4) kakzAlayaH, Vi.
Armistice, s. yudDavirati f., saMDiH, yudDanivarttanaM (niyatakAlaM yAvat).
ARMISTICE: (1) ayudDam;(2) yudDaviratiH; and sim. comp. s. Ph. from filial affection, asked for two day's a. yayAce putravAtsalyAdayudDaM divasadvayam; Raj. v. Truce.
ARMISTICE , s. kiYcitkAlaparyyantaM yudDanivarttanaM, sanDiH m., kzamA.
ARMLESS: I Without an arm:(1) aBujaH (jA, jaM);(2) BujahInaH (nA, naM); etc.II Without weapons:(1) aSastraH (strA, straM);(2) anAyuDaH (DA, DaM); etc.
ARMLESS , a. (Without an arm) aBujaH -jA -jaM. — (Without weapons) astrahInaH -nA -naM, aSastraH -strA -straM.
ARMLET: valayaH v. Bracelet.
ARMLET , s. (Bracelet) valayaH or yaM, keyUraM, aNgadaM. — (A little arm) kzudrabAhuH m., upaSAKA.
Armorial, s. kAvacika, AyuDIya, AyuDika. 2 kulacinhasaMbaMDinkulacihnasaMbaMDin.
ARMORIAL , a. kAvacikaH -kI -kaM, AyuDikaH -kA -kaM, AyuDIyaH -yA -yaM. — (Belonging to the escutcheon of a family) kulacihnasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
ARMORY , s. AyuDAgAraM, SastrAgAraM, astrAgAraH. — (A collection of arms) SastrasaMhatiH f., SastrasamUhaM.

Armour, s. varman n., kavacaH-caM, kaMcukaH, sannAhaH, tanuvAraM, tanutraM-trARa. ‘a(rmour) for the head’ SirastrARaM. [Armour]er, s. SastrakAraH, astrakAraH. [Armour]y, s. AyuDAgAraM, SastragfhaM. 2 SastrasamUhaH.
ARMOUR: (1) varman (n).;(2) kavaca (mn.);(3) vArabARaH;(4) saMnAhaH;(5) kaYcukaH;(6) tanutram. Chain a. jAlikA (rare).

ARMOUR , s. varmma n. (n), lOhavarmma n. (n), tanutraM, tanutrARaM, kavacaH or -caM, vAravARaH, kaYcukaH, tvaktraM, daMSanaM, sannAhaH, dehAvaraRaM, yudDAstraM, tanuvAraM, sajjA. — (Chain-armour) jAlikA, jAlaprAyA; ‘arrayed in ar- mour,’ varmmitaH -tA -taM, kavacI -cinI -ci (n).
ARMOUR-BEARER , s. sAnnahAnakaH, varmmavAhakaH.
ARMOUR-BEARER , i broken, read sAnnahanikaH.
ARMOURER: SastrakAraH; Perh. asiDArakaH.
ARMOURER , s. astrakArakaH, SastrakAraH, SastramArjaH, astranirmmARaSilpajYaH, sajjAkarttA m. (rttf), asiDAvakaH.
ARMOURY: (1) AyuDAgAram;(2) Sastragfham.
ARMS: I Weapons:(1) Sastram;(2) astram; (3) AyuDaH;(4) hetiH;(5) praharaRam.II War, hostility: q. v.III Armorial bearings: *kulacihrAni (n. pl.).

ARMS , s. astraM, SastraM, AyuDaH, yudDAstraM, SastrAstraM. — (War in gene- ral) vigrahaH, samaraH, raRaH, yudDaM, saNgrAmaH. — (State of hostility) yudDAvasTA, raRasamayaH; ‘dexterity in arms,’ astralAGavaM; ‘the taking up of arms,’ astragrahaRaM, yudDe pravfttiH, astraDAraRaM; ‘pas- sage of arms,’ astraSikzA, SastrAByAsaH; ‘a brother in arms,’ sahayuDvA m. (n). — (The ensigns armorial of a family) kulI- napadasUcakacihnaM, kulacihnaM.
Army, s. senA, sEnyaM, balaM, vAhinI, camUH, anIkaM, pftanA, daMqaH-qaM; ‘full a(rmy)’ caturaMgaM balaM, akzOhiRI.

ARMY: (1) sEnyam;(2) balam;(3) daRqacakram;(4) patAkinI;(5) camUH;(6) vyUhaH (an a. in battle array);(7) caturaNgabalam (an a. comprising the four complements, elephants, cars, horse and foot). N. B. sEnyam and balam are also used in the plural in the ‘singular’ sense.
ARMY , s. senA f., sEnyaM, balaM, vAhinI, camUH f., daRqaH or -RqaM, anIkaM, cakraM, DvajinI, vyUhaH, yoDasamUhaH, pftanA, varUTinI. — (A complete army) akzOhiRI, caturaNgaH. — (In motion) pracakraM.
Aroma, s. gaMDaH, AmodaH, parimalaH. [Aroma]tic, a. suraBi, sugaMDi. 2 suraBita; ‘a(romatic)s’ sugaMDidravyARi. [Aroma]tize, v. t. vAs 10.
AROMA: (1) ganDaH;(2) sOraBam;(3) AmodaH.
AROMA , s. ganDaH, vAsaH, AmodaH, DUpaH, parimalaH.
AROMATIC: (1) suganDi (mfn.);(2) suganDaH (nDA, nDaM);(3) suraBi (mfn.): v. Fragrant.
AROMATIC , a. suganDIyaH -yA -yaM, ganDI -nDinI -nDi (n), tiktaH -ktA -ktaM, suraBitaH -tA -taM, suvAsitaH -tA -taM, DUpitaH -tA -taM.
AROMATICS , s. upaskarAH m. pl., suganDidravyARi n. pl., suganDAni n. pl.
To AROMATISE , v. a. vAs (c. 10. vAsayati -yituM), DUp (c. 1. DUpAyati, DUpituM).
Around, prep. paritaH, amitaH (with acc.). adv. samaMtataH, sarvataH, vizvak, samaMtAt.
AROUND (prep.): paritaH (with acc.), a. the altar vedIM paritaH, B. i. 12.
AROUND (adv.): (1) paritaH;(2) sarvataH, looking a. sarvato vilokya, U.;(3) samantataH, samantAt, K.; (4) vizvak, with sparks scattered all a. vizvagvi- sftasPuliNagaH, Ki. xvi. 51.
AROUND , adv. (Circularly) paritas, aBitas. — (On every side) samantatas, sarvvatas, viSvatas, samantAt.
AROUND , prep. pari, aBi.
Arouse, v. t. (From sleep) jAgf c., prabuD c. 2 ut-prot-sah c., uttij c., utTA c. (utTApayati); udbuD c., jan c. (janayati).

AROUSE: I From sleep: praboDayati: v. To awake.II From inaction(1) uttejayati (tij, c. 10), will go to the island of Mahendra to a. Jāmadagnya jAmadagnyamuttejayituM mahendradvIpameva gacCAvaH Vi. ii.;(2) utTApayati (c. of sTA), and a. ing his natural enemies utTApya sahajAMSca dvizaH D. iv.;(3) praboDayati (rare).

To AROUSE , v. a. (To excite) utsah in caus. (-sAhayati -yituM), protsah, utTA for utsTA in caus. (utTApayati -yituM), udbuD in caus. (-boDayati -yituM), prabuD. — (To wake from sleep) jAgf in caus. (jAgarayati -yituM), prabuD in caus., nidrAM BaYj (c. 7. Banakti BaMktuM).
AROUSED , p. p. protsAhitaH -tA -taM. — (Awaked) praboDitaH -tA -taM, prabudDaH -dDA -dDaM, nidrABaNgaH -NgA -NgaM.
To ARPROVE , v. a. anumud, aBiman. APPROVED, anumoditaH -tA -taM.
ARRACK: (1) tAlI;(2) tAqiH or tAqI.
ARRAIGN: amiyunakti or yojayati (yuj, c. 7 and 10): v. To accuse.

To ARRAIGN , v. a. (To set in order) virac (c. 10. -racayati -yituM), svasTAne sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM). — (To accuse) aBiyogaM kf, Ahve (c. 1. -hvayati -hvAtuM), apavad (c. 1. -vadati -vadituM), aBiSap (c. 1. -Sapati -SaptuM).
ARRAIGNED , p. p. aBiyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, AhUtaH -tA -taM, aBiSaptaH -ptA -ptaM.
ARRAIGNMENT: aBiyogaH: v. Accusation.
ARRAIGNMENT , s. aBiyogaH, AhvAnaM, apavAdaH.

sanskrit.slp1: tasya fRaM kaTaM pratideyamiti mayA nirRItaM-AlocitaM
sanskrit.word: तस्य ऋणं कथं प्रतिदेयमिति मया निर्णीतं-आलोचितं
sanskrit.iast: tasya ṛṇaṃ kathaṃ pratideyamiti mayā nirṇītaṃ-ālocitaṃ

details.body: Arrange, v. t. rac 10, Gaw c., vi-Uh 1 U; saM-viDA 3 U, vini-as 4 U, sTA c. (sTApayati); ‘well a(rrang)ed’ suGawita; ‘a(rrange) in order’ yaTAkramaM rac, saMviDA c. &c. 2 (Settle) upakxp c., nirRI 1 P; ‘I have a(rrang)ed to pay his debts’ tasya fRaM kaTaM pratideyamiti mayA nirRItaM-AlocitaM. [Arrange]ment, s. racanA, vinyAsaH, saMviDA, vyUhanaM, krameRa sTApanaM, paripAwi-wI f., kramaH; ‘a(rrangement) of plot’ vasturacanA, saMviDAnakaM; saraRi-RI f. 2 nirRayaH; ‘all a(rrangement)s for his reception are complete’ sarvAstatsaMBAvanAsaMviDA upakalpitAH.

ARRANGE: I To put in order:(1) racayati, vi-, (rac, c. 1), a. ing the division of the forest vira- cayya kAnanaviBAgam, Ki. xii. 44.;(2) vinyasyati (as, c. 4), merely by a. ing sentences padavinyAsa- mAtreRa;(3) yaTAkramaM sTApayati (c. of sTA).II To adjust, settle, determine: q. v.
To ARRANGE , v. a. rac (c. 10. racayati -yituM), virac; viDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), saMviDA; krameRa or yaTAkramaM sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM), granT (c. 1. granTati, c. 9. graTnAti, granTituM).
ARRANGED , p. p. viracitaH -tA -taM, graTitaH -tA -taM, vinyastaH -stA -staM, vihitaH -tA -taM, prativihitaH -tA -taM, parimitaH -tA -taM, vyUQaH -QA -QaM; ‘well-arranged,’ suYcawitaH -tA -taM.
ARRANGEMENT: I Orderly disposition:(1) racanA;(2) vinyAsaH;(3) saMviDAnam.II Settle- -ment, adjustment, agreement: q. v.

ARRANGEMENT , s. vinyAsaH, paryyAyaH, prativiDAnaM, vyUhanaM, vyUQiH f., racanA, viracanaM, granTanaM, -nA, vyavasTApanaM, anusanDAnaM, krameRa sTApanaM, paripAwiH f. — (The state of being in order) kramaH.
ARRANGER , s. viracakaH, upAyajYaH, upetA m. (tf), vyAsaH.
Arrant, a. atyaMta, BfSa, ati pr. 2 atiniMdya, atiduzwa, nikfzwa.
ARRANT: pAmaraH (rI, raM): v. Infamous, vile.
ARRANT , a. (Bad in a high degree) atiduzwaH -zwA -zwaM, atinikfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, atikutsitaH -tA -taM. — (Excessive) atyantaH -ntA -ntaM.
ARRAS , s. nAnAvarRAni citritavastrARi.

Array, s. vyUhaH, racanaM, vinyAsaH, kramaH, SroRi-RI f., paMkti f. 2 vezaH, ABaraRaM, paricCadaH. v. t. krameRa rac 10, sajjIkf 8 U. 2 BUz 10, alaMkf; vastreRa AcCad 10; ‘he was richly a(rray)ed’ sa mahArGavastraBUzitaH, -vastrARi paryaDatta.
ARRAY (subs.): I Battle-array: q. v.II Arrangement, order: q. v.III Dress, clothing: q. v.: paricCadaH.IV Of jurymen *nyAyapratiBUgaRaH.
ARRAY (v. t.): I To arrange, draw up: q. v. racayati, vi-, (rac, c. 10).II To dress, deck: q. v. BUzayati.III To select jurymen *nyAya- pratiBuvo nirUpayati (rUp, c. 10).

ARRAY , s. (Of battle) vyUhaH, or -hanaM, vyUQiH f., balavinyAsaH; ‘to draw up in battle array,’ vyUh (c. 1. -Uhate -UhituM). — (Order) kramaH, SreRI, paNktiH f., racanA. — (Dress) ABaraRaM, BUpaRaM, paricCadaH.

To ARRAY , v. a. (To put in order) krameRa or vyUhena rac (c. 10. racayati -yituM), virac or sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM), or vyavasTA; or viDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), or sajjIkf. — (To dress) vastram ACad (c. 10. -CAdayati -yituM), saMvye (c. 1. -vyayati -vyAtuM), BUz (c. 10. BUzayati -yituM); alaNkf, parizkf.

ARRAY , s. (Of an army) senAracanA. The following are dif- ferent forms of array; ‘In a circle,’ maRqalavyUhaH, cakravyUhaH; ‘in a square,’ sarvatoBadraH; ‘in line,’ daRqavyUhaH; ‘in column,’ BogavyUhaH; ‘in mixed order,’ asaMhatavyUhaH; ‘like a wain,’ SakawavyUhaH; ‘like a shark or crocodile,’ makaravyUhaH; ‘like a banner,’ patAkAvyUhaH; ‘like a shoulder,’ skanDaH.
To ARRAY , v. a. vyUh (c. 1. -Uhate -hituM), prativiDAnaM kf.

Arrear, s. avaSizwadeyaM, fRaSezaM, aSoDito BAgaH; ‘clear up all a(rrear)s’ sarvamavaSizwadeyaM pariSoDayaH kAryapariSezaM samApayaH ‘his pay remained in a(rrear)s’ yaTAvasaramadattatvAttasya vetanaM samuccitaM.
ARREAR, ARREARS: *avaSizwadeyam, pay up your a. s *avaSizwadeyaM pariSoDaya; I owe large a. s *mayA bahu pariSoDanIyam; a. of rent *karaSezaH.
ARREAR , s. fRaSezaM, fRaSezAMSaH, fRasya aSoDito BAgaH, fRasya SoDanIyo BAgaH.

Arrest, v. t. niruD 7 U, grah 9 P, AsiD 1 P, baMD 9 P, Df 1 P, 10; fRahetoH rAjAjYayA Df 10. 2 nivft c., staMB 9 P or c. (nivartayAmAsa nfpasya dfzwiM) (R. ii. 28); ‘the Chitrakuta mountain a(rrest)s my eye’ baDnAti me cakzuScitrakUwaH (R. xiii. 47); ‘a(rrest) attention’ ananyamanas a. kf 8 U, ananyacitta a. kf. s. niroDaH, AseDaH, grahaRaM, DaraRaM, baMDanaM.

ARREST (v. t.): I To obstruct, stop: q. v.: [Page039] rURadDi (ruD, c. 7).II To apprehend legally: (1) AseDati (siDa, c. 1);(2) Darati or DArayati (Df, c. 1 and 10):(3) gfhvAti (grah, c. 9). III To fix, engage: Ph. (it) a. s my eyes baDnAti me cakzuH; R.; it a. s my attention mAmananya- manaskaM karoti.
ARREST (subs.): (1) AseDaH;(2) DftiH (?). Ph. a. of judgment *nirRayaroDaH.
ARREST , s. AseDaH, DaraRaM, grahaRaM, niroDaH, banDanaM. — (Stop) nivAraRaM.

To ARREST , v. a. (As a bailiff) AsiD (c. 1. -seDati -sedDuM), niruD (c. 7. -ruRadDi -rodDuM), fRahetoH or dozahetoH rAjaleKena or rAjAjYayA banD (c. 9. baGnAti -bandDuM), or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or Df (c. 1. Darati, DarttuM). — (Stop, bring to a stand) stamB in caus. (stamBayati -yituM), vizwamB (c. 5. -staBnoti, c. 9. -staBnAti -stamBituM), nivf in caus. (-vAra- yati -yituM).
ARREST , s. (Stop) stamBaH -mBanaM, gatistamBaH, gatiroDaH.
ARRESTED , p. p. AsidDaH -dDA -dDaM, DftaH -tA -taM, badDaH -dDA -dDaM, nirudDaH -dDA -dDaM.
ARRIVAL: (1) Agamanam;(2) AgamaH;(3) upayA- nam (rare), Ku. vii. 22.
ARRIVAL , s. AgamanaM, aBigamanaM, upasTitiH f., upayAtaM, AyaH.
Arrive, v. i. pra-saMpra-anupra-Ap 5 P, A-samA-sad 1 P, aBi-upA-gam 1 P, upasTA 1 U, prapad 4 A (yOvanadaSAM prapede). [Arriv]al, s. AgamanaM, upasTiti f. &c.

ARRIVE (v. i.): (1) pra-Apnoti, ava-, sampra-, anupra-, (Ap, c. 5), a. d at the hermitage af the saint maharzeH prApadASramam; R. i. 48.;(2) A-sIdati, samA-, (sad, c. 1), Kusha a. ing at the banks of the Sarayū kUlaM samAsAdya kuSaH sarayvAH, R. xvi. 35.; (3) pra-padyate (pad, c. 4), a. ed at the hermitage of Atri atrestapovanaM prapede, B. iv. 19.; after child- hood, she a. ed at youth bAlyAt paraM sATa vayaH prapede, Ku. i. 31. N. B. Observe that all these verbs take an acc. Ph.: a. ed at no conclu- sion nirRayaM nAsasAda; the news a. ed of the ass- assination of his father pitfvaDavArtA samAgatA.

To ARRIVE , v. n. Agam (c. 1. -gacCati -gantuM), aBigam, upagam; upasTA (c. 1. -tizWati -sTAtuM), prAp (c. 5. -Apnoti -AptuM), samprAp, avAp, anusamprAp, upasamprAp, AyA (c. 2. -yAti -yAtuM), aBiyA, upAyA, samAyA.
ARRIVED , p. p. AgataH -tA -taM, samAyAtaH -tA -taM, upasTitaH -tA -taM, prAptaH -ptA -ptaM.

Arrogance, s. OdDatyaM, darpaH, aBimAnaH, ahaMkAraH, garvaH, madaH, avalepaH, prAgalByaM, utsekaH, AwopaH. Arrogant, a. udData, dfpta, ahaMkArayukta, pragalBa, samada, garvita, avalipta. utsikta, mAnin; ‘a(rrogant) lady’ mAninI, pramadA. [Arrogant]ly, adv. udDataM, sAvalepaM, sadarpaM &c.
ARROGANCE: (1) OdDatyam;(2) prAgalByam;(3) utsekaH;(4) avalepaH.
ARROGANCE , s. garvaH, DarzaH, darpaH, mAnaH, aBimAnaH, madaH, avalepaH, aha- NkAraH, prAgalByaM, pragalBatA, AwopaH, cittasamunnatiH, OdDatyaM, pratiBAnaM.
ARROGANT: (1) udDataH (tA, taM);(2) pragalBaH (lBA, lBaM);(3) utsiktaH (ktA, ktaM);(4) ava- liptaH (ptA, ptaM).

ARROGANT , a. pragalBaH -lBA -lBaM, garvvI -rvviRI -rvvi (n), atigarvvitaH -tA -taM, sagarvvaH -rvvA -rvvaM, mAnI -ninI -ni (n), madodDataH -tA -taM, aha- NkArI -riRI -ri (n), AtmaSlAGI -GinI -Gi (n), praDarzitaH -tA -taM, avaliptaH -ptA -ptaM, udDataH -tA -taM, pratiBAmuKaH -KI -KaM. — (To be ar- rogant) pragalB (c. 1. -galBate -galBituM), dfp (c. 4. dfpyati, darptuM draptuM).
ARROGANTLY: (1) udDatam;(2) pragalBam;(3) sAva- lepam.
ARROGANTLY , adv. sagarvvaM, sadarpaM, sAwopaM, garvveRa, DarzeRa, pragalBaM.
Arrogate, v. t. sagarvaM-anyAyena-grah 9 P or svAyattIkf 8 U or AdA 3 A. [Arrogat]ion, s. anyAyagrahaRaM upaDA.
ARROGATE: *anyAyataH gfhRAti (grah, c. 9) or svIkaroti (kf, c. 8), anyAyena svasvatvaM KyApayati (c. of KyA) or prakawayati (nomi.).

To ARROGATE , v. a. (To claim proudly) garvvapUrvvakaM or sagarvvaM or anarhatas or aDarmmatas or miTyA grah (c. 9. gfhlAti grahItuM), aBigrah, parigrah; or laB (c. 1. laBate labDuM), or AdA (c. 3. -dadAti -dAtuM), or aByanujYA (c. 9. -jAnAti -jYAtuM), or AtmIyaM -yAM -yaM kf or svIkf; mfzA or miTyA grah; upaDAM kf, DvajIkf.
ARROGATION: *nyAyyagrahaRam; anyAyyasvIkAraH; anyAyena svasvatvaKyApanam.
ARROGATION , s. sagarvvagrahaRaM, anarhagrahaRaM, aBigrahaRaM, anyAyyagrahaRaM, mi- TyAgrahaRaM, DvajIkaraRaM, upaDA.
Arrow, s. SaraH, bARaH, sAyakaH, izuH, kAMqaM, BallaH, nArAcaH, mArgaRaH, SilImuKaH, viSiKaH. [Arrow]y, a. bARavat &c.; bARAkAra.

ARROW: (1) SaraH;(2) bARaH;(3) izuH;(4) sAyakaH or SAyakaH;(5) mArgaRaH;(6) SilImuKaH; (7) ASugaH;(8) patrI;(9) pfzatkaH;(10) viSiKaH A shower of a. s SaravarzaH. To discharge, shoot a. s SaraM nirasyati (as, c. 4), kzipati (kzip, c. 6), Ki.

ARROW , s. SaraH, vARaH, izuH m., SAyakaH, kARqa, Salya, vipAwaH, viSiKaH, pfzatkaH, patrI m. (n), BallaH, nArAcaH, prakzveqanaH, ajihmagaH, KagaH, ASugaH, mArgaRaH, kalambaH, ropaH; ‘arrow-head,’ vARAgra ‘arrow-shaft,’ SarakARqaM; ‘a shower of arrows,’ SarAkzepaH, SaravarzaM.
ARROW-HEAD: (1) Palam,(2) Salyam;(3) bARAgram.
ARROW-HEADED: *PalAkAraH (rA, raM), a. characters, *PalAkArAvarRAH.
ARROW-ROOT: KAdyopayogI dravyaviSezaH.
ARROWY: I Of arrows: Sara- (in comp.) a. shower SaravarzaH.II Crooked like an arrow: kuwilaH (lA, laM): v. Crooked.
ARROWY , a. (Consisting of arrows) vARI -RinI -Ri (n), vARavAn [Page026-a+ 51] -vatI -vat (t). — (Arrow-shaped) vARAkAraH -rA -raM.
Arsenal, s. AyuDAgAraM, SastragfhaM. 2 SastrAstrasamUhaH.
ARSENAL: (1) AyuDAgAram;(2) Sastragfham.
ARSENAL , s. AyuDAgAraM, AyuDagfhaM, SastrAgAraM, astrAgAraM, yudDaBARqAgAraM. — (A collection of arms) SastrasaMhatiH, SastrasamUhaM.
Arsenic, s. PenASman m.; manaHSilA.
ARSENIC: manaHSilA (=red a.).
ARSENIC , s. manaHSilA, SilA, manoguptA, nAgajihvikA, nEpAlI, kunawI.
Arson, s. gfhadahanAparADaH.
ARSON: (1) AgAradAhaH;(2) gfhadAhaH.
ARSON , s. AgAradAhaH, gfhadAhAparADaH.

Art, s. SilpaM, SilpavidyA, kalA, vyavasAyaH, nAwyakalA ‘a(rt) of dancing’. 2 kalpanA, vidyA (science). 3 nipuRatA, yukti f., kOSalaM; sADanaM; ‘a(rt)s of line’ jIvanasADanAni. 4 vyAjaH, kapawa, mAyA, vEdagDyaM, cAturyaM. [Art]ful, a. catura; mAyAvin, ‘a(rtful) look’ caturo dfzwikzepaH; vidagDa, mAyAvat. 2 Silpena kfta. 3 nipuRa, kuSala. [Art]fulness, s. cAturyaM, vEdagDyaM, &c. [Art]less, a. fju, amAya, akftaka, akftrima, avyAja; ‘a(rtless)ly lovely body’ avyAjamanoharaM vapuH (S. 1). [Art]lessness, s. saralatA, amAyitA, akftakatA, ArjavaM. Artifice, s. upAyaH, CalaM, Cadman n., vyapadeSaH, kapawaM, vyAjaH. Artificer, s. Silpin m., karma-Silpa-kAraH. 2 kartf m., nirmAtf m. Artificial, a. kftrima, kftaka; savyAja. 2 Silpanirmita; ‘a(rtificial) mountain’ krIqAparvataH. Artizan, Artist, s. Silpin m., citrakaraH. 2 paMqita; nipuRaH.

ART: I As opposed to nature: Silpam.II As opposed to science: kalA, in the a. s of dancing, singing, playing, and acting nftyagIta- vAdyanAwyakalAsu, D. ii. Ph. the industrial a. s SilpavidyA; the fine a. s saNgItAdi-kalA (?) or *SrezWakalAH (f. pl.).III Skill, dexterity: q. v.: kOSalam.IV Cunning, artifice: q. v. Calam.

ART , s. SilpaM, SilpavidyA, kalA, vyavasAyaH, karmma n. (n). — (Inven- tion) kalpanaM, -nA. — (Science) vidyA. — (Skill) nipuRatA, pARqityaM, dakzatA, yuktiH f., SikzASaktiH f. — (Cunning) vidagDatA, vEdagDyaM, mAyA.
ARTERIAL , a. nAqIsambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), raktavAhI -hinI -hi (n).
Artery, s. DamanI, raktavAhinI.
ARTERY: (1) raktavAhinI nAqiH;(2) raktavahA SirA.
ARTERY , s. nAqI, nAqiH f., kaRqarA, mAlI, nAliH f., sirA, raktavAhI m. (n).
ARTFUL: caturaH (rA, raM), Ku. iv. 20.: v. Cunn- -ing, crafty.

ARTFUL , a. (Performed with art) Silpena or pARqitpena kftaH -tA -taM. — (Skilful) SikzitaH -tA -taM, nipuRaH -RA -RaM, pawuH -wuH -wvI -wu. — (Cunning) upAyajYaH -jYA -jYaM, vidagDaH -gDA -gDaM, CalAnvitaH -tA -taM, mAyI -yinI -yi (n).
ARTFULLY: (1) nipuRam;(2) kOSalena. v. Cunn- -ingly, ingeniously, craftily.
ARTFULLY , adv. pARqityena, nEpuRyena, sapAwavaM, vEdagDyena, Calena.
ARTFULNESS: (1) cAturyam;(2) cAturI: v. Cunning, ingenuity.
ARTFULNESS , s. (Skill) pARqityaM, nipuRatA, cAturyyaM, dakzatA, pawutA. — (Cunning) vidagDatA, vEdagDyaM, SaWatA.
ARTHRITIC , a. (Gouty) vAtakI -kinI -ki (n). — (Relating to the joints) granTilaH -lA -laM.
ARTICHOKE: SAkaviSezaH.
ARTICHOKE , s. SAkaviSezaH.
Article, s. dravyaM, vastu n., sAmagrI. 2 vizayaH, padaM, BAgaH. 3 samayaH, samayapatraM. 4 vfttapatraleKaH.

ARTICLE (subs.): I A part of speech: viSezyasvaBAvanirUpakAvyayaSabdaH.II A commodity or substance: q. v. dravyam.III A Clause in a contract etc.: prakaraRam (?). Ph. we enter into this a. to remove this doubt etAmASaNkAM nivartayitumidamaDikaraRamAraByate, S. iii. 34.; the a. about Harisha Chandra was very good, *harISacandra- vizayakaH prabanDo'tyuttama AsIt; the a. s of war *sEnikaniyamAvaliH.IV A distinct part: (1) aMSaH (=part);(2) vizayaH (= subject). V. Moment:(1) kzaRaH;(2) samayaH.
ARTICLE (v. t.): *niyamapatreRa baDnAti (baDn, c. 9.), an a. d clerk *niyamabadDaH leKakaH.

ARTICLE , s. (Part of speech) vAkyArTanirRAyako'vyayaSabdaH. — (A particular part of any complex thing) aMSaH, BAgaH, padaM, vizayaH. — (Thing) dravyaM, vastu n., vizayaH. — (Apparatus) sAmagrI f. — (Terms, stipulation) niyamapatraM, samayaH; ‘articles of peace,’ sanDisamayaH. — (A point of time) kzaRaH, samayaH, velA.
To ARTICLE , v. n. samayaM kf, niyamapatreRa sTirIkf, saNGaww (c. 1. -Gawwate -GawwituM).
ARTICLE , s. (Item) prakaraRaM. — (Condition) saNketaH.
ARTICULAR: sanDigataH (tA, taM), a. disease sanDigata- rogaH, Sr.
ARTICULAR , a. granTilaH -lA -laM, granTisambanDakaH -kA -kaM.

Articulate, a. spazwa, parisPuwa, vyakta. v. t. spazwaM-sPuwaM-uccar c. or udIr 10. 2 graMT 9 P, saMyuj 10, saMDA 3 U. [Articulate]ness, s. spazwatA, sPuwatA; ‘a(rticulateness) in uttering syllables’ varRoccAraRe spazwatA ‘utters articulate sounds’ parisPuwAkzarAM giramudIrayati (Ka. 13). [Articulat]ion, s. uccAraRaM &c. 2 saMDAnaM.
ARTICULATE (adj.): (1) spazwaH (zwA, zwaM);(2) sPuwaH (wA, waM): v. Distinct.
ARTICULATE (v. t.) I To utter distinctly: [Page040] sPuwaM or spazwam uccArayati (c. of car), udIrayati (Ir, c. 10.), etc.II To joint: saMdaDAti (DA, c. 3.).
ARTICULATE , a. (Distinct) vyaktaH -ktA -ktaM, spazwaH -zwA -zwaM.

To ARTICULATE , v. a. (To utter words distinctly) spazwaM or vyaktaM uccar in caus. (-cArayati -yituM), or udIr (c. 10. -Irayati -yituM, c. 1. -Irati -IrituM), or udAhf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM). — (To joint) granT (c. 1. granTati, c. 9. graTnAti granTituM).
ARTICULATED , p. p. (Uttered) uccAritaH -tA -taM. — (Jointed) granTitaH -tA -taM, sanDitaH -tA -taM.
ARTICULATION: I Of words: Ph. distinct a. spazwatA varRoccAraRe K.II Of bones: sanDiH: v. Joint.
ARTICULATION , s. (Of words) uccAraRaM, udAharaRaM. — (The juncture of bones) granTiH m., asTisanDisTAnaM, sanDiH m.
ARTIFICE: (1) upAyaH:(2) CalaM;(3) upADiH, women are originators of all a. s striyaScopADInA- mudBavakzetram, D. N. B.(2) and(3) always in the bad sense: v. Stratagem.
ARTIFICE , s. (Stratagem, contrivance) upAyaH, Cadma n. (n), CalaM, vyapadeSaH, kapawaH -waM, kOSalaM.
ARTIFICER: I An artisan: q. v. SilpI.II A maker, contriver: q. v.: kartA.
ARTIFICER , s. (An artist) SilpakAraH, SilpI m. (n), karmmakAraH, karmmAraH, kAruH m. — (Maker) karttA m. (rttf), nirmmAtA m. (tf). — . (Contriver) upetA m. (tf), upAyajYaH.

ARTIFICIAL: I Made by art: kftrimaH (mA, maM), herds of a. young elephants kftrimakarikalaBayUTAni, K. Ph. sometimes over a. hills kadAcit krIqAparvatezu, K. a. lake kelipalvalam, N. ; a. clouds mAyAmeGamAlAH, K.II. Feigned, fictitious: q. v.: kftrimaH (mA, maM).III Ingenious. skilful: q. v.

ARTIFICIAL , a. SilpikaH -kI -kaM, kftrimaH -mA -maM, kftakaH -kA -kaM, kAlpa- nikaH -kI -kaM, pratiyatnapUrvvaH -rvvA -rvvaM. — (Made by art) kalpitaH -tA -taM, SilpanirmmitaH -tA -taM; ‘an artificial lake,’ krIqAsaraH n. (s).
ARTIFICIALLY , adv. Silpena, kftrimaprakAreRa, SilpikaprakAreRa.
Artillery, s. agnyastrARi; yudDAstrARi.

ARTILLERY: I Weapons in general: astrARi (n. pl.).II Cannon with all that apper- -tains to them: *kAmAnAni or (when the meaning is not clear) sopakaraRakAmAnAni (n. pl.).III The troops who manage can- -non etc.: *kAmAnabalam.
ARTILLERY , s. agnyastraM, yudDAstraM, AgneyAni astrARi n. pl.
ARTISAN: (1) Silpin (m.);(2) SilpakAraH;(3) kAruH or kArukaH;(4) karmakAraH. The workshop of an a. SilpaSAlA or SilpiSAlA. The business of an a. Silpakarman (n.).
ARTISAN , s. SilpI m. (n), SilpakAraH, karmmakAraH, kArukaH.
ARTIST: I An artisan: q. v.II A painter: q. v. citrakaraH.
ARTIST , s. SilpI m. (n). — (A skilful man) paRqitaH, nipuRaH, pawuH. — (Painter) citrakaraH.
ARTISTIC: vicitraH (trA, traM) (?): v. Ingenious.
ARTLESS: I Simple, frank, guileless: q. v.; (1) amAyaH (yA, yaM);(2) fju (mfn.).II Contrived without art:(1) nIrasaH (sA, saM) (=devoid of taste);(2) alaNkArahInaH (nA, naM) (=unadorned).

ARTLESS , a. (Without fraud) amAyaH -yA -yaM, amAyikaH -kI -kaM, kapawahInaH -nA -naM, dakziRaH -RA -RaM, saralaH -lA -laM, SudDamatiH -tiH [Page026-b+ 51] ti, CalarahitaH -tA -taM, nirvyAjaH -jA -jaM. — (Void of art) apawuH -wuH -wu, adakzaH -kzA -kzaM, anaBijYaH -jYA -jYaM.
ARTLESSLY: i. e. Simply, frankly: q. v.: (1) mAyAM vinA;(2) akapawena;(3) Arjavena.
ARTLESSLY , adv. CalavyatirekeRa, mAyAM vinA, kapawavyatirekeRa, amAyayA, dAkziRyena.
ARTLESSNESS: (1) amAyitA;(2) saralatA;(3) Arjavam: v. Simplicity.
ARTLESSNESS , s. amAyA, saralatA, dAkziRyaM.
ARUNDINEOUS , a. vetrakaH -kI -kaM, vetrakIyaH -yA -yaM, naqakIyaH -yA -yaM, vetasvAn -svatI -svat (t), vetravAn -vatI -vat (t).

As, conj., adv. Ex. by vat, iva; mAtfvat-mAtaramiva-paradArAn paSya. 2 yaTA, yadvat, anurUpaM-peRa; yaTA in comp. (yaToktaM kaTaya); ‘as-so’ yaTA-taTA with or without eva ‘as-as’ yaTEva-taTEva (yaTEva SAMtA taTEva sItA daSaraTasya priyA) (U. 4). ‘as since-therefore’ taTA-taTA, yataH-tataH, yat-tat; ‘as for instance’, yaTA (yaTA mahAnase), or taTAhi. 2 (On account of) ex. by abl. or instr. of noun. 3 (While) yAvat-tAvat; or by pres. part.; ‘as he was going, he thought’ gacCan sa itTaM manasi cakAra; ‘as high as’ daGna (GnI f.), mAtra, in comp.; ‘water as high as the knee’ jAnudaGnaM jalaM; UrumAtrA BittiH &c.; ‘as soon as’ yAvat-tAvat; or loc. abs. constr. with mAtra or eva; ‘as he had spoken’ uktavatyeva tasmin; ‘as before’, yaTApurA, yaTApUrvaM, pUrvavat; ‘as far as’ yAvat with acc., A with abl. or in comp. (AsamudrakzitISAnAM) ‘as if’, ‘as it were’ iva; oft. by man 4 A; ‘as if the city had been a large tank’ nagaraM mahAkAsAraM manyamAnaH; ‘as follows’ iti (iti vaktaM pracakrame), or ex. by yaTA-yat at the beginning of narratives; ‘it is as follows’ tadyaTA; ‘as to’, ‘as for’ tu, tAvat, iti, aDikftya, uddiSya; ‘as for ments, he has none’ guRAstAvattasya nEva vidyate; ‘as for doing it quickly it is easy’ SIGramiti sukaraM (niBftamiti tu ciMtanIyaM S. 3), ‘as well as’ ca-ca; ‘as many as’ ‘as much as’ yAvat-tAvat; ‘as yet’ adyApi, adya yAvat. 4 (Connecting words in apposition) ex. by iti; sa baMDuriti mataH, baMDurmataH ‘as a father he respects me’ piteti mAM sa mAnayati.

AS: I As a particle of comparison:(1) vat affixed, (he who looks on) other's wives as mothers, on other's things as clods mAtfvat paradArezu paradravyezu lozwravat, H. i.; as before pUrvavat;(2) yaTA (either in comp. to expr. sim. comparison, or with taTA or evaM to expr. as......so...... also to introduce illustrations): as ordered yaTAnideSaM; as prescribed yaTAviDi; as before yaTApurA, Sa. vi.; as eating is inferred from nourishment or country from its language, so is knowable inferred from knowledge, yaTA puzwayA BojanamanumIyate yaTA ca BAzayA deSaH taTA jYAnAkAreRa jYeyamanumeyam. D. s. (see also R. iii. 23 and notice the repetition of yaTA in such cases); as animals attempt to fly away when they see men with sticks, so.... yaTA paSvAdayaH daRqodyatakaraM purUzamaBimuKamupalaBya palAyitumAraBante evaM.. S. i. p.; as for instance, fire is inferred from smoke yaTA DUmenAgniriti, N. d. As for instance: sometimes expr. by taTAhiH he, as a rule, enjoyed the pleasures of youth as for instance, sometimes roamed over artificial mountains, sometimes walked through summer houses sa prAyaSo yOvanasuKamanubaBUva, taTAhi kadAcit krIqAparvatezu vicacAra kadAcillatAgfhezu baBrAma, K.II. While: expr. by the pres. part: as he went, he thought vrajaMSca samarTayAmAsa, K. III. Since, in as much as: q. v.:(1) by the abl. and when the subs. ends in tA or A by the ins.: as the motion of the vessels (at sea) depends on wind vAtADInapotagamanatvAt, K. b.; as there was much political work rAjakAryasya bahulatayA Sa. vi.;(2) yataH...tataH.. Miscell: as long as one lives yAvajjIvaM; as far as the ocean A samudrAt; as high as the knee jAnudaGnaH (GnA, GnaM); as yet adyApi. N. B. as, when it connects two subs. s in apposition is expr. by BUtvA or kftvA: I will remain as your queen tava mahizI BUtvA tizWAmi; sent me to you as his agent mAM pratiniDiM kftvA tvatsakASaM prerayAmAsa.

AS , conj. (In the same manner with something else) yaTA. — (Like) iva; vat affixed; ‘to act as a fool,’ mUrKavat kf. — (In the manner that) yaTA, yadvat, yatprakAreRa, rUpeRa; ‘they did as he commanded,’ tasya yaTAnideSaM cakruH. — (According as) anu- rUpeRa, anusAreRa. — (So as) yaTA taTA. — (While, at the same time) yAvat, yatsamaye, yatkAle. — (Because that) yatas. — (As many as, as much as) yAvAn -vatI -vat (t), yAvatsaMKyakaH -kA -kaM or yatsaMKyakaH, yati ind. — (As long as, as far as) yAvat, A prefixed with the abl. c.; as, ‘as far as the ocean,’ AsamudrAt; ‘as long as the vow lasted,’ AsamApanAd vratasya. — Sometimes paryyantaM or anta are affixed with the sense, ‘as far as;’ as, ‘the land as far as the ocean,’ sAgaraparyyantaM pfTivI, or sAgarAntA pfTivI. — (As soon as) yadA; mAtrAt affixed; ‘as soon as he had spoken,’ kaTanamAtrAt. — (As well as) yaTA. — (As yet) adya yAvat, adyaparyyantaM, adyApi, etat kAlaM yAvat. — (As how) yaTA. — (Equally with) tulyarUpeRa, samaM. — (As if, as though) iva, prAyas. — (As to, with reference to) prati, pratIkzya, uddiSya. — (As high as) daGnaM, mAtraM; as, ‘water as high as the knees,’ jAnudaGnaM jalaM.
AS BEING: Expr. By the ins. of subs. s in tA or by the abl. in other cases: a. few alpatayA; a. a child bAlatayA; a. weak dOrbalyAt; a. wonder- ful adButatvAt.

AS FOLLOWS: iti (at the end of the quota- -tion, which is placed first in Sanskrit). see R. iii. 47., Ku. iv. 43. Ph.: began to speak as follows vaktumitTamupacakrame vacaH, K. xiii. 36.; Bachaspati spoke a. vAcaspatiravAcedaM, Ku. ii. 30.
AS FOR, AS TO: vizayaH (yA, yaM) or vizayakaH (kA, kaM) in comp.: as for his valour, I will not say a word tasya SOryavizayaM na kiYcid vadAmi.

AS IF: iva (always after the word it governs): passed the night as if in a moment kzaRAdiva kzaRadAM [Page041] kzapitavatI, K.; as if painted, as if engraved, as if paralyzed liKitamivotkIrRamiva stamBitamiva, K.; as if from hell to heaven narakAdiva svargam, D.

sanskrit.slp1: jAtamAtraM na yaH SatruM rogaM ca
sanskrit.word: जातमात्रं न यः शत्रुं रोगं च
sanskrit.iast: jātamātraṃ na yaḥ śatruṃ rogaṃ ca

details.body: AS SOON AS: (1) by a comp. adj. with mAtraH (trA, traM), he who does not put down an enemy or a disease a. it appears jAtamAtraM na yaH SatruM rogaM ca praSamaM nayet, P. i. 8.;(2) yadA...tadEva. Ph.: a. I spoke madvacanAntarameva, K.
AS WELL AS: ca......caH anointed with nectar a. poison digDo'mftena ca vizeRa ca, Ma. i.; as a mother a. as a father mAtA ca pitA ca BUtvA D. v.
Asafœtida, s. hiMgu n., jatukaM, bAhlIkaM, rAmaWaM, sahasraveDi n.
ASAFŒTIDA: (1) hiNgu (n.);(2) jatukam, A.; (3) vAhlIkam, A.
ASCARIDES: A disease: kfmirogaH.

Ascend, v. i. udi 2 P, udam 1 P. v. t. A-aDi-ruh 1 P, A-aDi-kram 1 U, 4 P, (with acc.); ‘a(scend)ed the throne’ rAjapadamavApa, siMhAsanamAruroha. [Ascend]ant, a. aDirohin, 2 praDAna, prabala, uttama. s. uccatA, ucCrAyaH. 2 prADAnyaM, prAbalyaM, praButvaM; ‘his stars are in the a(scendant)’ tasya janmagrahAH uccasaMSrayAH. [Ascend]ancy, s. praButvaM, prADAnyaM, prAbalyaM. Ascent, s. ArohaRaM, udgamaH, udayaH, samutTAnaM, aDirohaRaM. 2 aDirohaRamArgaH, sopAnaM; ‘difficult of a(scent)’ durAroha.
ASCEND (v. i.): Arohati (with acc.): v. To mount, rise.
ASCEND (v. t.): A-rohati, aDi-, (ruha, c. 1.): v. To mount.

The astronomical divisions of time called Karaṇa karaRa are eleven in number: some of them are, kOlavaH, tEtilaH, baRik, BadrI or vizwiH f., SakuniH f., caturaNGriH, nAgaH, kintuGnaH &c. The divisions called Yoga yoga are twenty-seven in number, viz. vizkamBaH, prItiH, AyuzmAn, sOBAgyaM, SoBanaH, atigaRqaH, sukarmmA, DftiH, SUlaH, gaRqaH, vfdDiH, GruvaH, vyAGAtaH, harzaRaH, vajraH, sidDiH f., vyatIpAtaH, varIyAn, pariGaH, SivaH, sidDaH, sADyaH, SuBaH, SuklaH, brahmA, EndraH, vEDftiH.

ASTUTE , a. vidagDaH -gDA -gDaM, savyAjaH -jA -jaM, caturaH -rA -raM.
Asunder, adv. pfTak, viralaM, vigata-pragata a.; oft. by vi; ‘throw a(sunder)’ vikzip 9 P, ‘burst a(sunder)’ vidIrRa &c.
ASUNDER: pfTak: Ph. burst a. vidIrRaH (rRA, rRaM).
ASUNDER , adv. viralaM, pfTak, pragataH -tA -taM, vigataH -tA -taM. — ‘Asun- der’ may often be expressed by the prep. vi; as, ‘cut asunder,’ vicCinnaH.
AŚWINS , (Nāsatya and Dasra, the twin sons of the Sun by the constellation Aśvinī, physicians of heaven) aSvinO du., svarvEdyO du., nAsatyO du., dasrO du., aSvinIsutO du., ASvineyO du.
ASYLE , ASYLUM, s. ASrayaH, ASayaH, SrayaRaM, saMSrayaH, gatiH f., pratiSrayaH, vizayaH. — (To seek asylum with) ASri (c. 1. -Srayati -te -SrayituM), upASri, samupASri, saMSri.
Asylum, s. ASramaH. 2 ASrayaH, SaraRaM, saMSrayaH, gati f.; ‘seek a(sylum) with’ A-samupA-Sri 1 U.
ASYLUM: ASramaH: a. for travellers paTikASramaH.
ASYMPTOTE: *asparSareKA.

At, prep. (Denoting time or place) by loc. of noun; ‘a(t) Kasi’ kASyAM; ‘a(t) that time’ tasminkAle. 2 In other senses, by instr. or abl.; oft. by gerund, or loc. abs.; ‘a(t) this’ idaM SrutvA; ‘a(t) his arrival’ saMprApte tasmin; ‘a(t) his advice’ tasyopadeSena; ‘a(t) what price’ kiyatA mUlyena; ‘a(t) first’ praTamaM; ‘a(t) last’ aMtataH, ‘at once’ yugapat, samaM; ‘a(t) all’ manAgapi, kimapi.

AT: I Of place: by loc.: who is at the door ko'yaM dvAri tizWati, Mu. ii.II Of time: by loc.: at midnight ardDarAtre.III Of price: by ins.: at what price have you bought this book kiyatA mUlyenEtat pustakaM gfhItam, P. ii. 4.IV Denot- -ing reason, occasion etc.: by ins.: at Rāma's command rAmAjYayA, R.: v. By, on. Ph.: at all manAgapi; at present aDunA; at first praTamam; at least antatas; they are all at play sarve krIqanti; while the French and the Germans were at war *yuDyamAnayoH ParAsijarmAnajAtyoH.

AT , prep. expressed by A or aBi prefixed to roots, as, ‘to arrive at,’ Agam, aBigam. — Before names of towns, ex- pressed by the loc. c.; as, ‘at Ayodhyā,’ ayoDyAyAM. At home, svagfhe, svasTAne; ‘at night,’ rAtrO; ‘at evening,’ AsanDyaM; ‘at this time,’ tatkAle, tatkzaRe; ‘at the moment,’ sapadi; ‘at present,’ varttamAne kAle, aDunA, samprati; ‘at first,’ praTamatas, pUrvvaM; ‘at last,’ anantaraM, Sepe; ‘at least,’ tAvat; ‘at all, kaTaYcana, manAk; ‘at the sight,’ AdarSanAt; ‘at ease,’ yaTAsuKaM, suKena; ‘at large,’ nirviGnaM; ‘at the price,’ mUlyena; ‘at once,’ yugapat, ekadA, ekakAle. — ‘At,’ may often be ex- pressed by the indec. part., as, ‘at the sight of that,’ tad dfzwvA; or by the loc. c., as, ‘at their arrival,’ tezu Agatezu; or by the abl. c., as, ‘at his bidding,’ tasya nideSAt; or by the instr. c., as, ‘at the king's command,’ rAjAjYayA.
AT-HAND , adv. upasTitaH -tA -taM, AsannaH -nnA -nnaM; ‘to be at hand,’ upasTA (c. 1. -tizWati -te -sTAtuM), pratyupasTA.
AT-ONCE , ekadA, yugapat, ekapade, ekakAle.
Atelier, s. citrakarmagfhaM.
ATHEISM: (1) nAstikyam;(2) nirISvaravAdaH (=de- -nial of the existence of God.)
ATHEISM , s. nAstikatA, nAstikyaM, devanindA, paralokABAvabudDiH.
Atheist, s. nAstikaH anISvaravAdin m., nirISvaraH. [Atheist]ical, a. nAstikavftti. Atheism, s. nAstikyaM, ISvaraniMdA.
ATHEIST: (1) nAstikaH;(2) nirISvaraH.
ATHEIST , s. nAstikaH, devanindakaH, anISvaravAdI m. (n), nAstikamate sTitaH.
ATHEIST , s. anISvaraH, nAstikamatAnuyAyI, durduruwaH.
ATHEISTIC, ATHEISTICAL: (1) nAstika- (in comp.);(2) nirISvaraH (rA, raM): with a. doctrines nirISvareRa vAdena. P. p.
ATHEISTICAL , a. (Given to atheism) nAstikavfttiH -ttiH -tti, deva- nindakaH -kA -kaM.
ATHIRST: (1) tfzitaH (tA, taM);(2) pipAsu (mfn.): v. Thirsty.
ATHIRST , a. tfzArttaH -rttA -rttaM, tfzitaH -tA -taM, pipAsuH -suH -su.
Athlete, s. mallaH, mallayodDf m. Athletic, a. malla, bAhuvIra, balavat saMnadDaSarIra; ‘a exercise, sports’ vyAyAmaH.
ATHLETE: (1) mallaH;(2) BkallaH (rare);(3) vyAyAmakuSalaH (?).
ATHLETE , s. mallayodDA m. (dDf), mallaH, JallaH.
ATHLETIC: v. Strong, robust, Ph.: a. exercise: vyAyAmaH.

ATHLETIC , a. (Belonging to wrestling) mallayudDasambanDakaH -kA -kaM. — (Strong) bAhuvIraH -rA -raM, mallaH -llA -llaM, vyAyAmI -minI -mi (n), vyAyAmaSIlaH -lA -laM, vyUQoraskaH -skA -skaM, pfTuSarIraH -rA -raM, balavAn vatI -vat (t). — (Athletic exercise) vyAyAmaH.
Athwart, prep. vilomaM; vyatyastaM; pAraM, prati pr.
ATHWART , prep. koRAkoRi, viparItaM, vilomaM, vyatyastaM, pratikUlaM; ‘athwart the way,’ pratimArgaM; ‘athwart the stream,’ pratisrotas; ‘athwart the river,’ nadIpAraM, nadItIrAntaraM.

sanskrit.iast: mahāsamudrāṇāṃ madhye ya eṭlaṇṭikiti abhidhīyate mahāsamudraḥ

details.body: ATLANTIC , a. mahAsamudrARAM maDye ya ewlaRwikiti aBiDIyate mahAsamudraH.
