sanskrit.word: भूगोलस्य यत् किञ्चिद् देशसमुद्रनगरादि विद्यते तदाकारनामादि-
sanskrit.iast: bhūgolasya yat kiñcid deśasamudranagarādi vidyate tadākāranāmādi-

details.body: Atlas, s. deSAleKyasaMgrahaH.
ATLAS: *mAnacitrakAvaliH; mAnacitrakasaMgrahaH.
ATLAS , s. BUgolasya yat kiYcid deSasamudranagarAdi vidyate tadAkAranAmAdi- mudritaH patrasamUhaH.
ATLAS , s. deSAleKyamAlA, deSasamudrAdyAleKyamAlA.
Atmosphere, s. gaganaM, AkASaH-SaM, aMtari(-rI)kzaM, naBas n. 2 SUnyaM. [Atmospher]ical, a. AMtarIkza (kzI f.), vAyava (vI f.), AkASIya.
ATMOSPHERE: vAyuH: v. Air (I) and (II).
ATMOSPHERE , s. AkASaH, naBaH n. (s), gagaRaM, aBraM, antarIkzaM, vAyuvartma n., (n), vihAyasaH -saM, maRqalaM, SUnyaM, SUnyatvaM, AzwaM.
ATMOSPHERE , s. sAmAnyavAyuH m., sAmAnyavAtaH, vAyucakraM, vAtAvaraRaM, GanASrayaH, meGamaRqalaM, vAtAspadaM, vAyvAspadaM.
ATMOSPHERIC: (1) vAyavaH (vI, vaM);(2) vAyavyaH (vyA, vyaM).
ATMOSPHERICAL , a. AkASIyaH -yA -yaM, AntarIkzaH -kzI -kzaM, vAyavaH -vI -vaM, vEhAyasaH -sI -saM, vihAyasIyaH -yA -yaM.
Atom, s. paramARuH, aRuH, kaRaH, lavaH, leSaH; ‘a(tom)ic theory’ paramARuvAdaH. [Atom]ical, a. paramARumaya (yI f.), sUkzma. 2 aRuvizaya, aRuvizayaka.
ATOM: (1) paramARuH;(2) aRuH.
ATOM , s. paramARuH m., aRuH m., kaRaH, lavaH, leSaH, kaRikA, sUkzmaH.
ATOM , s. kAkiRikA. ATOMISM, s. paramARuvAdaH, sUkzmavAdaH.
ATOMIC: Ph.: the a. theory paramARuvAdaH.
ATOMICAL , a. (Consisting of atoms) ARakaH -kI -kaM, aRakaH -kA -kaM, paramARumayaH -yI -yaM. — (Minute) sUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM. — (Relating to atoms) aRuvizayaH -yA -yaM, paramARusambanDakaH -kA -kaM.
ATOMIST , s. paramARuvAdI m. (n), sUkzmavAdI.

Atone, v. i. prAyaScittaM kf 8 U, nizkftiM kf, prAyaScittena pariSuc c.; pramfj 2 P; upacArAtikramaM pramArzwumayamasmAkamAraMBaH (M. 4) ‘to a(tone) for the slighting of prostration’ &c. 2 anunI 1 P, saMDA 3 U, praSam c. (Samayati) [Atone]ment, s. prAyaScittaM, nizkfti f. 2 pramArjanaM.
ATONE: I To expiate: q. v.: prAyaScittaM karoti (kf, c. 8.) or carati (car, c. 1.).II To make amends: pariSoDayati (c. of SuD) (?).

To ATONE , v. a. (To expiate, answer for) prAyaScittaM kf, nizkftiM kf, prAyaScittena pApaM pariSuD in caus. (-SoDayati -yituM), or pApAt muc (c. 6. muYcati moktuM); pApakzamAM siD in caus. (sADayati -yituM). — (To reconcile) sanDA (c. 3. -daDyati -DAtuM), anunI (c. 1. -nayati -netuM), praSam in caus. (-Samayati -yituM).
To ATONE , v. n. (To agree) samman (c. 4. -manyate -mantuM). — (To stand as an equivalent) prAyaScittaH or pratiniDiH or pratiBUH BU.
ATONEMENT: I Agreement, reconciliation: q. v.II Expiation: q. v. prAyaScittaH. To make a. for pariSoDayati (?)
ATONEMENT , s. prAyaScittaH, nizkftiH f., pApakzamAsADanaM, pApanASaH, agnizwut f. — (One who atones) prAyaScittakArI m. (n), nizkftikarttA m. (rttf), pApakzamAsADakaH.
ATONEMENT , l. 1. for prAyaScittaH, read prAyaScittaM.
Atonic, a. agninASaka, atejasvin.
ATONIC , a. agninASakaH -kA -kaM, atejasvI -svinI -svi (n).
ATONY: (1) nistejatA (?);(2) nirvIryatA (?).
ATRABILARIOUS , a. kAlapittasampUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, durmanAH -nAH -naH (s).
Atrabilious, a. durmanas, vimanaska.
ATRAMENTOUS , a masivarRaH -rRA -rRaM, kfzRavarRaH -rRA -rRaM.
Atrocious, a. Gora, bIBatsa (of things); atipApin atidurvftta, pApizWa, nfSaMsa. [Atrocious]ness, Atrocity, s. nfSaMsatA, bIBatsatA, GoratA. 2 atipApaM, Gorakarman n.

ATROCIOUS: (1) bIBatsaH (tsA, tsaM), you great sinner, doer of impure, disgustful, a. deeds mahApAtakin, aSizwavikftacezwa, bImatsakarman. Vi. iii. v. Loathsome;(2) vikftaH (tA, taM) v. Dis- -gustful;(3) pApizWaH (zWA, zWaM). v. Sinful;(4) nfSaMsaH (sA, saM). v. Cruel, Ph. a. crime GorapAtakaH.
ATROCIOUS , a. atipApI -pinI -pi (n), atidozI -ziRI -zi (n), atipAtakI -kinI -ki (n), atipApizWaH -zWA -zWaM, atyantadurAcAraH -rA -raM, durvfttaH -ttA -ttaM, dAruRaH -RA -RaM.
ATROCIOUSNESS: (1) bIBatsatA;(2) vikftatA;(3) nfSaMsatA. Better expr. by atrocious.
ATROCITY: I Atrociousness: q. v.II An atrocious deed: bIBatsakarman; vikftacezwitam; etc. v. Atrocious.
ATROCITY , ATROCIOUSNESS, s. atipAtakaM, atipApaM, atidozaH, atiduzwatA.
Atrophy, s. kzayaH, kzayarogaH, agnyaBAvaH.
ATROPHY: SarIraSozaRam (?).
ATROPHY , s. kzayaH, kzayarogaH, SarIraSozaRaM, agnyaBAvaH, ajIrRatA.

Attach, v. t. AsaMj c., anuraMj c., saMbaMD c., ‘a(ttach) great importance to public censure’ lokApavAdo balavAnmato me (R. xiv. 40) ‘a(ttach) friends to you by virtue’ sadAcaraRenAtmani mitrARyAsaMjaya-anuraMjaya. 2 AsiD 1 P, Akram 1 U, 4 P, Df 10. 3 ‘Ascribe’, q. v. v. i. saMbaMD 9 P, anuzakta a. BU 1 P. [Attach]ed, a. anurakta, Asakta, saM-pra-sakta. 2 Baktimat sAnurAga, avirakta (with loc.). 3 AsidDa, AkrAMta. ‘to be a(ttached)’ AsaMj-anuraMj- pass.; ‘subjects are firmly a(ttached) to the king’ deve sudfQamanuraktAH prajAH (Mu. 1); ‘fondly a(ttached)’ badDagAQAnurAgaH [Attach]ment, s. anurAgaH, aBiniveSaH, Asakti f., prIti f., Bakti f., prasakti f., AsaMgaH (all with loc.). 2 AseDaH, grahaRaM.
ATTACH: I To fasten, lit. and fig.:(1) AsaYjayati (c. of saYj);(2) saMSlezayati (c. of Sliz); (3) lagayati (c. of lag) ?.II To a. one's property *krokaM karoti. (with gen.): v. Also to arrest.

To ATTACH , v. a. (To fix to one's interests, win over) saYj in caus. (saYjayati -yituM), anuraYj in caus. (-raYjayati -yituM). — (To connect) sambanD (c. 9. -banDAti -bandDuM). — (To seize) AseDaM kf; Df (c. 1. Darati, DarttuM), Akram (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM). — (To attribute) Aruh in caus. (-ropayati -yituM). — (To be attached) AsaYj in pass. (-sajyate), anuraYj in pass. (-rajyate). — (To be connected) [Page031-a+ 51] sambanD in pass. (-baDyate).
ATTACHED: AsaktaH (ktA, ktaM). To be a. Asajyate.

ATTACHED , p. p. anuraktaH -ktA -ktaM, AsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, saMsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, prasaktaH -ktA -ktaM, lagnaH -gnA -gnaM, lagitaH -tA -taM, BaktaH -ktA -ktaM, BaktimAn -matI -mat (t), aviraktaH -ktA -ktaM, saMhitaH -tA -taM, anurAgavAn -vatI -vat (t), sAnurAgaH -gA -gaM.

ATTACHMENT (subs.): I Connexion, con- -tact: q. v.II Affection, devotion:(1) AsaktiH;(2) prasaktiH;(3) saNgaH;(4) AsaNgaH. N. B. All these words cons. with the loc. III In law: a. of property *krokaH.
ATTACHMENT , s. AsaktiH f., prasaktiH f., anurAgaH, anuraktiH f., raktiH f. saNgaH, AsaNgaH, prasaNgaH, BaktiH f., cittAsaNgaH, samprItiH f., parAyaRaH, turAyaRaH.

Attack, v. t. aBidru 1 P, avaskaMd 1 P, Akram 1 U, 4 P, aBiyuj 7 A; Apat 1 P, aBiprayA 2 P, pratiyuD 4 A; Asad c. 2 A-parA-han 2 U; (an opinion &c.) parAmfS 6 P, pratyavasTA 1 A (with loc.); ‘a(ttack)ed by a disease’ vyADigrastaH, rogAkrAMtaH. s. aBiyogaH, avaskaMdaH-danaM, ApAtaH, AkramaH.
ATTACK (subs): (1) AkramaH;(2) AkramaRam;(3) aBikramaH;(4) aBiyogaH;(5) aBigrahaH;(6) avaskandaH or avaskandanam (=storming). A. of any disease: AkramaH, -Ram.

ATTACK (v. t.); I Of physical force:(1) A-krAmati or krAmyati, aBi-, (kram, c. 1. and 4.); (2) aBiyunakti or yojayati (yuj c. 7. and 10.), Anantavarmā raised an army to a. him anantavarmA tamamiyoktuM balasamutTAnamakarot, D. viii.;(3) ava-skandati (skand, c. 1.) (=to fall upon), Mādhavasena coming to me was, in the way, a. ed and seized by your Antapāla mADavaseno mamo- pAntikamupasarpannantarA tvadIyenAntapAlenAvaskandya gfhItaH, Mal. i. To a. in defence:(1) pratyamiyunakti; (2) pratigfhvAti (graha c. 9.), a. ed the opposite army pratibalaM pratijagrAha, D. i.;(3) pratiyuDyate (yuD, c. 4.). v. To fight.II To assail with words: (1) AkrAmati;(2) avaskandayati (skand c. 10.), Vi. iii.;(3) A-hanti, aBi-, parA-, (han, c. 2.), a. ed by his haughty words vacOBirudDatEH parAhataH, Ki. xiv. 1.III To a. an opinion etc.:(1) parAmarzati (mfz, c. 1.);(2) pratyavatizWate (sTA, c. 1.) (with loc.) (=to stand up against).IV Of disease:(1) AkrAmati, a. ed with fever jvarAkrAntaH (ntA, ntaM);(2) carati (car, c. 1.), O fever, listen to me how you would a. men SfRuzva jvara sandeSaM yaTA loke carizyasi.

To ATTACK , v. a. Akram (c. 1. -krAmati, c. 4. -krAmyati -kramituM), upakram, upAkram, aBikram; Asad (c. 10. -sAdayati -yituM), Askand (c. 1. -skandati -skantuM); AyuD (c. 4. -yuDyate -yodDuM), pratiyuD, yuD in caus. (yoDayati -yituM), aBidru (c. 1. -dravati -drotuM), upadru, samAdru, aBiDAv (c. 1. -DAvati -te -DAvituM), aBiprayA (c. 2. -yAti -yAtuM).
ATTACK , s. aBiyogaH, aBigrahaH, aBikramaH, AkramaH, avaskandaH, aBimarddaH.
ATTACK , s. aDikramaH -maRaM; ‘of any disease,’ avatAraH, avataraRaM, AveSaH; ‘of fever,’ AtapalaNGanaM; ‘first attack of disease,’ pUrvvAvataraH.
ATTACKED , p. p. aBiyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, AkrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, AsAditaH -tA -taM.

Attain, v. (to) prAp 5 P, prati-pra-A-pad 4 A, laB 1 A, aDigam 1 P, A-samA-sad c. aS 5 A; ‘easy to a(ttain)’ sulaBa a.; ‘difficult to a(ttain)’ durApa a.; duzprApa a. [Attain]ment, s. aDigamaH, lABaH, avApti f., prApti f., samAsAdanaM.

ATTAIN (v. t.): (1) aDi-gacCati (gam, c. 1.), even after a. ing knowledge SrutamapyaDigamya, Ki. ii. 41.;(2) A-sIdati (sad, c. 1.), the king will a. divine form by means of charms rAjA kila mantrabalena devayogyaM vapurAsAdayizyati, D. iii.;(3) prApnoti: v. To obtain;(4) spfSati (spfS, c. 6.) (=to touch), by this time would have a. ed your age iyatA kAlena tavemAM vayovasTAmasprakzyetAM, D. iii.
ATTAIN (v. i.): (1) aDigacCati (with acc.); (2) AsIdati (with acc.).

To ATTAIN , v. a. prAp (c. 5. -Apnoti -AptuM), samprAp; laB (c. 1. laBate, labDuM), gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM), with acc., aDigam; yA (c. 2. yAti, yAtuM), AyA; i (c. 2. eti, etuM), aBI (aByeti); f (c. 1. fcCati, artuM), aS (c. 5. aSnute, aSituM), upAS, samaS; spfS (c. 6. spfSati, sprazwuM), AviS (c. 6. -viSati -vezwuM).
ATTAINABLE: (1) laByaH (ByA, ByaM);(2) sulaBaH (BA, BaM);(3) prApyaH (pyA, pyaM)(4) aDigamyaH (myA, myaM);(5) AsAdanIyaH (yA, yaM).
ATTAINABLE , a. prApyaH -pyA -pyaM, prApaRIyaH -yA -yaM, gamyaH -myA -myaM, laByaH -ByA -ByaM, samAsAdyaH -dyA -dyaM, sulaBaH -BA -BaM, sADyaH -DyA -DyaM.
Attainder, s. kalaMkaH, apayaSas n. 2 ADarzaRaM, aBiyogaH.
ATTAINDER: v. Stain. Ph.: a bill of a. *aBiyogapatram.
ATTAINDER , s. (The conviction of a crime) ADarzaRaM. — (Taint, sully of character) kalaNkaH, apayaSaH n. (s), apakIrtiH f.
ATTAINED , p. p. prAptaH -ptA -ptaM, labDaH -bDA -bDaM, aDigataH -tA -taM.

ATTAINMENT: I The act of attaining:(1) aDigamaH;(2) lABaH;(3) prAptiH;(4) avAptiH. By the a. of: expr. by the part. of the verb ‘to attain’. For the a. of: expr. by the inf. of the verb ‘to attain’.II Of knowledge: (1) vyutpattiH;(2) pAradarSitA, of great mathe- matical a. s gaRitaSAstrasya pAradarSI.
ATTAINMENT , s. lABaH, labDiH f., prAptiH f., avAptiH f., utpattiH f., arjjanaM, upArjjanaM; ‘attainment of knowledge,’ vidyAgamaH.
Attaint, v. t. ADfz c., aBiyuj 7 A. 2 ‘Stain’, q. v.
ATTAINT: I To stain: q. v.II Leg t. t.: a. ed of high treason rAjadrohadUzitaH (tA, taM) (?).
To ATTAINT , v. a. (To corrupt, disgrace) duz in caus. (dUzayati yituM), kalaNka (nom. kalaNkayati -yituM), kalaNkaM kf. — (To convict) ADfz (c. 10. -Darzayati -yituM), ADazarRaM kf.
ATTAINTED , p. p. (Convicted) ADarzitaH -tA -taM. — (Corrupted) dUzitaH -tA -taM.
Attemper, v. t. yaTAMSataH miSr 10 or saMyuj 10. 2 niyam 1 P, Sam c. (Samayati)

To ATTEMPER , v. a. (To mingle in just proportions) yaTAMSatas miSr (c. 10. miSrayati -yituM) or saMyuj in caus. (-yojayati -yituM); dravIkf. — (To soften, mollify) Sam in caus. (Samayati -yituM), srada (nom. sradayati -yituM), snigDIkf. — (To regulate) niyam (c. 1. -yacCati -yantuM).

Attempt, v. t. prayat 1 A, Gaw 1 A, upakram 1 A, AraB 1 A, udyam 1 P, pravft 1 A, cezw 1 A, vyavaso 4 P (SamIlatAM CettuM vyavasyati S. 1). 2 Attack, q. v. s. yatnaH, prayatnaH, udyamaH, AraMBaH, prayAsaH, upakramaH, pravftti f., udyogaH.

ATTEMPT (subs.): (1) udyamaH, I have resolved on an a. on his life badDo vaDAyodyamaH, Vi. v.;(2) yatnaH, prayatnaH (=effort), I fancy the a. of Dāru- varmā has been unsuccessful aPalaM dAruvarmaRaH prayatna- mavagacCAmi, Mu. iii.;(3) AramBaH (=beginn- -ing), with success proportionate to a. s AramBa- sadfSodayaH, R. i. 15;(4) cezwA.

ATTEMPT (v. t.): I To endeavour:(1) yatate, pra-, (yat, c. 1.), which princes a. to appropriate even by misdeeds duritErapi kartumAtmasAt prayatante nfpa- sUnavo hi yat, R. viii. 2.;(2) yasati or yasyati, pra- (yas, c. 1 and 4). repeatedly a. ed to fly up punaH punaH prAyasadutplavAya saH, N. i. 125;(3) cezwate, (cezw, c. 1.) Mu. v.;(4) A-raBate, pra-, (raB, c. 1.) (=to begin), low people do not a. at all from fear of obstacles prAraByate na Kalu viGnaBayena nIcEH, Mu. iii.;(5) Gawate (Gaw, c. 1.) (rare) B. xii. 26.II To attack: q. v.

To ATTEMPT , v. a. (To try) yat (c. 1. yatate, yatituM), upakram (c. 1. -kramate -kramituM), AraB (c. 1. -raBate -rabDuM), samAraB; udyam (c. 1. -yacCati -yantuM), pravft (c. 1. -varttate -varttituM), Gaw (c. 1. Gawate, GawituM), vyavaso (c. 4. -syati -sAtuM), cezw (c. 1. cezwate, cezwituM), udyogaM kf. — (To at- tack) Akram (c. 1. -krAmati, c. 4. -krAmyati, -kramituM).
ATTEMPT , s. samudyamaH, udyamaH, AramBaH, upakramaH, udyogaH, pravfttiH f., cezwA, grahaH, sADanaM, vyApAraH. — (Attack) AkramaH.
To ATTEMPT , v. n. yatnaM kf, prayatnaM kf, udyogaM kf, pravft; ‘he attempted to raise the stick,’ daRqam unnamayituM pravfttaH.
ATTEMPTED , p. p. ArabDaH -bDA -bDaM, aDyavasAyitaH -tA -taM, samudyataH -tA -taM.
ATTEMPTER , s. AramBakaH, pravarttakaH, upakramitA m. (tf), AkrAmakaH.

Attend, v. t. upasTA 1 U, saMniDA 3 U, A-samA-gam 1 P; ‘a(ttend) the meeting’ saMsadi saMnihito BavaH ‘a(ttend) school’ SAlAM gacCa. 2 anu-i-yA 2 P, parivf c., saha gam; ‘good luck a(ttend)s our lord in every respect’ sarvaTA spfSaMti naH svABinamaByudayAH. (Rat. 1). 3 (on, upon) upa-paryupa-sTA 1 A, upa-As 2 A, upacar 1 P, upasev 1 A, Sru desid. (SuSrUzate), (with acc.). 4 (to words) Sru 5 P, AkarR 10; ‘a(ttend) to me’ madvacanaM SfRu; ‘a(ttend) now’ sAvaDAno Bava, avaDIyatAM; (duty &c.) avaDA 3 U, manaH-dA, niDA, 3 U, mano yuj 10, (with loc.); avekz 1 A. 5 vilaMb-pratIkz 1 A. [Attend]ed, a. sameta, parivfta, samanvita, anuyAta, sahita, sa in comp.; ‘a(ttended) by maidservants’ saKIgaRaparivftA, saKIparivArA. [Attend]ance, s. upasTAnaM, saMniDAnaM; SuSrUzA, upacAraH, upAsanaM, sevA. [Attend]ant, a. AnuzaMgika (kI f.), sahagAmin, sahacArin. s. anucaraH, sevakaH, anuyAyin m., paricaraH; ‘a group of a(ttedant)s’ anuyAyivargaH, paricCadaH, parivAraH, paribarhaH. Attention, s. Asakti f., aBiniveSaH, avaDAnaM, manoyogaH, avekzA, apramAdaH, apramattatA. 2 anuzWAnaM, upasevanaM, parAyaRatA; ‘a(ttention) to one subject’ ekAgratA, nivizwacittatA, ‘pay a(ttention)’ avaDAnaM dA (with loc.). Attentive, a. avahita, sAvaDAna, dattAvaDAna, samAhita, apramatta, Asakta, aBinivizwa; ‘closely a(ttentive)’ ekAgra, ananyavftti, ekatAna, sAdara, dakziRa (to ladies), ‘in-a(ttentive) to household &c.’ gfhadAranirapekza. [Attentive]ly adv. sAvaDAnaM, avahitaM &c.

ATTEND (v. t.) I To attend on or upon: q. v. II To await, stay for: q. v. pratIkzate (Ikz, c. 1.)III To be present at:(1) upa-tizWati (sTA, c. 1.) (see Ki. vi. 29);(2) saMni-daDAti or Datte (DA, c. 3.) I a. ed it with my friend Dhanamitra ahaM ca saha saKyA DanamitreRa tatra sannayaDizi, D. ii.;(3) better by gacCati, saNgacCati or AgacCati, samAgacCati, according as it means going or coming.IV To attend to: q. v.
To ATTEND , v. n. (To be attentive) avaDA in pass. (-DIyate); ‘let attention be paid,’ avaDIyatAM. — (To delay) vilamb (c. 1. -lambate -lambituM).

ATTEND ON OR UPON: (1) upa-tizWate, paryupa- (sTA, c. 1.), returning after a. ing on the sun sUryopasTAna- sannivfttaM, V. i.;(2) upa-carati, pari-, (car, c. 1.), a. on her with care yatnAdupacaryaMtAM, Sa. iii.;(3) upa-Aste (As, c. 2.), N. xxii. 1.

ATTEND TO: (1) SfRoti (Sru, c. 5.) (=to listen: q. v.), a. to that (message) SfRu...tAM, R. viii. 77.; a. to me mama vacanaM SfRu;(2) ava-daDAti or Datte (DA, c. 3.), let the superintendents also a. each to his own work sve sve karmaRyaTa samavaDattApyaDi- kftAH, Vi. vii.;(3) mano yacCati or dadAti (dA, c. 1. and 3.) or nidaDAti (DA, c. 3.), or yunakti (yuj, c. 7.) (=to apply the mind; fix one's attention on);(4) avekzate (Ikz, c. 1.) (=to look after: q. v.), I have a. ed to only one civil action ekameva mayA pOrakAryamavekzitam, Sa. vi.

ATTENDANCE: I The act of waiting on or serving:(1) upacAraH;(2) upasTAnam (rare); (3) SuSrUzA (=reception of a guest).II Presence: q. v. upasTitiH. Ph. there was a good a. in the meeting samAyAM bahavaH samAgaman. III A train, a retinue: q. v.: anuyAyivargaH. IV Attention: q. v.
ATTENDANCE , s. SuSrUzA, paricaryyA, upAsanaM, upacAraH, sevA, upasevA, anugamanaM.
ATTENDANT (subs.): (1) anucaraH;(2) anuyAyin (m.);(3) paricaraH: v. Companion, servant, follower. Ph. a train of a. s:(1) anuyAyivargaH; (2) paribarhaH;(3) paricCadaH: v. Also conco- -mitant.
ATTENDANT (adj.): (1) AnuzaNgikaH (kI, kaM);(2) anugAmin (f. nI).
ATTENDANT , a. sahagAmI -minI -mi (n), sahacArI -riRI -ri (n).
ATTENDANT , s. sevakaH, paricaraH, sahacArI m. (n), anuyAyI m. (n), anusArI m. (n), anucaraH, pArizadaH, pariDisTaH. — (Train of at- tendants) parivAraH, parivarhaH. — (Of Siva) pramaTaH.

ATTENDED , p. p. (Accompanied) sahitaH -tA -taM, sametaH -tA -taM, pari- vAritaH -tA -taM, parivftaH -tA -taM, vftaH -tA -taM, samanvitaH -tA -taM. — (At- tended to) anuzWitaH -tA -taM. When only two persons are re- ferred to, dvitIya or sahAya may be used; as, ‘attended by Indrasena,’ indrasenadvitIyaH -yA -yaM or indrasenasahAyaH -yA -yaM; ‘at- tended by servants,’ saprezyaH -zyA -zyaM.
ATTENT , a. nivizwaH -zwA -zwaM, avahitaH -tA -taM, AhitaH -tA -taM.

ATTENTION: I The act or state of attending: (1) avaDAnam, please lend me your a. for a moment mAM muhUrtamavaDAnadAnenAnugfhvantu, Ma. ix.;(2) manoyogaH; (3) apramAdaH or apramattatA (=carefulness);(4) aBiniveSaH (=application, study);(5) avekzA (=looking after). Ph.: his whole a. being devoted to it ananyahfdayatayA, K.; it engages my a. mano me baDnAti, (after R. xiii. 47.); to draw the a. of the king narapatipraboDanArTam, K.II. Politeness, courtesy: q. v. AdaraH or samAdaraH.

ATTENTION, PAY: (1) avaDAnaM dadAti (dA, c. 3.), paying a. to the buzzing of bees dattAvaDAnaM maDulehi- gItO B. ii. 7.;(2) Adriyate (df, c. 6.) (=to respect), the king without paying any a. (to what he said) rAjA anAdftya, Sa. vi.:(3) Asajyate (=to devote to: q. v.): v. Attend to.

ATTENTION , s. avaDAnaM, avaDAnatA, avekzA, anvavekzA, apekzA, aBi- niveSaH, manoniveSaH, manoniDAnaM, manaHpraveSaH, nivizwacittatA, manoyogaH, AsaktiH f., anurAgaH, apramAdaH. — (To a pursuit) parAyaRaH, anuzWAnaM, sevanaM, upasevA. — (To discourse) kaTAnurAgaH. — (To one object) ekAgratA.

ATTENTIVE: I Heedful, observant:(1) avahitaH (tA, taM); dattAvaDAnaH or kftAvaDAnaH (nA, naM) (=paying attention);(3) sAvaDAnaH (nA, naM) (4) samAhitaH (tA, taM);(5) apramattaH (ttA, ttaM).II Attentive to a guest etc.:(1) darSitAdaraH (rA, raM), K.;(1) dakziRaH (RA, RaM) (as a lover ?) V. iii.

ATTENTIVE , a. sAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, avahitaH -tA -taM, dattAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, kftAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, aBinivizwaH -zwA -zwaM, AsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, AsaktacittaH -ttA -ttaM, ASravaH -vA -vaM, samAhitaH -tA -taM, pramAdarahitaH -tA -taM, yatna- vAn -vatI -vat (t), prasitaH -tA -taM, apramattaH -ttA -ttaM. — (Closely at- tentive) ananyamanAH -nAH -naH (s), ekAgraH -grA -graM, ananyavfttiH -ttiH -tti, ekatAnaH -nA -naM, ekAyanaH -nA -naM.
ATTENTIVELY: (1) avahitam;(2) sAvaDAnam;(3) apramattam;(4) manoyogena.
ATTENTIVELY , adv. sAvaDAnaM, avaDAnAt, avahitaM, manaHpraveSena, pramAda- vyatirekeRa.
ATTENUANT (adj. and subs.): vidrAvakaH or vilAyakaH (kA, kaM) (?).
Attenuate, v. t. kzE c. (kzapayati), tanUkf 8 U, kzIRI-kfSI-kf. [Attenuat]ed, a. kfSa, kzIRa, tanu, kzAma, apacita (apacitaM gAtraM). [Attenuat]ion, s. kfSatA, kzAmatA, kfSAMgatvaM.
ATTENUATE: (1) kfSIkaroti;(2) tanUkaroti.
To ATTENUATE , v. a. kraS (nom. kraSayati -yituM), tanUkf, kzi in caus. (kzapayati -yituM), SlakzRa (nom. SlakzRayati -yituM), sUkzmIkf.
ATTENUATED: (1) kfSaH (SA, SaM);(2) kzIRaH (RA, RaM);(3) apacitaH (tA, taM): v. Thin.

ATTENUATED , p. p. kfSaH -SA -SaM, prakfSitaH -tA -taM, parikfSaH -SA -SaM, tanuH -nuH -nvI -nu, kzIRaH -RA -RaM, SIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, kzAmaH -mA -maM. — (In body) kfSANgaH -NgI -NgaM, SuzkANgaH -NgI -NgaM.
ATTENUATION , s. kArSyaM, kzAmatA, SIrRatA. — (Of body) kfSANgatvaM, SarIraSozaRaM.
Attest, v. t. sAkzyaM dA 3 P; (sAkzyeRa) pramA RIkf 8 U, vyaMj 7 P, prakawIkf, diS 6 P. 2 sAkziRaM kf, sAkzye Ahve 1 P. [Attest]ation, s. sAkzyaM, pramARaM, pratyakzapramARaM.

ATTEST: I To a deed: *patrasya viSudDipradarSanAya sAkzI Bavati or svanAma patre liKati: Ph. the will is a. ed by three witnesses *asyecCApatrasya viSudDipradarSakA- strayaH sAkziRaH santi.II To manifest: q. v.: (1) prakawIkaroti;(2) vyanakti (aYj, c. 7.).

To ATTEST , v. a. (To bear witness of) sAkzyaM or sAkzitAM dA (c. 3 dadAti, dAtuM), sAkzyeRa or sAkziRA or pratyakzadarSanena pramARaM dA, or pramA- RIkf, or diS (c. 6. diSati dezwuM). — (To call to witness) Avhe (c. 1. -hvayati -te -hvAtuM), sAkziRaM kf.
ATTEST , ATTESTATION, s. sAkzyaM, sAkzitA, pramARaM, dfQoktiH, pratyakzapramARaM.

sanskrit.slp1: yezAM sAkziRAM nAmAni liKitAni tat sarvaM kftrimam
sanskrit.word: येषां साक्षिणां नामानि लिखितानि तत् सर्वं कृत्रिमम्
sanskrit.iast: yeṣāṃ sākṣiṇāṃ nāmāni likhitāni tat sarvaṃ kṛtrimam

details.body: ATTESTATION: I Verbal: sAkzyam.II Written: Ph. the a. s of the will are all forged *icCApatre yezAM sAkziRAM nAmAni liKitAni tat sarvaM kftrimam.
Attic, s. kzOmaH-maM, awwaH.
ATTIC (adj.): *eTinIyaH (yA, yaM); yavanaH (nI, naM) (with less precision).
ATTIC (subs.): Perh. awwaH; Sirogfham.
ATTIC , s. (Upper room) awwaH, kzOmaH, SirogfhaM.

Attire, s. vezaH, veSaH, vastraM, pariDAnaM, ABaraRaM, paricCadaH, nepaTyaM, alaMkAraH; ‘richly attired’ gfhItamahArGavezaH, udAra-Arya-nepaTyaH. v. t. (vastreRa) AcCad 10, vezwa 1 A, saMvye 1 P. 2 BUz 10; See Adorn, ‘a(ttire) oneself’ vas 2 A; ‘a(ttir)ing business’ nepaTyaviDAnaM.
ATTIRE (v. t.): (1) vaste (vas, c. 2.) (=to put on, dress: q. v.);(2) BUzayati (=to adorn: q. v.).
ATTIRE (subs.): (1) veSaH;(2) paribarhaH, in rich a. sPItaparibarhaH (rhA, rhaM), D. ii.: v. Dress, closses.

To ATTIRE , v. a. (To attire one's self) vas (c. 2. vaste, vasitu). — (To clothe) vezw (c. 1. vezwate, vezwituM), vastra (nom. vastrayati -yituM), ACad (c. 10. -CAdayati -yituM), saMvye (c. 1. -vyayati -vyAtuM). — (To adorn) parizkf (c. 8. -karoti -karttuM), alaNkf, saMskf; BUz (c. 10. BUzayati -yituM).
ATTIRE , s. vastraM, veSaH, pariDAnaM, paricCadaH, ABaraRaM, BUzRaM, ambaraM, [Page032-a+ 51] saMvyAnaM, alaNkAraH, parizkAraH.
ATTIRED , p. p. AcCAditaH -tA -taM, pracCAditaH -tA -taM, paricCannaH -nnA -nnaM, saMvItaH -tA -taM, prAvftaH -tA -taM, alaNkftaH -tA -taM, parizkftaH -tA -taM.
Attitude, s. saMsTiti f., saMsTitaM, BAvaH, avasTA, vftti f., AkAraH, ‘hostile a(ttitude)’ vEraBAvaH, vipakzavfttiH.
ATTITUDE: v. Posture, position. Ph. Russia has assumed a threatening a. towards Persia *pArasyarAjyaM prati rusiyErvirudDavfttiH kakzIkftA.
ATTITUDE , s. sTAnaM, BAvaH, avasTA, sTitiH f., AkAraH, rUpaM, vfttiH f., BUmiH f.
Attorney, s. parakAryasADakaH, pratipuruzaH-hastakaH.
ATTORNEY: *vyavahArapratiniDiH; moktAraH. A power of a. *vyavahArapratiniDipatram. A general *vyavahAra- sacivaH, vicArAdikAryezu rAjapakzasamarTako rAjakIya- praDAnopadezwA.
ATTORNEY , s. parakAryyasADakaH, parakAryyasampAdakaH, pratipuruzaH, pratihastaH.
ATTORNEY , s. pratiniDiH m. ATTRACTION, s. anukarzaH, AkzepaH.

Attract, v. t. A-samA-kfz 1 P, anukfz (in grammar); Avfj 10, aBipraRI 1 P, vimuh c., vi-pra-luB c. [Attract]ion, s. A-samA-karzaRaM, AvarjanaM; anukarzaH-rzaRaM. 2 pra-vi-loBanaM. [Attract]ive, a. Akarzaka, AkarzaRaSIla, manohara, citta-apahArin-hArin. 2 mohaka, praloBaka.
ATTRACT: Akarzati, samA-, (kfz, c. 1.) (Lit. and Fig.): v. To draw, allure.

To ATTRACT , v. a. Akfz (c. 1. -karzati, c. 6. -kfzati -krazwuM), samAkfz, pratikfz, samupakfz; aBipraRI (c. 1. -Rayati -RetuM). — (To beguile) muh in caus. (mohayati -yituM), vimuh, sammuh; praluB in caus. (-lo- Bayati -yituM), viluB.
ATTRACTED , p. p. AkfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, AkarzitaH -tA -taM, pralIBitaH -tA -taM, viloBitaH -tA -taM, mohitaH -tA -taM.
ATTRACTION: I The power of a.: AkarzaRaSaktiH. II The act of attracting.:(1) AkarzaRam; (2) AkfzwiH;(3) samAkarzaRam.III Allurement, enticements: q. v.
ATTRACTION , s. AkarzaH -rzaRaM, AkfzwiH f., sannikarzaRaM. — (Allurement) praloBanaM, viloBaH, viloBanaM; ‘desire to blend,’ yiyavizA.
ATTRACTIVE: I Lit.: Ph. the a. force (of bodies): AkarzaRaSaktiH.II Fig.; alluring, charming: q. v.: hArin (f. RI).

ATTRACTIVE , a. AkarzakaH -kI -kaM, karzakaH -kA kaM, manoharaH -rA -raM, AkarzaRaSIlaH -lA -laM, cittApahArI -riRI -ri (n). — (Beguiling) mohI -hinI -hi (n), praloBakaH -kA -kaM. — (Winning friends) mitrayuH -yuH -yu.
ATTRACTIVENESS: manohAritvam: v. Charm.
ATTRIBUTABLE: (1) AropaRIyaH (yA, yaM);(2) aDyAropaRIyaH (yA, yaM). Ph.: it was a. to you that we did not take the fort *tvannimittaM durgaM na gfhItam.
ATTRIBUTABLE , a. AropaRIyaH -yA -yaM, aDyAropaRIyaH -yA -yaM, aBisa- mbanDanIyaH -yA -yaM.
Attribute, v. t. See Ascribe; ‘a(ttribut)ing to themselves false grearness’ AtmanyAropitAlIkABimAnAH (Ka. 108). s. DarmaH, upADiH, guRaH. 2 viSezaRaM. [Attribut]ive, a. vAcya, viSezaka-Ra.
ATTRIBUTE (v. t.): Arozayati (c. of rUpa): v. To ascribe.

ATTRIBUTE (subs.): (1) DarmaH, and on the contra- -ry, the imputation of the subject and its a. s on the object tadviparyayeRa vizayiRastadDarmARAM ca vizaye'DyAsaH, S. i. p.;(2) guRaH, possessed of the eight a. s, minuteness etc. aRimAdyazwaguRopetasya.

To ATTRIBUTE , v. a. (As an action, quality, &c., to any one) karmma guRaM vA ityAdi kasmiMScit or kasmEcid Aruh in caus. (-ropayati -yituM), aDyAruh or aBisambanD (c. 9. -baDnAti -bandDuM) or sambanD, or dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM). — (To attribute a fault) dozA- ropaRaM or dozakalpanaM or dozaprasaNgaM kf.
ATTRIBUTE , s. guRaH, viSezaH, viSezaRaM, saMjYAvizayaH.

ATTRIBUTE , s. upADiH m., DarmmaH. The eight divine attributes, or the attributes of Śiva as the deity, are: 1. Minuteness, aRimA m.; 2. Greatness, mahimA m.; 3. Heaviness, garimA m.; 4. Lightness, laGimA m.; 5. The power of reaching every thing, prAptiH f.; 6. Supremacy, ISitA; 7. Holding in sub- jection, vaSitA; 8. Irresistible will, prAkAmyaM.
ATTRIBUTIVE (subs.): viSezaRam.
ATTRIBUTIVE , a. vAcyaH -cyA -cyaM, viSezakaH -kA -kaM, viSezaRaH -RA -RaM.
Attrition, s. GarzaRaM, pezaRaM, kzayaH. 2 anutApaH, anuSayaH.
ATTRITION: GarzaRam: v. Friction.
ATTRITION , s. (The act of wearing things by rubbing one against another) GarzaRaM, sammarddaH -rddanaM, pezaRaM, kzayaH, kzIRatvaM. — (Grief for sin) BayamUlaH paScAttApaH, anutApaH, santApaH.
ATTRITION , s. saMharzaH, saNGarzaH.
Attune, v. t. tAlopeta a. kf 8 U. 2 ekatAlaM kf, tulyasvaraM-tOryatrikaM-kf.
ATTUNE: Ph. a. your voice to the lyre. *vIRAnu- gataM svaraM kuru.

To ATTUNE , v. a. (To make any thing musical) susvaraM -rAM -raM kf, tAlopetaM -tAM -taM kf. — (To tune one thing to another) gItavA- ditrAdi tulyasvaraM kf, gItavAditrAdInAm ekatAlaM kf, tOryyatrikaM kf, nAnADvanInAM tUryyAdInAm EkyaM kf.
Auburn, a. piSaMga (gI f.), gOra (rI f.), kapiSa, pAMquvarRa.
AUBURN: (1) piSaNgaH (NgA, NgaM): v. Tawny; (2) SyAvaH (vA, vaM): v. Brown;(3) gOraH (rI, raM): v. Yellow.
AUBURN , a. SyAvaH -vA -vaM, kapiSaH -SA -SaM, pARquvarRaH -rRA -rRaM.
Auction, s. GozaRapUrvako dravyavikrayaH. [Auction]eer, s. saGozaRaM vikretf m.
AUCTION: *AhvAnavikrayaH; sarvoccamUlyadAtre prakASa- vikrayaH, A. room *AhvAnavikrayagfhaM; AhvAnavikrayaSAlA.
AUCTION , s. vardDamAnamUlyena nAnAdravyavikrayaH, GozaRapUrvvakaM nAnAdravyavikrayaH. — (Auction-room) dravyavikrayagfhaM.

AUDACIOUSNESS , AUDACITY, s. pragalBatA, DArzwyaM, DfzwatA, sAhasaM, nirlajjatvaM, pratiBAnaM.

AUDIBLY: sPuwam (=distinctly: q. v.): v. Audible.
AUDIBLY , adv. SrAvyaprakAreRa, karRagocaraM.

(=spectators).

AUDIENCE , s. (The act of hearing) SravaRaM, AkarRanaM, niSamanaM. — (Liberty of speaking to or seeing a superior) rAjadarSanaM, darSanaM; ‘he is come begging an audience,’ darSanArTam Agato'sti. [Page032-b+ 51] — (An auditory, hearers) SrotAraH m. pl. (tf), saBA, saBAsadaH m. pl., sadaH n. (s), paripad f., prekzakAH m. pl. — (Audience-chamber) darSanaSAlA, darSanagfhaM.
AUDIENCE , s. (Assembly of hearers) SrotfmaRqalaM, SrotfsamUhaH, Srotf- janAH m. pl., SrotfgaRaH, SrotfsamAjaH.

AUDIT (subs.): I In gen.: parIkzA.II Of accounts: *gaRanAparIkzA, gaRanASoDanam.
AUDIT (v. t.): pari-Ikzate (Ikz, c. 1); (2) SoDa- yati (c. of SuD) (?), have you a. ed the account *api gaRanA pariSoDitA.
AUDIT , s. gaRitaSoDanaM, gaRitaSudDIkaraRaM, guRanI, vigaRanaM, anusanDAnaM, anuyogaH, parIkzaRaM.

To AUDIT , v. a. gaRitAni SuD in caus. (SoDayati -yituM), or SudDIkf or anusanDA (c. 3. -daDAti -Datte -DAtuM), or anuyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM) or parIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -IkzituM); guRanIM kf, vigaRanaM kf.
AUDITED , p. p. SudDIkftaH -tA -taM, SoDitaH -tA -taM, vigaRitaH -tA -taM
AUDITOR: I A hearer: q. v.: SrotA.II Of accounts: *gaRanASoDakaH; parIkzakaH or SoDakaH (when the meaning is clear).
AUDITOR , s. SrotA m. (tf). — (One employed to take an account) gaRitaSoDakaH, anusanDAyI m. (n), guRakaH.
AUDITORY (adj.): Ph. a. passages SravaRamArgAH (m. pl.).
AUDITORY , s. (A collection of hearers) SrotAraH m. pl., saBAsadaH m. pl., saBA, sadaH n. (s), paripad f. — (A lecture room) pAWaSa lA, SravaRaSAlA.
AUGER: (1) AsPowanI:(2) veDanikA.
AUGER , s. AsPowanI, veDanikA, AviDaH.
Aught, s. kimapi, kiMcana, kiMcit.
AUGHT , s. kiYcit, kimapi, kiYcana.
Augment, v. t. vfD c., eD c., ApyE c., pracurIkf 8 U, upaci 5 U. v. i. vfD-eD 1 A, upaci pass., pyE 1 A. s. vfdDi f. 2 AgamaH. [Augment]ation, s. vfdDi f., varDanaM. 2 upacayaH, fdDi f., samunnati f.
AUGMENT (v. i.): varDate (vfD c. 1): v. To in- -crease.
AUGMENT (v. t.): varDayati (c. of vfD): v. To increase.
AUGMENT (subs.): vfdDiH v. Augmentation.
To AUGMENT , v. a. vfD in caus. (varDayati -yituM), saMvfD, parivfD; eD in caus. (eDayati yituM), sameD; pracurIkf; ApyE in caus. (-pyAyayati -yituM), samApyE.

To AUGMENT , v. n. vfD (c. 1. varDate, varDituM), aBivfD, pravfD, vivfD; fD (c. 5. fnDoti, c. 4. fDyati, arDituM), samfD; upaci in pass. (-cIyate), pyE (c. 1. pyAyate, pyAtuM), vfMh in caus. (vfMhayati -yituM), upavfMh, samupavfMh.
AUGMENT , s. vfdDiH f. — (In grammar) AptoktiH f.
AUGMENT , s. AgamaH. AUTHORESS, s. granTakartrI, granTakAriRI.

AUGMENTATION: (1) vfdDiH;(2) varDanam: v. In- -crease, enlargement.
AUGMENTATION , s. (The act) vardDanaM. — (The state) vfdDiH f., vivfdDiH f., fdDiH f., upacayaH, unnatiH f., samunnatiH f.
AUGMENTATIVE: (1) varDizRu (mfn.);(2) varDa- mAnaH (nA, naM).
AUGMENTED , p. p. saMvardDitaH -tA -taM, vfdDaH -dDA -dDa, pravfdDaH -dDA -dDaM, upacitaH -tA -taM, pracurIkftaH -tA -taM, sameDitaH -tA -taM.

SuBASuBaM parIkz 1 A or AlAc 10. 2 anumA 3 A, SaMk 1 A; ‘this does not a(ugur) well forth success of your undertaking’ tava kAryasidDernEtacCuBalakzaRaM. [Augur]y, s. nimittajYAnaM, SakunajYAnaM. 2 SakunaM, ajanyaM, pUrvalakzaRaM, nimittaM.

AUGUR (subs.): (1) SakunajYaH or SakunajYAnavid (m.) (from birds), I heard from the a. that I would meet you just after 30 days SakunajYAttasmAttriMSa drivasAvasAnantarameva BavatsaNgaH samBavizyatItyaSfRavam, D.; (2) nimittajYaH. (from any omen) K.: v. Soothsayer.
AUGUR (v. t.): I To betoken, predict: q. v.: sUcayati (sUc, c. 10).II To infer, conjec- -ture: q. v.: SaNkate. A. ed (by birds): Sakuna- nirdizwaH (zwA, zwaM), D.
AUGUR , s. SakunaparIkzakaH, ajanyajYaH, pUrvvacihnanirIkzakaH, pUrvvalakzaRajYaH, pakzigatihastareKAdilakzaRAt SuBASuBadarSakaH, BUkampAdyutpAtapakzigatica- kzuHspantAdinimittaPalakaTakaH.

To AUGUR , v. n. BUkampAdyutpAtapakzigaticakzuHspandAdinimittaPalakaTanena SuBASuBaM or maNgalAmaNgalaM or adyaSvInaM pradfS in caus. (-darSayati -yituM); SavunAni or pUrvvaliNgAni parIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -IkzituM). — (To con- jecture) anumA (c. 2. -mAti -mAtuM), SaNk (c. 1. SaNkate, SaNkituM).
AUGURED , p. p. (Foreshewn) pradarSitaH -tA -taM. — (Inferred) anumitaH -tA -taM.

AUGURY , s. (The act of prognosticating) pakzigatihastaresvAcakzuHspa- ndAdilakzaRAt SuBASuBadarSanaM or BavizyadanumAnaM, SakunaparIkzaRaM, pUrvvala- kzaRajYAnaM. — (An omen) SakunaM, ajanyaM, pUrvvacihnaM, pUrvvalakzaRaM.

AUGUST (adj.): (1) mahAmahiman (mfn.);(2) pfTu- DAman (mfn.): v. Majestic, grand.
AUGUST (subs.): uttaraSrAvaRapUrvaBAdrasaMvAdIyurupIyavatsara- syAzwamo mAsaH.
AUGUST , a. ESvaraH -rI -raM, ESikaH -kI -kaM, pratApavAn -vatI -vat (t), mahAmahimA -mA -ma (n), atyutkfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, atimahAn -hatI -hat (t), rAjayogyaH -gyA -gyaM.
AUGUST , s. SrAvaRaH, naBAH m. (s), BAdraH, naBasyaH, prozwapadaH.
AUGUSTNESS , s. mahApratApaH, atimahattvaM, atyutkfzwatA, pratApaH.

AUNT , s. (By the mother's side) mAtulI, -lA, -lAnI. — (Fa- ther's sister) pitfsvasA f. (sf).
Auricle, s. karRaSazkulI. Auricular, a. kArRika (kI f.), SrAvaRa (RI f.). 2 karRe-upakarRaM kaTita, japita, gupta.

AURICLE , s. (The external ear) karRaSazkulI f., karRavahiBAgaH. — (Of the heart) hfdraktaDft karRAkAraH kozaH.
AURICULAR: SrOtaH (tI, taM) Ph. a. confession niBftasvIkAraH (?).

AURICULAR , a. (Relating to the ear) kArRaH -rRI -rRaM, kArRikaH -kI -kaM. SrAvaRaH -RI -RaM, SrOtaH -tI -taM. — (Told in the ear, secret) upakarRaM [Page033-a+ 51] or karRe japitaH -tA -taM or japyaH -pyA -pyaM, suguptaH -ptA -ptaM. — (Within the sense of hearing) karRagocaraH -rA -raM.
Auriferous, a. suvarRamiSrita.
Aurist, s. karRavEdya.
AUROCHS: polaRqadeSasya vanyagoviSezaH.
Aurora, s. uzas f., aruRaH.
AURORA: (1) aruRaH;(2) uzas (n.);(3) dina- muKam;(4) aharmuKam.
AURORA , s. (The dawn) aruRaH, divasamuKaM, aharmuKaM, uzaH, pUrvvasanDyA.
AURORA BOREALIS: vidyududBavo rAtridfSyo mahojjvalaH prakASaviSezaH.

Auspice, s. SakunaM, nimittaM, pUrvalakzaRaM; ‘a(uspice)s’ anugrahaH, ASrayaH, prasAdaH. Auspicious, a. Siva, SuBa, SivaM-SuBaM-kara, mAMgalika (kI f.), kalyARa (RI f.), maMgala, Badra; ‘a(uspicious) time’ lagnavelA, SuBalagnaM. 2 SrIyukta, sOBAgyavat. 3 prasanna, anugrAhin. [Auspicious]ly, adv. SuBakzaRe. sOBAgyena, kzemeRa. [Auspicious]ness, s. kalyARaM, maMgalaM, mAMgalyaM, sOBAgyaM, BadraM, kzemaH-maM, SuBaM.
AUSPICE: I An omen: q. v.: Sakunam.II Pro- -tection, patronage: q. v. ASrayaH.
AUSPICE , s. (An omen drawn from birds) SakunaM, nimittaM, pakzi- gatiprayuktaM pUrvvalakzaRaM, pUrvvacihnaM. — (Favour, protection) ASrayaH, anugrahaH.
AUSPICIOUS: I Lucky, propitious: q. v.: (1) SuBaH (BA, BaM);(2) kalyARaH (RA, RaM);(3) maNgalaH (lA, laM)II Fortunate, prosperous: q. v. fdDimat (f. tI).

AUSPICIOUS , a. SuBaH -BA -BaM, kalpARaH -RI -RaM, SaNkaraH -rI -raM, SivaNkaraH -rA -raM, BadraH -drA -draM, maNgalyaH -lyA -lyaM, mANgalikaH -kI -kaM, SarmmavAn -vatI -vat (t), SuBaNkaraH -rA -raM, kzemakaraH -rA -raM, tizyaH -zyA -zyaM. — (Prosperous) sOBAgyavAn -vatI -vat (t), SrIyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, kzemavAn -vatI -vat (t). — (Favourable) prasannaH -nnA -nnaM, anugrAhI -hiRI -hi -(n); ‘an auspicious moment,’ SuBalagnaH, lagnavelA.
AUSPICIOUSLY: SuBalagne (=at an a. moment): v. Propitiously, favourably.
AUSPICIOUSLY , adv. dizwyA, SuBalagne, SuBakzaRe, sOBAgyena, kOSalyena, kzemeRa.
AUSPICIOUSNESS , s. kalyARaM, maNgalaM, mANgalyaM, kOSalyaM, kzemaH.
Austere, a. tIvra, ugra, (tapaH), nizWura, karkaSa, kaWora, nirdaya, kaWina; (in taste) Sukta, rUkza, kawu. [Auster]ity, s. ugratA, kaWoratA &c. ‘religious a(usterily)’ tapas n., kfcCraM.
AUSTERE: I Severe, stern, harsh: q. v.; kaWoraH (rA, raM).II Harsh, rough (to the taste): q. v.: SuktaH (ktA, ktaM) (?).
AUSTERE: (1) kaWoraB;(2) ugram;(3) nizWuram: v. Severely.
AUSTERE , a. nizwuraH -rA -raM, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, kaWinaH -nA -naM, ugraH -grA -graM, kawumatiH -tiH -ti, kaWoraH -rA -raM, nirdayaH -yA -yaM. — (In taste) SuktaH -ktA -ktaM.
AUSTERELY , adv. nizWuraM, kAWinyena, kaWoraM, nEzWuryyeRa, ugraM.

AUSTERENESS , AUSTERITY, s. (Severity) kArkaSyaM, kAWinyaM, kaWinatA, ugratA, nizWuratA, nEzWuryyaM, kaWoratA, kawutA. — (Penance) tapaH n. (s), kfcCaM; ‘patient of austerities,’ tapaHkleSasahaH; ‘to practise austerities,’ tap in pass. (tapyate), santap; tapasy (nom. tapasyati).
AUSTERITY: (1) kArkaSyam;(2) kaWoratA: v. Severity, sternness.
AUSTRAL , a. (Southern) dakziRaH -RA -RaM, apAcInaH -nA -naM,

Authentic, [Authentic]al, a. akftrima, taTya, pramARayukta; akalpita, satya. [Authentic]ate, v. t. sapramARa a. kf 8 U, pramARIkf. [Authentic]ity, s. sapramARatA, satyatA, prAmARyaM. [Authentic]ally, adv. sapramARaM, pramARAnusAreRa.

AUTHENTIC: I Genuine, true:(1) taTyaH (TyA, TyaM);(2) satyaH (tyA, tyaM);(3) akftrimaH (mA, maM) (=not forged, as an a. register).II Of approved authority, reliable: q. v. prAmA- RikaH (kI, kaM), an a. writer prAmARikaleKakaH.

AUTHENTICAL , AUTHENTIC, a. sidDapramARaH -RA -RaM, aKaRqapramARaH -RA -RaM, prAmARikaH -kI -kaM, pramARayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, AptaH -ptA -ptaM. — (Real, genuine) vAstavaH -vI -vaM, vAstavikaH kI -kaM, nirvyalIkaH -kA -kaM, nirvyAjaH -jA -jaM, akftrimaH -mA -maM, akalpitaH -tA -taM, mUlikaH -kI -kaM, sAraH -rA -raM, taTyaH -TyA -TyaM, satyaH -tyA -tyaM.
AUTHENTICALLY: (1) pramARataH;(2) tattvataH;(3) sArataH.
AUTHENTICALLY , adv. pramARatas ind., pramARAnurUpeRa, vastutas, tattvatas, nirvyalIkaM, sAratas.
AUTHENTICATE: I To render authentic: prAmARyaM karoti (kf, c. 8)II To prove authen- -tic: pramARayati (nomi.).
To AUTHENTICATE , v. a. pramARIkf, pramARa (nom. pramARayati -yituM), satyAkf.
AUTHENTICATION: Ph. for a. prAmARyaM kartum: v. Confirmation.
AUTHENTICITY: (1) prAmARyaM;(2) satyatA;(3) akftrimatA (=the quality of not being for- -ged).
AUTHENTICITY , s. prAmARyaM, pramARatvaM, vAstavatA, nirvyalIkatA, akftri- matA, mOlatA, sAratA, satyatA.

Author, s. kAraH-kft in comp.; ‘a(uthor) of Gadādhari’ gadADarIkAraH-kft; graMTakAraH. 2 kft m., praRetf m., leKakaH. 2 pravartakaH, AraMBakaH, utpAdakaH, janakaH, saMpAdayitf m. [Author]ship, kartftvaM, pravartakatA.

AUTHOR: I The writer of a book:(1) kAraH or kft (in comp.), a. of the commentary BAzya- kAraH; the a. of the Mitākṣarā mitAkzarAkft, Da. com.;(2) granTakAraH or -kartA or -kft (=a. of a book and hence to be used when a. is used abs.);(3) leKakaH;(4) racakaH or racayitA;(5) praRetA;(6) nibanDf (m.) (rare);(7) kftin (m.) (very rare). N. B. 3, 4, 5, and 6. are gen. used with some defining word.II A [Page050] maker, contriver, originator: q. v.: kartA, a. of great wonders kartA mahAScaryARAm, K.

AUTHOR , s. (The first beginner of any thing) prayojakaH, pravarttakaH, AramBakaH, AdikarttA m. (rttf). — (The effector) sADakaH, utpAdakaH, sampAdakaH, janakaH, karttA m. (rttf), kArakaH, nirvvAhakaH. — (A writer) nibanDA m. (nDf), granTakAraH, granTakarttA m. (rttf), racakaH.
AUTHORESS: (1) kft (in comp.);(2) granTakartrI; praRetrI;(4) racayitrI.

(-sTApayati -yituM), sapra- mARaM -RAM -RaM kf, pramARavantaM -vatIM -vat kf. — (To give authority to any one) niyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yuMkte -yoktuM, c. 10. -yojayati -yituM), aDikAritvaM dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM). — (To permit) anujYA (c. 9. -jAnAti -nIte -jYAtuM), anuman (c. 4. -manyate -mantuM).
AUTHORISED , p. p. pramARIkftaH -tA -taM, sapramARaH -RA -RaM, niyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, aDikftaH -tA -taM, niyogI -ginI -gi (n), viDIyamAnaH -nA -naM. — (Permitted) anujYAtaH -tA -taM, anumataH -tA -taM.
AUTHORITATIVE: I Determinative:(1) sapra- mARaH (RA, RaM) (=with proof).(2) dfQaH (QA, QaM) (=firm).II Dictatorial, overbearing: q. v.
AUTHORITATIVE , a. prAmARikaH -kI -kaM, pramARaDArI -riRI -ri (n), vEDikaH -kI -kaM, AcArikaH -kI -kaM, SAsanAnurUpaH -pA -paM.
AUTHORITATIVE , a. AptaH -ptA -ptaM, sapramARaH -RA -RaM, pramARayuktaH &c.
AUTHORITATIVELY: (1) sapramARam;(2) dfQam (=firmly).
AUTHORITATIVELY , adv. pramARatas ind., pramARAnusAreRa, viDivat, AcArAnurUpaM, SAsanAt.

Authority, s. praButvaM, praBAvaH, Sakti f. 2 aDikAraH, praButvaM. 3 ESvaryaM, ADipatyaM, AjYA, SAsanaM, niyogaH. 4 pramARaM, AptavacanaM, nidarSanaM; ‘Panini is an a(uthority) in this respect’ atra vizaye pARiniH pramARaM. 5 prAmARyaM, viSvasanIyatA. 6 gurutvaM, gOrava. 7 aDikArin m., niyogin m., aDikftaH puruzaH, praBuH. Award, v. t. dA 3 P. 2 dA c. (dApayati). s. nirRayaH; vicAraH, AjYA.
AWARD (v. t.): (1) dadAti (dA, c. 3);(2) vi- tarati (tF, c. 1);(3) dApayati (c. of dA) (in the legal sense, when a judge a. s damages etc.)
AWARD (subs.): nirRayaH: v. Judgment, sen- -tence.
To AWARD , v. a. dA in caus. (dApayati -yituM), tIr (c. 10. tIrayati -yituM).
AWARD , s. (Judgment, sentence) vicAraH, nirRayaH, nizpattiH f., tIraRaM, samADAnaM, daRqaH, AjYA.
AWARDED , p. p. dApitaH -tA -taM, tIritaH -tA -taM.
AWARDER , s. vicArakaH, nirRetA m. (tf), dApakaH.
Aware, a. vijYApita, sAvaDAna. 2 vedin-jYa in comp.; or by jYA 9 U; See Know.
AWARE, BE: (1) jAnAti (YjA, c. 9);(2) ava- gacCati (gam, c. 1): v. To know.
AWARE, MADE: (1) boDitaH (tA, taM);(2) vibo- DitaH (tA, taM);(3) avaboDitaH (tA, taM).

AWARE , a. (Excited to consciousness) vijYApitaH -tA -taM, boDitaH -tA -taM. — (Knowing) vedI -dinI -di (n), jYaH -jYA -jYaM in comp. — (Vigilant, attentive) sAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, jAgaraH -rA -raM, -rI -riRI -ri (n); ‘he is aware,’ vetti, jAnAti.
Away, a. parokza, avidyamAna, anupasTita; dUrasTa. adv. alaM, kftaM (instr.). 2 apehi, apasara.

AWAY: v. the several verbs with which it is used. Ph.: a. with begging kftameva yAcYayA, Ki. xiv. 20; a. with shame alaM hriyA, R. v. 58; a. (=begone; q. v.) antaramantaram, Mr. ii.; she is a. (=absent, q. v.).

AWAY , a. and adv., expressed by the preposition apa. — (Ab- sent) parokzaH -kzA -kzaM, sTAnAntaraNgataH -tA -taM, anupasTitaH -tA -taM, avi- dyamAnaH -nA -naM. — (Far away) dUrasTaH -sTA -sTaM, dUrasTAyI -yinI -yi (n). — (Come along) yAtu. — (Begone!) apEhi, apasara, hUm; ‘away with this fear,’ alam anayA SaNkayA.

details.body: Awe, s. sADvasaM, BayaM, trAsaH, AdaraH, saMBramaH, AdaraprayuktaM BayaM; ‘I approach the king with a(we)’ cakitaM nfpasya pArSvamupEmi (M. 1); ‘Stand in a(we) of’ BI 3 P, tras 1, 4 P. v. t. BI c., tras c. saMBrameRa AkulIkf 8 U; ‘a(w)ed, struck with awe’ saMBrAMta, vismayAkula; BayAkula, Bayavipluta, sasADvasa. Awful, a. Gora, dAruRa, BIzaRa, BErava (vI f.) (of things). 2 atitejasvin, mahAtejas, AdaraRIya, pUjya; ‘how a(wful) is royal greatness’ aho durAsado rAjamahimA (M. 1). 3 praSAMtagaMBIra (araRyaSrIH). [Awful]ly, adv. saBayaM, atyaMtaM. [Awful]ness, s. tejas n.; dAruRatA, GoratA.

AWE (subs.): (1) Bayam;(2) trAsaH;(3) sADvasam; (4) AdaraH. N. B. There is no exact equiv. of awe: 1, 2 and 3 mean fear, 4 means respect. To stand in a. of: biBeti (BI, c. 3) (with abl.). Ph.: he is known to me and not disagreeable, still I approach him with a na ca na paricito na cApyaramyaScakitamupEmi taTApi pArSvamasya, Mal. i.
AWE , s. AdaraH, samBramaH, vismayaH, trAsaH, AtaNkaH, AdaraprayuktaM BayaM. — (To stand in awe of) BI (c. 3. biBeti, BetuM), tras (c. 4. trasyati, trasituM) with abl., Adf (c. 6. -driyate) with acc.
To AWE , v. a. (To strike terror into) BI in caus. (BAyayati or BIzayati -yituM), tras in caus. (trAsayati -yituM), vyAkulIkf, AkulIkf, samBrameRa upahan (c. 2. -hanti -hantuM).
AWE STRUCK: (1) BayaviplutaH (tA, taM);(2) sADvasa- parItaH (tA, taM);(3) trAsAkulaH (lA, laM).
AWE-STRUCK , a. samBrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, vismayAkulaH -lA -laM, BayaviplutaH -tA -taM.

AWFUL: I Awe-inspiring:(1) GoraH (rA, raM) [Page052] (=terrific: q. v.: not applicable to men); (2) atitejasvin (f. nI) or mahAtejas (mfn.) (full of that which inspires awe: appli- -cable to men only and their appearance). Ph.: Oh how a. is royal majesty aho ! durAsado rAjamahimA, Mal. i.; wild mountain scenery, grand and a. praSAntagammIranIlavipulaSrIraraRyagiriBUmiH, Vi. v.II Awestruck: q. v.
AWFUL , a. GoraH -rA -raM, dAruRaH -RA -RaM, BEravaH -vA -vaM, BIzaRaH -RA -RaM, BayaNkaraH -rA -raM, BayAnakaH -kA -kaM. — (Worshipful) AdaraRIyaH -yA -yaM, AdftyaH -tyA -tyaM, pUjyaH -jyA -jyaM.
AWFULLY: I Fearfully q. v.II Exceedingly: q. v. atyantam.
AWFULLY , adv. dAruRaM, GoraM, yaTA samBrama utpadyate taTA.
AWFULNESS: (1) tejaH (of men etc.);(2) praSAnta- gamBIratA (=calm solemnity).
AWFULNESS , s. GoratA, dAruRatA, BIzaRaM, BEravaM, BIzmaM.
Awhile, adv. kiMcitkAlaM, muhUrtaM, kzaRa yAvat.
AWHILE: kiyatkAlam; (2) kaYcitkAlam;(3) muhU- rtam (=for a moment).
AWHILE , adv. kiyatkAlaM, kiYcitkAlaM, alpakAlaM, iyatkAlaM, muhUrttaM, kzaRaM, yatkiYcitsamayaM.
Awkward, a. akuSala, adakza, akzipra, apawu. 2 (Manners) grAmya; virUpa, sTUla. [Awkward]ness, s. adakzatA; grAmyatA &c.
AWKWARD: I Unskilful: q. v.: adakzaH (kzA, kzaM).II Inelegant, clumsy: q. v.:(1) apa- rUpaH (pA, paM);(2) grAmyaH (myA, myaM) (=rustic), (applicable to manners etc.).

AWKWARD , a. (Clumsy, unskilful) adakzaH -kzA -kzaM, anAptaH -ptA -ptaM, apawuH -wuH -wu, akzipraH -prA -praM, avijYaH -jYA -jYaM, akftI -tinI -ti (n). — (Inelegant) virUpaH -pI -paM, sTUlaH -lA -laM.
AWKWARDLY , adv. apawu, adakzaM, akzipraM, anAptaM.
AWKWARDNESS: I Unskilfulness: q. v.II Inelegance: q. v.: grAmyatA.
AWKWARDNESS , s. (Unskilfulness) apAwavaM, apawutA, adakzatvaM, akzi- pratvaM. — (Inelegance) sTUlatA, vErUpyaM.
Awl, s. ArA, carmapraBedikA.
AWL: (1) ArA;(2) carmapraBedikA (shoemaker's a.);(3) veDanikA. v. Gimlet.
AWL , s. ArA, carmmapraBedikA, AviDaH, veDanikA.
Awn, s. SUkaM, kiMSAruH.
AWN: (1) kiMSAruH;(2) SasyaSUkam;(3) SuNgaH; (4) SUkam.
AWN , s. (A beard of corn) SUkaH -kaM, SasyaSUkaM, kiMSAruH m.
Awning, s. vitAnaM AcCAdanaM.
AWNING: (1) vitAnam;(2) ullocaH: v. Veil.
AWNING , s. vitAnaM, vitAnakaM, AcCAdanaM, ullocaH.
Awry, adv. tiryak, sAci, jihmaM. 2 viparItaM, pratilomaM, pratikUlaM.
AWRY: (1) tiryak;(2) tiraScInam;(9) sAci; (4) kuwilam.
AWRY , adv. tiras, sAci, tiryyak, kuwilaM, jihmaM, anfju. — (Per- versely) viparItaM, pratikUlaM, vilomaM.
Axe, s. waMkaH, paraSuH, kuWAraH, paraSvaDaH.
AXE: (1) kuWAraH;(2) paraSuH;(3) paraSvaDaH. A small a. kuWArikA.
AXE , s. waNkaH, kuWAraH, paraSuH m., paraSvaDaH, CidiH f., vfkzaBid f., vfkzaBedI m. (n), svaDitiH m.
Axiom, s. tattvaM, sidDAMtaH. 2 vacanaM, sUtraM. [Axiom]atic, a. svayaMsidDa.
AXIOM: *aprameyatatvam, svataHsidDavastu, K. d.
AXIOM , s. tattvaM, sUtraM, sidDAntaH, AdeSaH, vacanaM.
AXIOMATIC , a. sOtraH -trI -traM, sidDAntI -ntinI -nti (n).
Axis, s. akzareKA, akzaH, DruvaH.
AXIS: *akzareKA.
AXIS , s. akzaH, DruvaH, meruH m.
Axle, s. akzAgraM.
AXLE, AXLE-TREE: (1) cakradaRqaH (?);(2) akzAgram (?);(3) anukarzaH (?).
AXLE , AXLE-TREE, s. akzAgraM, akzadantaH.
Ay, adv. taTeti, evaM, Am, nUnaM
AY , adv. taTeti, evaM, hUm, Am.
Ayah, s. upamAtf f., DAtrI, AsannaparicArikA.
Aye, adv. sadA, sarvadA, ajasraM.
AYE , adv. sarvvadA, sadA, nityaM, nityadA, SASvataM, ajasraM, SASvatIH samAH.
Azure, a. nIla, nIla-AkASa-varRa.
AZURE: nIlaH (lA, laM).
AZURE , a. nIlaH -lA -laM, nIlavarRaH, -rRA -rRaM, AkASavarRaH -rRA -rRaM.
